children.title: Node-Activated Gossip
children.top_down_role: Communication initiated through randomized node selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Activated Gossip
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical node-clock gossip with one neighbor selected conditionally on the active node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let node \(i\) hold \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\). Define the stacked state \(x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample an active node \(i_k\) with probability \(q_i>0\), then sample \(j_k\in N(i_k)\) with conditional probability \(r_{j\mid i}>0\). Nodes \(i_k\) and \(j_k\) replace their states by their arithmetic mean, and all other states remain unchanged. Thus \[x^{k+1}=\left(\left[I_n-\tfrac12(e_{i_k}-e_{j_k})(e_{i_k}-e_{j_k})^\top\right]\otimes I_d\right)x^k,\] where \(e_i\) is the \(i\)-th standard basis vector of \(\mathbb R^n\). The current stacked state is the output, with optional termination at a chosen disagreement tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activated node chooses a neighbor, and the selected pair averages its states while every other node retains its state.
assumptions_latex: Every node has at least one neighbor.
\(q_i r_{j\mid i}>0\) on every directed neighbor choice required for information propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update preserves \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k\) and changes only the selected pair.

notation.meaning: probability of choosing neighbor \(j\) given active node \(i\)
the ith standard basis vector of \(\mathbb R^n\)

children.title: Activation-Dependence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Temporal dependence patterns in randomized communication events.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Dependence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence classes for a sequence of random communication activations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) denote the activated node, edge, or subgraph at time \(k\), and let \(\mathcal F_k=\sigma(A_0,\ldots,A_k)\). The activation process is independent when the variables \((A_k)_{k\ge0}\) are mutually independent; conditionally independent with fixed law when \(\mathbb P(A_k\in S\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})=\mu_k(S)\) almost surely for deterministic probability measures \(\mu_k\); Markov when \(\mathbb P(A_k\in S\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})=K_k(A_{k-1},S)\); and history-dependent otherwise. Any convergence claim for randomized communication must state which regime is assumed and impose connectivity or mixing conditions appropriate to that regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activation laws may be independent, conditionally fixed-law, Markov, or generally history-dependent; convergence assumptions must match the chosen dependence class.
assumptions_latex: \((A_k)_{k\ge0}\) is defined on a common probability space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional law \(\mathbb P(A_k\in\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\) determines the activation-dependence regime.
review_flags: Terminology and admissible dependence classes vary across distributed-optimization analyses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the selected terminology. In particular, the stated deterministic conditional-law condition already entails independence from the activation history and is not clearly distinct from the preceding mutual-independence regime.

children.title: Unreliable Communication Network Family
children.top_down_role: Communication affected by packet loss, dropouts, or link failures.

children.title: Intermittent-Link Regimes
children.top_down_role: Links that become available only during selected periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Intermittent-Link Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-varying subgraph model in which fixed physical links may be temporarily unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a fixed physical graph. An intermittent-link regime is a sequence \((G_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) and \(E_k\subseteq E\), where an edge may alternate between available and unavailable states. Writing \(a_e(k)=\mathbf 1\{e\in E_k\}\), deterministic intermittency specifies the binary sequences \(a_e(k)\), whereas stochastic intermittency specifies their joint law relative to a filtration. A bounded-intermittency condition with window \(B\ge1\) requires \[\left(V,\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}E_t\right)\text{ to be connected for every }k.\] This condition permits disconnected instantaneous graphs while enforcing recurrent network-wide information paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Physical links may switch on and off; bounded intermittency requires every fixed-length union graph to remain connected.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the fixed physical graph containing every possible active edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Instantaneous disconnection is allowed, while \(B\)-window connectivity guarantees recurrent aggregate connectivity.

notation.meaning: set of available links at time \(k\)

review_flags: A dedicated time-varying-network source is required for the selected bounded-window convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The time-varying graph model is standard, but a source is required for calling uniform B-window connectivity a bounded-intermittency condition in this exact container.

children.title: Packet-Loss Networks
children.top_down_role: Communication affected by dropped or missing messages.

knowledge_statements.title: Packet-Loss Networks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed message-delivery model allowing asymmetric loss on nominal communication links.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a nominal directed communication graph. For each \((i,j)\in E\) and time \(k\), let \(\delta_{ij}(k)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether the packet sent by \(i\) is received by \(j\). The realized graph is \(G_k=(V,E_k)\), where \(E_k=\{(i,j)\in E:\delta_{ij}(k)=1\}\). A packet-loss network is the nominal graph together with the joint law, or deterministic specification, of \((\delta_{ij}(k))\). Losses may be asymmetric, correlated across links, and temporally dependent; any algorithm using missing messages must additionally specify whether a receiver skips, renormalizes, substitutes, or stores delayed information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each directed transmission has a delivery indicator; its realized edges and missing-message rule define the packet-loss network seen by the algorithm.
assumptions_latex: Packets are indexed by a discrete communication time \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_k=\{(i,j)\in E:\delta_{ij}(k)=1\}\) is the realized communication edge set.

notation.meaning: delivery indicator for the packet from \(i\) to \(j\) at time \(k\)

review_flags: Packet-loss conventions differ on acknowledgments, delays, and missing-message handling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The delivery-indicator model is plausible, but no source supports the precise packet-loss and missing-message conventions.

children.title: Node-Dropout Networks
children.top_down_role: Networks with temporarily or permanently unavailable agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Dropout Networks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-varying participation model in which inactive nodes neither send nor receive updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a fixed graph and let \(s_i(k)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether node \(i\) participates at time \(k\). The active set is \(V_k=\{i\in V:s_i(k)=1\}\), and the realized communication graph is the induced graph \(G_k=G[V_k]\), unless a protocol explicitly retains edges to inactive nodes. In the strict-dropout convention, an inactive node sends no message, receives no message, and preserves its local state: \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\) whenever \(s_i(k)=0\). The dropout process is specified by the deterministic sequence or joint probability law of \((s_i(k))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A participation indicator selects active nodes; strict dropouts communicate with nobody and retain their previous states.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) contains every communication link available when both endpoints participate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict-dropout realized graph is \(G_k=G[V_k]\), and inactive states satisfy \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\).

notation.meaning: participation indicator of node \(i\) at time \(k\)

review_flags: The strict-dropout convention must be matched to a dedicated source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-dropout model is internally coherent, but a dedicated source is needed to support the induced-subgraph and state-preservation convention.

children.title: Persistent-Connectivity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure patterns separating recoverable communication from network fragmentation.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Connectivity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic obstruction caused by permanent separation of a time-varying network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph sequence \(G_k=(V,E_k)\), define the persistent union \(G_\infty=(V,E_\infty)\) by \(E_\infty=\{e:e\in E_k\text{ for infinitely many }k\}\). If \(G_\infty\) is disconnected, choose a nonempty proper component \(S\subset V\). After some finite time no edge crossing \((S,V\setminus S)\) is activated. Consequently, any distributed protocol whose node updates depend only on local states and received messages cannot, for every initial condition, compute a consensus value that depends nontrivially on data from both sides of the cut. Thus connectivity of \(G_\infty\) is necessary for universal exact consensus, although it is not sufficient without quantitative recurrence and weight assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If no cross-cut link recurs infinitely often, the two sides eventually cannot exchange information, preventing universal exact consensus.
assumptions_latex: Updates use only locally stored information and messages delivered along active edges.
The required consensus value depends nontrivially on every node's initial datum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Universal exact consensus implies that \(G_\infty\) is connected.

notation.meaning: graph of edges activated infinitely often
one component of a disconnected persistent union

review_flags: A source is required for the precise protocol class and necessity formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the necessity claim lacks a source defining the applicable protocol class, and the statement includes proof-style intermediate reasoning.

children.title: Graph-Algebra Representations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent representations of agreement and network conditioning.

children.title: Graph-Laplacian Consensus Representation
children.top_down_role: Agreement geometry expressed in node space.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Laplacian Consensus Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus subspace characterized as the nullspace of a connected graph Laplacian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(w_{ij}=w_{ji}\ge0\) and \(w_{ii}=0\), and suppose the undirected positive-weight support graph with edges \(\{i,j\}\) such that \(w_{ij}>0\) is connected. Define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij})\) and \(L=D-W\). For stacked node variables \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\), \[(L\otimes I_d)x=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_1=\cdots=x_n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=\mathbf 1_n\otimes z\text{ for some }z\in\mathbb R^d.\] Moreover, \[x^\top(L\otimes I_d)x=\tfrac12\sum_{i,j=1}^n w_{ij}\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert^2,\] so the Laplacian energy measures weighted disagreement and vanishes exactly on the consensus subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the positive-weight support graph is connected, stacked node states agree exactly when the graph Laplacian annihilates them; the Laplacian quadratic form is their weighted disagreement energy.
assumptions_latex: The graph formed by the pairs satisfying \(w_{ij}>0\) is connected.

notation.meaning: symmetric matrix of nonnegative edge weights

children.title: Node-Edge Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Agreement relations expressed through node-edge structure.

children.title: Node–Edge Incidence Representation
children.top_down_role: Graph structure expressed through node-to-edge orientation.

knowledge_statements.title: Node–Edge Incidence Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oriented incidence operators map node potentials to edge differences and edge flows to node imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orient each edge of an undirected weighted graph \(G=(V,E,w)\) arbitrarily, and define \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) so the column for \(e=(i,j)\) is \(e_i-e_j\). For node states \(x\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\), the vector \((B^\top\otimes I_d)x\) contains the oriented edge differences \(x_i-x_j\). For edge vectors \(y\in(\mathbb R^d)^m\), \((B\otimes I_d)y\) is their node divergence. With \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(w_e)\), the weighted Laplacian factorization is \[L=BQB^\top,\qquad L\otimes I_d=(B\otimes I_d)(Q\otimes I_d)(B^\top\otimes I_d).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The incidence transpose forms edge differences, the incidence matrix forms node divergence, and their weighted product is the graph Laplacian.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and undirected.
Each edge is assigned one arbitrary orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=BQB^\top\), and consensus constraints are \((B^\top\otimes I_d)x=0\) when \(G\) is connected.

children.title: Edge-Space Decision Variables
children.top_down_role: Distributed quantities represented directly on network edges.

knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Space Decision Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edge variables parameterize local constraint multipliers or flows, with node effects produced by incidence divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) be an oriented incidence matrix and let \(y=(y_e)_{e\in E}\in(\mathbb R^d)^m\) assign a decision vector to each edge. Its induced node-space vector is \[u=(B\otimes I_d)y,\qquad u_i=\sum_{e\text{ leaves }i}y_e-\sum_{e\text{ enters }i}y_e.\] Hence \((\mathbf 1_n^\top\otimes I_d)u=0\). In a Lagrangian for the consensus constraint \((B^\top\otimes I_d)x=0\), the edge multiplier \(y\) couples through \(\langle y,(B^\top\otimes I_d)x\rangle=\langle(B\otimes I_d)y,x\rangle\). Edge variables differing by an element of \(\ker(B\otimes I_d)\) induce the same node vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An edge decision vector induces zero-sum node imbalances through incidence divergence and serves naturally as a multiplier for edgewise consensus constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an oriented incidence matrix of a finite graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\mapsto(B\otimes I_d)y\) maps edge variables into the zero-sum node subspace and is nonunique along \(\ker(B\otimes I_d)\).

notation.meaning: node-space divergence induced by edge variables

children.title: Cycle-Space Structure
children.top_down_role: Edge-space organization associated with network cycles.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Space Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circulations form the incidence nullspace and encode the nonuniqueness of edge-space variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite graph with oriented incidence matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), the cycle space is \[\mathcal C(G)=\ker B=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:By=0\}.\] Its elements are divergence-free edge flows; reversing an edge orientation only changes the corresponding coordinate sign and not the underlying space. If the graph has \(c\) connected components, then \(\operatorname{rank}B=n-c\) and \(\dim\mathcal C(G)=m-n+c\). Under the Euclidean inner product, \[\mathcal C(G)=\left(\operatorname{im}B^\top\right)^\perp.\] For vector-valued edge variables, the cycle space becomes \(\ker(B\otimes I_d)=\mathcal C(G)\otimes\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycle flows have zero node divergence, have dimension edges minus vertices plus components, and are orthogonal to all incidence gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite graph with \(n\) vertices, \(m\) edges, and \(c\) connected components.

children.title: Cut-Space Structure
children.top_down_role: Edge-space organization associated with network cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Space Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence gradients form the cut space, orthogonally complementing cycle circulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite graph with oriented incidence matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), the cut space is \[\mathcal K(G)=\operatorname{im}B^\top=\{B^\top z:z\in\mathbb R^n\}.\] It consists of edge differences generated by node potentials and is spanned by signed incidence vectors of vertex cuts. If the graph has \(c\) connected components, then \(\dim\mathcal K(G)=n-c\). The fundamental edge-space decomposition is orthogonal: \[\mathbb R^m=\operatorname{im}B^\top\oplus\ker B=\mathcal K(G)\oplus\mathcal C(G).\] For vector-valued variables, \(\operatorname{im}(B^\top\otimes I_d)=\mathcal K(G)\otimes\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-space vectors are edge differences of node potentials and form the orthogonal complement of divergence-free cycle flows.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite graph with \(n\) vertices and \(c\) connected components.

children.title: Mixing-Operator Representation
children.top_down_role: Communication represented by averaging or transport operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Operator Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stacked-state representation of one synchronous linear communication round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For agent states \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\), stack \(x=(x_1^\top,\ldots,x_n^\top)^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}\). Given a mixing matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), one communication round is represented by \[x^+=(W\otimes I_d)x,\qquad x_i^+=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j.\] Thus the block operator \(W\otimes I_d\) applies the same network transport to every coordinate. If \(W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n\), it fixes every consensus state \(\mathbf{1}_n\otimes u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A communication round multiplies the stacked agent state by the Kronecker-lifted mixing matrix, equivalently replacing each local state by a weighted combination of received states.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)

notation.meaning: identity on the local state space

children.title: Network Subspace Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Separation of aggregate motion from network error.

children.title: Consensus Subspace
children.top_down_role: Network states representing agreement across agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Subspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agreement subspace for stacked Euclidean agent states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) agents with local states in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), the consensus subspace is \[\mathcal{C}:=\{\mathbf{1}_n\otimes u:u\in\mathbb{R}^d\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{nd}.\] A stacked state \(x=(x_1^\top,\ldots,x_n^\top)^\top\) belongs to \(\mathcal{C}\) if and only if \(x_1=\cdots=x_n\). Its orthogonal projector is \(P_{\mathcal C}=J\otimes I_d\), where \(J:=\mathbf{1}_n\mathbf{1}_n^\top/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The consensus subspace consists exactly of stacked states in which every agent holds the same local vector.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(\mathbb{R}^{nd}\) has its standard inner product

children.title: Disagreement Subspace
children.top_down_role: Network states representing deviations from agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Disagreement Subspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal complement of consensus for stacked Euclidean states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C=\{\mathbf{1}_n\otimes u:u\in\mathbb{R}^d\}\). The disagreement subspace is \[\mathcal C^\perp:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}:(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)z=0\}.\] Equivalently, writing \(z=(z_1^\top,\ldots,z_n^\top)^\top\), one has \(z\in\mathcal C^\perp\) exactly when \(\sum_{i=1}^n z_i=0\). Its orthogonal projector is \(P_{\mathcal C^\perp}=(I_n-J)\otimes I_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The disagreement subspace contains precisely the zero-sum stacked perturbations and is the orthogonal complement of consensus.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(\mathbb{R}^{nd}\) has its standard inner product

children.title: Aggregate-Motion Component
children.top_down_role: Collective optimization motion shared across the network.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Motion Component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal decomposition of stacked motion into network average and disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(J:=\mathbf{1}_n\mathbf{1}_n^\top/n\), and define \(\mathcal C:=\{\mathbf{1}_n\otimes u:u\in\mathbb{R}^d\}\) and \(\mathcal C^\perp:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}:(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)z=0\}\). For any \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}\), define \(\bar x:=(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)x/n\). Then \[x=(\mathbf{1}_n\otimes\bar x)+x_\perp,\qquad x_\perp:=((I_n-J)\otimes I_d)x.\] The first term lies in \(\mathcal C\), the second lies in \(\mathcal C^\perp\), and this decomposition is unique and orthogonal. Equivalently, the aggregate-motion component is \((J\otimes I_d)x=\mathbf{1}_n\otimes\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every stacked state uniquely and orthogonally splits into a replicated network average and a zero-sum disagreement component.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(x\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}\)
\(J=\mathbf{1}_n\mathbf{1}_n^\top/n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=(J\otimes I_d)x+((I_n-J)\otimes I_d)x\) is the unique orthogonal consensus-disagreement decomposition.

children.title: Network-Error Modes
children.top_down_role: Disagreement components shaped by graph propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Error Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral representation of disagreement dynamics for symmetric mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(W=W^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n\), and define \(\mathcal C^\perp:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}:(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)z=0\}\). Choose an orthonormal eigenbasis \(q_1=\mathbf{1}_n/\sqrt n,q_2,\ldots,q_n\) of \(W\), with corresponding eigenvalues \(1=\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_n\). Every \(e\in\mathcal C^\perp\) has a unique expansion \[e=\sum_{k=2}^n q_k\otimes a_k,\qquad a_k\in\mathbb{R}^d.\] Under one mixing step, \[e^+=(W\otimes I_d)e=\sum_{k=2}^n\lambda_k(q_k\otimes a_k).\] Hence each network-error mode is scaled independently by its associated nonconsensus eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For symmetric average-preserving mixing, every disagreement vector decomposes uniquely into orthogonal network eigenmodes, each multiplied by its associated nonconsensus eigenvalue per communication round.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(W=W^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)
\(W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n\)
\(e\in\mathcal C^\perp\)

children.title: Mixing-Matrix Conditions

children.title: Doubly Stochastic Mixing Conditions
children.top_down_role: Average-preserving mixing on balanced networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Doubly Stochastic Mixing Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative mixing that preserves both consensus and the arithmetic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is doubly stochastic when \[w_{ij}\ge 0,\qquad W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n,\qquad \mathbf{1}_n^\top W=\mathbf{1}_n^\top.\] Consequently, \(W\otimes I_d\) fixes every consensus state and preserves the arithmetic average: for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{nd}\), \[(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)(W\otimes I_d)x=(\mathbf{1}_n^\top\otimes I_d)x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative matrix is doubly stochastic when every row and column sums to one; its mixing preserves consensus and the arithmetic average.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)

children.title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Conditions
children.top_down_role: Agent-wise convex mixing on directed networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receiver-normalized nonnegative mixing for agent-wise convex combinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is row-stochastic when \[w_{ij}\ge 0\quad\text{for all }i,j,\qquad W\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n.\] Equivalently, \(\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}=1\) for each receiving agent \(i\). Therefore the update \(x_i^+=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j\) is a convex combination of the states used by agent \(i\), and every consensus state is fixed. Row stochasticity alone need not preserve the arithmetic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each row contains nonnegative weights summing to one, so every agent forms a convex combination and consensus states remain fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)

notation.meaning: weight used by receiver \(i\) on sender \(j\)

children.title: Column-Stochastic Mixing Conditions
children.top_down_role: Mass-preserving transport used by push-based methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Stochastic Mixing Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sender-normalized nonnegative transport preserving total mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is column-stochastic when \[w_{ij}\ge 0\quad\text{for all }i,j,\qquad \mathbf{1}_n^\top W=\mathbf{1}_n^\top.\] Equivalently, \(\sum_{i=1}^n w_{ij}=1\) for each sending agent \(j\). Hence, for \(x^+=(W\otimes I_d)x\), total mass is preserved: \[\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^+=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i.\] Column stochasticity alone need not fix consensus states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each column contains nonnegative weights summing to one, so a sender distributes all its mass and the network total is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)

notation.meaning: fraction sent from agent \(j\) to agent \(i\)

children.title: Mixing-Weight Admissibility Conditions
children.top_down_role: Weight-support and nondegeneracy requirements tied to communication edges.

children.title: Positive-Weight Conditions
children.top_down_role: Nondegeneracy requirements for active mixing weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Weight Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform lower bound on every active communication weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence of nonnegative mixing matrices \(\{W^k\}_{k\ge0}\), a uniform positive-weight condition holds if there exists \(\eta>0\) such that, for every time \(k\) and pair \((i,j)\), \[w_{ij}^k>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad w_{ij}^k\ge\eta.\] Thus active coefficients cannot approach zero along the sequence. For a single fixed matrix, the analogous condition is \(w_{ij}>0\Rightarrow w_{ij}\ge\eta\) for some \(\eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every active communication coefficient is bounded below by one common positive constant, uniformly over agents and time.
assumptions_latex: \(W^k\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n\times n}\) for every \(k\ge0\)

children.title: Graph-Support Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Alignment between nonzero weights and permitted communication links.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Support Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix sparsity constrained by the directed communication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed communication graph on \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \((j,i)\in E\) meaning that agent \(j\) can transmit to agent \(i\). A mixing matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\) is support-compatible with \(G\) when \[w_{ij}>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (j,i)\in E\ \text{ or }\ i=j.\] If every available non-self edge must be used, impose additionally \((j,i)\in E\Rightarrow w_{ij}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixing weight may be nonzero only when its sender-to-receiver communication edge exists, with diagonal self-weights treated separately.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is directed with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
\(W\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n\times n}\)

notation.meaning: weight assigned by receiver \(i\) to sender \(j\)

children.title: Self-Weight Requirements
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing retention of an agent's own information.

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Weight Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly positive diagonal weights retaining each agent's current state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence of nonnegative mixing matrices \(\{W^k\}_{k\ge0}\), a uniform self-weight requirement holds if there exists \(\eta>0\) such that \[w_{ii}^k\ge\eta\qquad\text{for every agent }i\text{ and time }k.\] Under the update \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k\), each agent therefore retains at least the fraction \(\eta\) of its own current state at every mixing round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every agent assigns its own current state a weight bounded below by the same positive constant at every communication round.
assumptions_latex: \(W^k\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n\times n}\) for every \(k\ge0\)

children.title: Degenerate-Weight Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Weight patterns that obstruct reliable information mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Weight Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of aperiodic contraction when admissible weights lie on the stochastic boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\) and let \(P\) be the cyclic-permutation matrix defined by \(Pe_i=e_{i+1}\), with indices modulo \(n\). Then \(P\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic, and its directed support graph is strongly connected, but \(P^k\) does not converge to \(J=\mathbf{1}_n\mathbf{1}_n^\top/n\). For any nonconsensus state \(x^0\), the iteration \(x^{k+1}=(P\otimes I_d)x^k\) merely cycles agent values. Thus stochasticity and strong connectivity alone do not ensure consensus when positive self-weight or an equivalent aperiodicity condition is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cyclic permutation is strongly connected and doubly stochastic but only rotates agent values, showing that connectivity and stochasticity alone do not guarantee consensus.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the cyclic-permutation matrix
\(x^0\notin\mathcal C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^k\not\to J\) and \((P\otimes I_d)^kx^0\) does not converge to consensus.

children.title: Long-Horizon Mixing Conditions
children.top_down_role: Condition families connecting graph structure to long-horizon information propagation.

children.title: Static-Graph Connectivity Conditions
children.top_down_role: Connectivity families for fixed undirected and directed networks.

assumptions_latex: The network has a finite vertex set \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Communication edges are fixed throughout the execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The static network satisfies the stated connectivity condition exactly when every ordered pair can exchange information through an admissible path.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed finite networks; both undirected connectivity and directed strong connectivity are specified.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Decentralized optimization with graph consensus p. 234
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be fixed. If \(G\) is undirected, the static connectivity condition is that for every \(i,j\in V\) there exist \(v_0=i,v_1,\ldots,v_r=j\) with \(\{v_{\ell-1},v_\ell\}\in E\) for all \(\ell\). If \(G\) is directed, strong connectivity requires such a path with \((v_{\ell-1},v_\ell)\in E\) for every ordered pair \((i,j)\). Under the convention that \((j,i)\in E\) permits agent \(i\) to receive from agent \(j\), these conditions permit information originating at any agent to reach every other agent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed undirected graph must be connected, while a fixed directed graph must be strongly connected, so information can travel between every pair of agents.
knowledge_statements.title: Static-Graph Connectivity Conditions

children.title: Time-Varying Graph Connectivity Conditions
children.top_down_role: Joint-connectivity families for graph sequences.

assumptions_latex: Each \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) has the same finite vertex set \(V\).
Time is indexed by \(k\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform \(B\)-joint connectivity holds when every consecutive window of \(B\) graphs has a connected union, or a strongly connected union in the directed case.

notation.meaning: communication graph active at time k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform joint connectivity for synchronous graph sequences with a common finite vertex set.

source_refs.locator: 11.3 Decentralized optimization with mixing matrices p. 237
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph sequence \((G_k)_{k\geq0}\) is uniformly \(B\)-jointly connected if some integer \(B\geq1\) satisfies the following condition for every \(s\geq0\): the union graph \(G_{[s,s+B-1]}=(V,\bigcup_{k=s}^{s+B-1}E_k)\) is connected when the graphs are undirected. For directed graphs, the corresponding uniform joint-strong-connectivity condition requires every such union to be strongly connected. A rooted variant replaces strong connectivity by the existence, in each union, of a directed spanning tree rooted at some vertex; that weaker variant must be stated explicitly when used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every window of a fixed finite length must contain enough edges in aggregate to connect the network; directed analyses may instead specify strong or rooted connectivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Varying Graph Connectivity Conditions

children.title: Ergodicity of Mixing-Matrix Products
children.top_down_role: Long-horizon contraction families for switching and directed networks.

assumptions_latex: Every \(W_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is row-stochastic with positive diagonal.
Every positive entry of every \(W_k\) is at least \(\alpha>0\).
The induced directed graph sequence is uniformly \(B\)-jointly strongly connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Products of the mixing matrices approach the rank-one stochastic family geometrically and therefore contract disagreement uniformly.

notation.meaning: backward product from time s through t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform geometric weak ergodicity for row-stochastic products on switching directed networks.

source_refs.locator: 11.3 Decentralized optimization with mixing matrices p. 237
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated assumptions, there exist constants \(C<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\), depending only on \(n\), \(B\), and \(\alpha\), such that for every \(t\geq s\), \[\inf_{q\in\Delta_n}\left\|W_{t:s}-\mathbf{1}q^{\mathsf T}\right\|\leq C\rho^{\lfloor (t-s+1)/B\rfloor}.\] Here \(\Delta_n=\{q\in\mathbb{R}^n:q\geq0,\ \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}q=1\}\), and the norm is any fixed matrix norm, with a corresponding value of \(C\). Thus all rows of a sufficiently long product become equal asymptotically, although their common limiting weights need not be uniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive stochastic matrices over jointly connected windows make long products geometrically close to a rank-one stochastic matrix, eliminating disagreement even when limiting weights are nonuniform.
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodicity of Mixing-Matrix Products

children.title: Network Propagation Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Spectral and diameter measures governing information propagation.

children.title: Spectral-Gap Measures
children.top_down_role: Spectral quantities associated with information propagation.

assumptions_latex: The matrix \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and doubly stochastic.
The eigenvalue \(1\) of \(W\) is simple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute spectral gap \(\gamma=1-\rho_\perp\) measures one-step contraction on the disagreement subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric doubly stochastic mixing; the absolute gap handles possible negative eigenvalues.

source_refs.locator: 11.3 Decentralized optimization with mixing matrices p. 237
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order the eigenvalues of \(W\) as \(1=\lambda_1(W)\geq\lambda_2(W)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n(W)\geq-1\). Define \[\rho_\perp=\|W-J\|_2=\max\{|\lambda_2(W)|,|\lambda_n(W)|\},\qquad \gamma=1-\rho_\perp.\] For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\|(W-J)x\|_2\leq\rho_\perp\|(I-J)x\|_2\). Hence \(\gamma>0\) exactly when one mixing step is a strict Euclidean contraction on the disagreement subspace. If \(W\) is positive semidefinite, then \(\rho_\perp=\lambda_2(W)\) and \(\gamma=1-\lambda_2(W)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute spectral gap is one minus the largest nonconsensus eigenvalue magnitude; it quantifies Euclidean contraction of disagreement by one symmetric mixing step.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Gap Measures

source_witnesses.locator: 11.3 Decentralized optimization with mixing matrices p. 237

children.title: Network Condition Numbers
children.top_down_role: Conditioning measures derived from graph or mixing operators.

assumptions_latex: The graph \(G\) is finite, connected, undirected, and has weighted Laplacian \(L\).
Edge weights are nonnegative and \(L\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The network condition number is \(\kappa_G=\lambda_{\max}(L)/\lambda_2(L)\), with larger values indicating worse propagation conditioning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laplacian condition number for a connected undirected weighted graph.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Decentralized optimization with graph consensus p. 234
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(G\) is connected, its Laplacian eigenvalues satisfy \(0=\lambda_1(L)<\lambda_2(L)\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n(L)=\lambda_{\max}(L)\). The Laplacian network condition number is \[\kappa_G=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(L)}{\lambda_2(L)}.\] Equivalently, \(\kappa_G\) is the spectral condition number of the restriction of \(L\) to \(\mathbf{1}^{\perp}\). It is invariant under uniform rescaling of all edge weights. For a mixing matrix of the form \(W=I-\eta L\), the admissible step size and resulting disagreement contraction depend on these two extreme nonzero eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The network condition number is the ratio of the largest Laplacian eigenvalue to algebraic connectivity, measuring the spectral difficulty of reducing disagreement.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Condition Numbers

children.title: Diameter–Mixing Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between graph distance and mixing quality.

assumptions_latex: Communication in one round crosses at most one edge of a fixed connected graph \(G\).
The graph diameter is \(D=\max_{i,j}d_G(i,j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global influence requires at least \(D\) rounds, and pairwise distributional mixing requires at least \(\lceil D/2\rceil\) rounds in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-speed relation between graph diameter and local synchronous mixing.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Decentralized optimization with graph consensus p. 234
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(t\) synchronous neighbor-communication rounds, the state at vertex \(i\) can depend only on initial data at vertices in \(\{j:d_G(i,j)\leq t\}\). Consequently, information from one endpoint of a diameter-realizing path cannot affect the other endpoint before \(D\) rounds. If \(P\) is any row-stochastic matrix supported on self-loops and edges of \(G\), and \(u,v\) satisfy \(d_G(u,v)=D\), then for \(2t<D\) the supports of \(e_u^{\mathsf T}P^t\) and \(e_v^{\mathsf T}P^t\) are disjoint. Their total-variation distance is therefore \(1\), precluding uniform pairwise mixing before \(\lceil D/2\rceil\) rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local communication has finite speed: diameter-separated agents cannot influence each other before D rounds, and their mixing distributions remain disjoint for fewer than half that many rounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Diameter–Mixing Relations

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Decentralized optimization with graph consensus p. 234
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Poor-Connectivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Network geometries producing severe propagation bottlenecks.

assumptions_latex: The network is the path graph \(P_n\) with \(n\geq2\).
Mixing uses a symmetric lazy nearest-neighbor stochastic matrix with edge probabilities bounded above and below by positive constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For paths, \(\gamma=\Theta(n^{-2})\), \(\kappa_G=\Theta(n^2)\), and constant-factor disagreement reduction requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) rounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path graphs exhibit a canonical vanishing-gap, ill-conditioned connectivity regime.

source_refs.locator: 11.3 Decentralized optimization with mixing matrices p. 237

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the path family \((P_n)_{n\geq2}\), the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues scale as \(\lambda_2(L)=\Theta(n^{-2})\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(L)=\Theta(1)\). Hence \(\kappa_G=\Theta(n^2)\). A symmetric lazy nearest-neighbor mixing matrix with uniformly comparable edge probabilities likewise has absolute spectral gap \(\gamma=\Theta(n^{-2})\). Its disagreement contraction factor is \(1-\Theta(n^{-2})\), so reducing Euclidean disagreement by a factor \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires \(\Theta(n^2\log(1/\varepsilon))\) rounds. Thus connectivity alone does not provide dimension-independent propagation or consensus rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connected path networks become increasingly ill-conditioned: their gap shrinks quadratically, and ordinary local mixing needs quadratically many rounds even for constant-factor disagreement reduction.
knowledge_statements.title: Poor-Connectivity Regimes

children.title: Neighborhood Broadcast Communication
children.top_down_role: A common message delivered to available neighbors.

assumptions_latex: At round \(k\), agent \(i\) has state \(x_i^k\) and available out-neighbors \(N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\).
A transmitted message is delivered reliably to every currently available out-neighbor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One broadcast action sends the same message \(m_i^k\) to every agent in \(N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A neighborhood broadcast by agent \(i\) at round \(k\) consists of forming one payload \(m_i^k=\phi_i(x_i^k)\) and delivering that identical payload to every \(j\in N_i^{\mathrm{out}}(k)\). The encoder \(\phi_i\) cannot tailor the payload to the recipient within the same broadcast action. After reception, each agent \(j\) may apply a recipient-specific update \(x_j^{k+1}=\psi_j^k(x_j^k,(m_i^k)_{i\in N_j^{\mathrm{in}}(k)})\). Thus broadcast restricts message formation, not how receivers aggregate the messages they obtain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent forms one message and sends that identical payload to all currently available neighbors; receivers may still process received messages differently.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Broadcast Communication

children.top_down_role: Selected pairs exchange and combine information.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected pair replaces its values by their average, preserving the global sum and contracting their local disagreement.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize arbitrary states \(x_1^0,\ldots,x_n^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At round \(k\), select an edge \(\{i_k,j_k\}\) according to a specified schedule or probability distribution and perform \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{j_k}^{k+1}=\frac{x_{i_k}^k+x_{j_k}^k}{2},\qquad x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\ \text{for }\ell\notin\{i_k,j_k\}.\] Stop under a prescribed round budget or disagreement tolerance and output the current local states. Every update preserves \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k\); convergence to the initial average additionally requires a selection rule that activates sufficient edges repeatedly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, one selected neighboring pair replaces both values by their average while all other agents remain unchanged; adequate repeated edge activation yields average consensus.

Payloads associated with two different outgoing edges may differ even when they have the same sender. Agent \(j\) updates according to \(x_j^{k+1}=\psi_j^k(x_j^k,(m_{i\to j}^k)_{i:(i,j)\in E_k})\). This model represents edge-specific coupling data, dual variables, or residuals and strictly contains identical-payload neighborhood broadcast as a special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each active edge may carry its own recipient-specific message, allowing agents to communicate edge variables, coupling information, or distinct residuals to different neighbors.

Messages are exchanged only along edges active at round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stateful communication updates both the primary state and persistent memory from current local information and received neighbor messages.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stateful neighbor-communication mechanism has the local state-space form \[m_{i\to j}^k=H_{ij}^k(x_i^k,z_i^k),\qquad (x_i^{k+1},z_i^{k+1})=F_i^k\left(x_i^k,z_i^k,(m_{j\to i}^k)_{j\in N_i^{\mathrm{in}}(k)}\right).\] The auxiliary variable \(z_i^k\) persists between rounds and is initialized by a specified value \(z_i^0\). Memoryless communication is recovered when \(z_i^k\) is absent or constant. Gradient trackers, compression residuals, and cached neighbor estimates fit this representation by choosing the state space and maps \(H_{ij}^k\) and \(F_i^k\) appropriately.

children.title: Linear Consensus Methods
children.top_down_role: Deterministic averaging over fixed or switching networks.

assumptions_latex: Each \(W_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is compatible with the communication graph and satisfies \(W_k\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\).
For average preservation, also \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}W_k=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\).
The matrix products contract the disagreement subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration \(X^{k+1}=W_kX^k\) converges to the rowwise initial average under doubly stochastic mixing and disagreement contraction.

notation.meaning: matrix whose rows are agent states

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial states \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), stack them as rows of \(X^0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\). At each round choose the prescribed graph-compatible mixing matrix \(W_k\) and update \[X^{k+1}=W_kX^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n (W_k)_{ij}x_j^k.\] Stop after a fixed budget or when \(\|(I-J)X^k\|\) is below a stated tolerance, and output each row. Row stochasticity preserves consensus states; column stochasticity preserves \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}X^k\). If \(\|W_{k-1:0}-J\|\to0\), then \(X^k\to JX^0\), whose rows equal \(n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents repeatedly replace their states by weighted neighbor averages. Doubly stochastic weights preserve the initial average, and contracting matrix products drive all agents to that average.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Consensus Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus certificate for fixed symmetric nonnegative mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\ge0\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). If \(\lambda_2(W)\) is the largest eigenvalue below one, then \[(I-W)X=0\iff X=JX,\qquad \|(I-J)X\|_F\le\frac{\|(I-W)X\|_F}{1-\lambda_2(W)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixing residual vanishes exactly at consensus, and the spectral gap bounds distance to consensus.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\ge0\) and \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
\(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Need Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit selected by primitive unbalanced deterministic mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W\ge0\) is primitive and row stochastic, there is a unique \(\pi>0\) with \(\pi^{\mathsf T}W=\pi^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=1\), and \[W^k\to\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T},\qquad X^k\to\mathbf1\pi^{\mathsf T}X^0.\] This equals arithmetic-average consensus for every \(X^0\) if and only if \(\pi=\mathbf1/n\), equivalently \(W\) is also column stochastic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primitive row-stochastic mixing reaches Perron-weighted consensus and preserves the arithmetic average only when it is doubly stochastic.
assumptions_latex: \(W\ge0\) is primitive.
\(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Need Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Characterization and Linear Rate of Fixed Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed symmetric deterministic mixing; gossip and polynomial acceleration are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and let \(1=\lambda_1>\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n>-1\). For \(X^{k+1}=WX^k\), \[(I-J)X^k=(W-J)^k(I-J)X^0,\qquad \|(I-J)X^k\|_2\le\rho^k\|(I-J)X^0\|_2,\] where \(\rho=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i|<1\). Conversely, convergence to \(JX^0\) for every initial state requires all nonconsensus eigenvalues to have modulus below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric average-preserving mixing reaches average consensus exactly when every nonconsensus eigenvalue lies inside the unit disk; the largest modulus is the linear factor.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) and \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\).
Eigenvalue one is simple and \(\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i(W)|<1\).

notation.meaning: Largest modulus of a nonconsensus eigenvalue.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Characterization and Linear Rate of Fixed Consensus

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let each agent hold \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\), and let \(X^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) have rows \((x_i^k)^\top\). At iteration \(k\), independently sample an edge \(e_k=\{i,j\}\) with probability \(p_{ij}>0\), and set \[x_i^{k+1}=x_j^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^k+x_j^k}{2},\qquad x_\ell^{k+1}=x_\ell^k\quad(\ell\notin\{i,j\}).\] Equivalently, \(X^{k+1}=W_{e_k}X^k\), where \(W_{\{i,j\}}=I_n-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^\top\) and \(e_i\) is the ith standard basis vector of \(\mathbb R^n\). After a prescribed number \(K\) of activations, output \(x_i^K\). Every activation preserves the network average, and connectivity with positive edge probabilities gives almost-sure convergence to that average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly selected neighbors replace their vector values by their mean. The network average is preserved, and independent positive-probability edge activations yield average consensus almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Gossip Averaging Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral rate for independent pairwise edge sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let edge \(e=\{i,j\}\) be sampled independently with probability \(p_e\), let \(W_e=I-\tfrac12(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^{\mathsf T}\), and define \(L_p=\sum_ep_e(e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)^{\mathsf T}\). For \(Z^k=(I-J)X^k\), \[\mathbb E[\|Z^{k+1}\|_F^2\mid Z^k]\le\left(1-\tfrac12\lambda_2(L_p)\right)\|Z^k\|_F^2.\] Hence \(k=O(\lambda_2(L_p)^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))\) activations suffice for relative mean-square error \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise gossip contracts mean-square disagreement geometrically at a rate governed by the probability-weighted graph's algebraic connectivity.
assumptions_latex: Edges are sampled independently with probabilities \(p_e\).
The positive-probability support graph is connected.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected Mean-Square Gossip Contraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp reachability boundary for independent pairwise gossip.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_+=\{e:p_e>0\}\). If \((V,E_+)\) is disconnected, every gossip update preserves each connected component's average independently. Initial component averages that differ can never converge to one global average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise gossip cannot reach global average consensus when the edges that can activate form a disconnected graph.
assumptions_latex: Only edges with \(p_e>0\) can activate.
The positive-probability support graph is disconnected.
knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Activation-Support Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and doubly stochastic, suppose that its eigenvalue \(1\) is simple, and suppose every other eigenvalue lies in \([-\beta,\beta]\) for some \(0<\beta<1\). For an integer \(K\ge1\), define \[q_K(t)=\frac{T_K(t/\beta)}{T_K(1/\beta)},\qquad x^K=q_K(W)x^0,\] where \(T_K\) is the degree-\(K\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind and \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). The filtered state is computable by a three-term Chebyshev recurrence using one multiplication by \(W\) per degree. Since \(q_K(1)=1\), it preserves \(\bar x^0=n^{-1}\mathbf1^\top x^0\), and its disagreement satisfies \[\|x^K-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2\le \frac{1}{|T_K(1/\beta)|}\|x^0-\mathbf1\bar x^0\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized degree-K Chebyshev filter of a symmetric mixing matrix preserves the average and contracts every nonconsensus eigenmode by at most the reciprocal of the normalization factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Consensus Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability boundary for Chebyshev consensus filters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter designed for \([-\beta,\beta]\) controls a mode \(\lambda\) only through \(|q_K(\lambda)|\). If an actual nonconsensus eigenvalue satisfies \(|\lambda|>\beta\), the minimax bound gives no contraction guarantee and \(|q_K(\lambda)|\) can exceed one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating the nonconsensus spectral interval can make a Chebyshev filter noncontractive.
assumptions_latex: The filter uses a declared spectral bound \(\beta\).
An actual nonconsensus eigenvalue may lie outside that interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Interval Misspecification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chebyshev Minimax Optimality and Accelerated Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal degree-limited contraction on a known symmetric spectral interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\beta<1\). Among real polynomials \(p\) of degree at most \(K\) satisfying \(p(1)=1\), \[q_K(t)=\frac{T_K(t/\beta)}{T_K(1/\beta)}\] minimizes \(\max_{|t|\le\beta}|p(t)|\), with optimal value \(|T_K(1/\beta)|^{-1}\). Moreover, \[|T_K(1/\beta)|^{-1}\le2\left(\frac{\beta}{1+\sqrt{1-\beta^2}}\right)^K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized Chebyshev filter is minimax-optimal among degree-K average-preserving polynomial filters and yields inverse-square-root-gap communication scaling.
assumptions_latex: The nonconsensus spectrum is contained in \([-\beta,\beta]\), \(0<\beta<1\).
Filters are real polynomials of degree at most \(K\) satisfying \(p(1)=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Chebyshev Minimax Optimality and Accelerated Rate

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing-Stepsize Distributed Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-subgradient iteration for an unconstrained convex sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agent \(i\) initializes \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and, for \(k\ge0\), selects \(g_i^k\in\partial f_i(x_i^k)\) and updates \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k g_i^k.\] Here \(W=(w_{ij})\) is a fixed doubly stochastic mixing matrix and \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\). Stop using a prescribed iteration budget or tolerance and return the local iterates. If the aggregate objective has a minimizer and all subgradients are uniformly bounded, then consensus and convergence to a common minimizer follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring iterates and takes a diminishing local subgradient step. Standard nonsummable, square-summable steps yield consensus at a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is convex and has uniformly bounded subgradients.
\(W\) is nonnegative, primitive, and doubly stochastic.
\(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i f_i(x)\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex Lipschitz rate under fixed balanced mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under fixed primitive doubly stochastic mixing and uniformly bounded subgradients, run the distributed subgradient recursion for a known horizon \(K\) with \(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\) for \(0\le k<K\), and form \[\widehat x_K=\frac1{nK}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^k.\] If an aggregate minimizer exists, constants independent of \(K\) satisfy \[\sum_i f_i(\widehat x_K)-\sum_i f_i(x^\star)\le\frac{C}{\sqrt K}.\] The constant depends on initialization, the subgradient bound, \(c\), and network mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A horizon-tuned vanishing step gives the standard order-one-over-square-root-K ergodic objective rate with a network-dependent constant.
assumptions_latex: Local objectives are convex with uniformly bounded subgradients.
Mixing is fixed, primitive, and doubly stochastic.

\(\alpha_k=c/\sqrt K\) during the length-\(K\) run.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=1\), \(f(x)=|x|\), choose \(x^0>\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k>0\), and use \(g^k=1\in\partial f(x^k)\). Then \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k,\qquad x^k\to x^0-\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k>0.\] Thus positive but summable steps can fail to reach the minimizer even without network error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite total step length can make subgradient descent stop short of the minimizer.

\(x^0>\sum_k\alpha_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Stepsize Distributed Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent disagreement in constant-step decentralized gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two agents, scalar states, \(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), \(f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-a)^2\), and \(f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x-b)^2\), where \(a\ne b\). Constant-step distributed gradient descent is \[x^{k+1}=Wx^k-\alpha\bigl(x^k-(a,b)^\top\bigr),\qquad 0<\alpha<1.\] It converges to a unique fixed point whose average equals the aggregate minimizer \(x^\star=(a+b)/2\), but whose disagreement is \[x_1^\infty-x_2^\infty=\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}(a-b)\ne0.\] Thus a fixed positive step does not generally produce exact consensus, even for smooth strongly convex quadratic objectives and complete averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-agent quadratic example shows that constant-step distributed gradient descent can converge to nonconsensual local states, with disagreement proportional to the stepsize.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb R\) with \(a\ne b\).
\(W=\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Stability Test for Quadratic DGD
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient linear stability condition for quadratic local objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}H_ix-b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\), with \(H_i=H_i^{\mathsf T}\), and set \(H=\operatorname{blkdiag}(H_1,\ldots,H_n)\). Then \[x^{k+1}=(W\otimes I-\alpha H)x^k+\alpha b.\] It converges to a unique fixed point for every initialization if and only if \(\rho(W\otimes I-\alpha H)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For quadratic objectives, fixed-step DGD is globally stable exactly when its affine iteration matrix has spectral radius below one.
assumptions_latex: Each local objective is quadratic.
The stacked iteration has the displayed affine form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\) converges uniquely for every \(x^0\) if and only if \(\rho(W\otimes I-\alpha H)<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Stability Test for Quadratic DGD

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric-mixing representation explaining constant-step network bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) and \(I-W\succeq0\), then \(X^{k+1}=WX^k-\alpha\nabla F(X^k)\) is gradient descent with stepsize \(\alpha\) on \[\Phi_\alpha(X)=F(X)+\frac1{2\alpha}\langle X,(I-W)X\rangle.\] Thus every fixed point satisfies \((I-W)X+\alpha\nabla F(X)=0\), the stationarity equation of a quadratic-penalty relaxation rather than generally the exact consensus problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plain fixed-step DGD is gradient descent on a quadratic-penalty relaxation whose penalty strength is inversely proportional to the stepsize.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\).
\(I-W\succeq0\).
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalized-Objective Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and define \(X_C^\star:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Agent \(i\) initializes \(x_i^0\in C\) and iterates \[v_i^k=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}x_j^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=P_C\bigl(v_i^k-\alpha_k\nabla f_i(v_i^k)\bigr).\] The method stops after a prescribed budget or when feasibility and consensus residuals meet specified tolerances, and it returns the local states. If the local objectives are differentiable and convex with gradients uniformly bounded on \(C\), \(W=(w_{ij})\) is nonnegative, primitive, and doubly stochastic, \(X_C^\star\neq\varnothing\), and \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then the local iterates asymptotically agree and approach \(X_C^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents average neighboring feasible states, take local gradient steps, and project onto a shared closed convex set. Under the stated mixing, bounded-gradient, minimizer-existence, and diminishing-stepsize assumptions, they approach constrained minimizers and consensus.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Distributed Subgradient Method with Agent-Local Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-constraint variant complementing the shared-set seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agent \(i\) know a nonempty closed convex set \(C_i\), with \(C=\bigcap_iC_i\ne\varnothing\). Set \[v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=P_{C_i}(v_i^k-\alpha_kg_i^k),\quad g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k).\] Under primitive doubly stochastic mixing, bounded subgradients, nonsummable square-summable steps, existence of a constrained aggregate minimizer, bounded iterates, and bounded linear regularity of \(\{C_i\}\) on the iterate region, feasibility errors and disagreement vanish and every cluster point is an aggregate minimizer over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent projects onto its own set; intersection regularity and standard diminishing steps yield common feasible optimal cluster points.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(C=\cap_iC_i\ne\varnothing\).
The iterate sequence is bounded and the sets are boundedly linearly regular on its region.
Mixing is primitive and doubly stochastic.
Subgradients are bounded and the stepsizes are nonsummable but square summable.
A constrained aggregate minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x_i^k,C)\to0\), \(\max_{i,j}\|x_i^k-x_j^k\|\to0\), and every cluster point lies in \(X_C^\star\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Distributed Subgradient Method with Agent-Local Sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for agent-local feasibility on a connected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a connected undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), define \[r_{\mathrm{feas}}(X)=\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x_i,C_i),\qquad r_{\mathrm{cons}}(X)=\max_{\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|.\] Then both residuals vanish if and only if \(x_i=x\) for every agent for some \(x\in\bigcap_iC_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero local-feasibility and edge-disagreement residuals certify a common point in every local set.
assumptions_latex: The communication graph is connected.
Each \(C_i\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Feasibility and Consensus Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility obstruction for agent-local constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bigcap_iC_i=\varnothing\), no bounded sequence can satisfy both \(\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x_i^k,C_i)\to0\) and \(\max_{i,j}\|x_i^k-x_j^k\|\to0\). Hence convergence to a common feasible optimizer is impossible regardless of the gradient or stepsize rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With empty set intersection, bounded iterates cannot become both locally feasible and consensual.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is closed.
\(\cap_iC_i=\varnothing\).
The iterate sequence is bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Intersection Boundary for Local Projections

knowledge_statements.title: Diffusion Adaptation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapt-then-combine and combine-then-adapt diffusion recursions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=(a_{\ell i})\) be nonnegative with \(\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}=1\) and \(a_{\ell i}=0\) outside agent \(i\)'s neighborhood. Adapt-then-combine diffusion uses \[\psi_i^k=x_i^k-\mu_i g_i(x_i^k),\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}\psi_\ell^k.\] Combine-then-adapt diffusion instead uses \[\phi_i^k=\sum_\ell a_{\ell i}x_\ell^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\phi_i^k-\mu_i g_i(\phi_i^k).\] Here \(g_i\) may be an exact or sampled local gradient. Initialize arbitrary local states, stop under a prescribed budget or residual rule, and output the final local states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diffusion methods either adapt locally before mixing or mix before adapting. Both use neighborhood-weighted combinations and local exact or sampled gradients.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is a local gradient or stochastic gradient oracle.
\(A\) respects the communication graph and has unit column sums.
\(\mu_i>0\) is agent i's stepsize.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursions respectively define the adapt-then-combine and combine-then-adapt diffusion families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perron-Weighted Stationarity of Diffusion Fixed Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary stationarity condition under primitive combination weights and heterogeneous stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the seed orientation and set \(B=A^{\mathsf T}\), so the combination is \(x^+=B\psi\). If \(B\) is primitive and row stochastic and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}B=\pi^{\mathsf T}\), then any consensual deterministic ATC fixed point satisfies \[\sum_i\pi_i\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0.\] A consensual CTA fixed point satisfies the stronger componentwise equations \(\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\), and hence also the displayed weighted equation. The unweighted aggregate stationarity equation is ensured for ATC when \(\pi_i\mu_i\) is constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perron weights and local stepsizes determine ATC fixed-point stationarity; a consensual CTA fixed point requires every local gradient to vanish.
assumptions_latex: The effective combination matrix is primitive and row stochastic.
Local gradients are exact.
The fixed point is consensual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i\pi_i\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for ATC, while CTA additionally requires \(\mu_i\nabla f_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative constant-step mean-square stability for ATC and CTA diffusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the Perron-and-stepsize-weighted aggregate objective is strongly convex, local gradients are Lipschitz, the combination matrix is primitive, and sampled gradients are conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moments. For sufficiently small positive constant stepsizes, ATC and CTA are mean-square stable. With \(\mu=\max_i\mu_i\), \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-x^\star\|^2=O(\mu),\qquad \limsup_{k\to\infty}\sum_i\mathbb E\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|^2=O(\mu^2).\] Persistent gradient noise therefore prevents exact last-iterate convergence at a fixed positive stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small constant-step stochastic diffusion is mean-square stable, with order-step optimization error and order-step-squared disagreement.
assumptions_latex: The weighted aggregate objective is strongly convex.
Local gradients are Lipschitz.
Samples are conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moments.
Mixing is primitive and all constant stepsizes are sufficiently small.

For differentiable local objectives \(f_i:\mathbb R^d	o\mathbb R\), initialize \(x_i^0\) arbitrarily and \(y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0)\). With a doubly stochastic matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\), iterate \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha y_i^k,\qquad y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Offset under Incorrect Tracker Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of exact tracking despite balanced mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For doubly stochastic \(W\), the tracker recursion preserves
\[
\sum_i y_i^k-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)=\sum_i y_i^0-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^0)=:\delta.
\]
Thus exact tracking requires \(\delta=0\). In the one-agent case with \(f_1\equiv0\), \(y_1^0=c\ne0\), and fixed \(\alpha>0\), one has \(y_1^k=c\) and \(x_1^k=x_1^0-k\alpha c\), although the true gradient is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced mixing cannot repair a wrong aggregate tracker initialization; the permanent offset can drive motion on a zero objective.
assumptions_latex: The tracker uses gradient differences and doubly stochastic mixing.
For the explicit example, \(n=1\), \(f_1\equiv0\), \(y_1^0=c\ne0\), and \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Offset under Incorrect Tracker Initialization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centralized descent law followed by the network average, perturbed by disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the immutable balanced gradient-tracking recursion,
\[
\bar x^{k+1}=\bar x^k-\alpha\bar y^k
=\bar x^k-\alpha{1\over n}\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k).
\]
If every \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz and \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), then
\[
\|\bar y^k-\nabla F(\bar x^k)\|\le {1\over n}\sum_iL_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The network average takes a centralized gradient step evaluated at local states, with error relative to the gradient at the average controlled by disagreement.
assumptions_latex: The immutable recursion uses a doubly stochastic matrix.
\(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\).
Each \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz for the error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x^{k+1}=\bar x^k-\alpha\bar y^k,\qquad\|\bar y^k-\nabla F(\bar x^k)\|\le n^{-1}\sum_iL_i\|x_i^k-\bar x^k\|.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient tracking driven by unbiased sampled local gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At agent \(i\), let \(g_i(x;\xi_i)\) be a stochastic gradient. Draw \(\xi_i^0\), initialize \(x_i^0\) arbitrarily and \(y_i^0=g_i(x_i^0;\xi_i^0)\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k y_i^k,\] draw \(\xi_i^{k+1}\), set \(g_i^{k+1}=g_i(x_i^{k+1};\xi_i^{k+1})\), and update \[y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+g_i^{k+1}-g_i^k.\] Stop after a prescribed sample budget and output local or averaged iterates. The tracker sum equals the sum of current sampled gradients pathwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent tracks changing stochastic gradients while mixing with neighbors. The tracker sum exactly matches the current sampled-gradient sum.

\(\mathbb E[g_i(x;\xi_i)\mid x]=\nabla f_i(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduced Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVRG-type local estimators embedded in balanced gradient tracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f_i(x)=m_i^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{m_i}f_{ir}(x)\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) samples \(r_i^k\) uniformly and forms the snapshot estimator \[v_i^k=
abla f_{i r_i^k}(x_i^k)-
abla f_{i r_i^k}(\widetilde x_i)+
abla f_i(\widetilde x_i).\] With \(y_i^0=v_i^0\), update \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha y_i^k,\qquad y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+v_i^{k+1}-v_i^k.\] Refresh each snapshot and its full local gradient periodically, stop after a prescribed component-gradient budget, and output the final local states. Conditionally, \(v_i^k\) is unbiased for \(
abla f_i(x_i^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SVRG estimator replaces raw stochastic gradients inside the tracking recursion, reducing sampling variance through periodically refreshed local snapshots.
assumptions_latex: Each local objective is a finite average of differentiable component functions.
Each component index is sampled uniformly, conditionally on the current history.
\(W\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.

knowledge_statements.title: Tracking under Gradient Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tracking invariant and residual variance under additive gradient noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\varepsilon_i^k\), initialize \(y_i^0=g_i^0\), and use \[y^{k+1}=Wy^k+g^{k+1}-g^k\] with a doubly stochastic \(W\). Then the telescoping identity \(\sum_i y_i^k=\sum_i g_i^k\) holds pathwise. Consequently, the average tracker equals \[\bar y^k=\frac1n\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)+\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k,\] rather than the exact average gradient. If the noises are conditionally independent, centered, and satisfy \(\mathbb E[\|\varepsilon_i^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2\), then the mean-square average tracking noise is at most \(\sigma^2/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient tracking preserves the sum of noisy gradients, not true gradients. Independent centered noise leaves average tracker variance of order one over the network size.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(y^0=g^0\).
\(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and noises are conditionally independent across agents.

Then \[\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k=z^k,\qquad \mathbb E\left[\left\|\frac1n\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k\right\|^2\middle|\mathcal F_k\right]=\sigma^2,\] independently of \(n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\varepsilon^k=n^{-1}\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k\), with conditionally centered square-integrable vector noises. Then \[\mathbb E[\|\bar\varepsilon^k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E[\langle\varepsilon_i^k,\varepsilon_j^k\rangle\mid\mathcal F_k].\] Hence the \(1/n\) variance reduction in the seed follows from vanishing cross terms and does not follow from centered marginals alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network averaging reduces gradient-noise variance only to the extent that cross-agent covariances cancel.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents be indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Agent \(i\) holds \(m_i\) differentiable component functions \(f_{ij}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) and has local objective \(f_i(x)=m_i^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}f_{ij}(x)\). Let \(\mathcal F_k\) denote the history before iteration-\(k\) sampling, with \(x_i^k\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_k\). Independent sampling uses indices that are conditionally independent across agents, with fresh draws over iterations. Common-randomness sampling uses a shared random variable or seed that may induce dependence among the agents' indices. Random reshuffling draws a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,m_i\}\) for each local epoch and visits every component once in that order. If \(\mathbb P(\xi_i^k=j\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_{ij}>0\), then the importance-weighted estimator \(g_i^k=(m_i p_{i\xi_i^k})^{-1}\nabla f_{i\xi_i^k}(x_i^k)\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local finite sum may be sampled using conditionally independent draws, shared randomness, or random reshuffling. For a draw having the stated conditional probabilities, importance weighting makes the sampled gradient conditionally unbiased.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
During a random-reshuffling epoch, let \(S_k\) be the component indices not yet visited. Conditional on the within-epoch history, \[\mathbb E[
abla f_{i\xi_i^k}(x_i^k)\mid\mathcal F_k]= rac1{|S_k|}\sum_{j\in S_k}
abla f_{ij}(x_i^k),\] which generally differs from \(
abla f_i(x_i^k)=m_i^{-1}\sum_j
abla f_{ij}(x_i^k)\). Thus with-replacement martingale-difference arguments do not apply stepwise without modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random reshuffling is uniform over the remaining components, so its within-epoch gradient is generally not conditionally unbiased for the full local gradient.
assumptions_latex: A uniformly random permutation is traversed without replacement within each epoch.
The conditioning history reveals the indices already visited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Variance of Importance-Weighted Component Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-sample variance formula and variance-minimizing probabilities at a fixed local iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At fixed \(x\), write \(a_j=\nabla f_{ij}(x)\), \(\bar a=m_i^{-1}\sum_j a_j\), and sample \(J\) with \(p_j>0\). For \(g=a_J/(m_ip_J)\), \[\mathbb E\|g-\bar a\|^2=\frac1{m_i^2}\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}\frac{\|a_j\|^2}{p_j}-\|\bar a\|^2.\] If every \(a_j\ne0\), this is minimized by \(p_j=\|a_j\|/\sum_\ell\|a_\ell\|\). If some \(a_j=0\) while strict positivity is required, the same value is an infimum approached by assigning those indices arbitrarily small positive mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance sampling is unbiased, and probabilities proportional to nonzero component-gradient norms minimize its conditional second moment at a fixed iterate.
assumptions_latex: The component gradients exist at the fixed iterate.
Sampling probabilities are strictly positive and sum to one.

notation.meaning: component gradient at the fixed local iterate
