knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed balanced-network rate family for smooth strongly convex aggregate optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be fixed, symmetric, and doubly stochastic, with \(\rho=\|W-n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\|_2<1\). Suppose every \(f_i\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. For correctly initialized deterministic gradient tracking, there is a variant-dependent threshold \(\bar\alpha(L,\mu,\rho)>0\) such that, for \(0<\alpha<\bar\alpha\), constants \(C<\infty\) and \(q\in(0,1)\) satisfy \[\|X^k-\mathbf1(x^*)^\top\|_F^2+\|Y^k\|_F^2\le Cq^k.\] Hence this squared-error metric reaches \(\varepsilon\) in \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\) communication rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth strongly convex deterministic gradient tracking converges geometrically for a sufficiently small network-dependent constant stepsize.
assumptions_latex: The fixed balanced network has disagreement contraction \(\rho<1\).
Every local gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz and the aggregate objective is \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
The tracker is correctly initialized and the constant stepsize is below the selected recursion's stability threshold.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\) is bounded below, every \(f_i\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, the fixed balanced network contracts disagreement, and deterministic gradient tracking uses correct initialization and a sufficiently small constant stepsize. Standard Lyapunov analyses give \[\min_{0\le k<K}\left(\|\nabla F(\bar x^k)\|^2+\|X^k-\mathbf1(\bar x^k)^\top\|_F^2\right)\le\frac{C}{K}.\] Thus this squared stationarity-consensus metric reaches \(\varepsilon\) in \(O(1/\varepsilon)\) rounds.

children.title: Successive-Update Difference Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Correction structures based on differences across consecutive network states.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Update Differences Are Not an Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of successive-update residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(X^{k+1}-X^k\to0\) alone implies neither \((I-W)X^k\to0\) nor \(\mathbf1^\top G(X^k)\to0\). A constant nonconsensual sequence has zero update differences, and a constant consensual sequence can have nonzero aggregate first-order information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero update difference can occur at a nonconsensual or nonstationary state.
assumptions_latex: No method-specific fixed-point equation or initialization invariant is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Update Differences Are Not an Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic mechanism supplied by consecutive first-order differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Delta G^k=G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\), \[\sum_{k=1}^{K}\Delta G^k=G(X^K)-G(X^0).\] Thus accumulation of a successive-difference correction depends only on endpoint first-order maps; aggregate stationarity still requires a method-specific initialization invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive first-order differences telescope to an endpoint difference but do not alone imply stationarity.
assumptions_latex: All \(G(X^k)\) belong to the same vector space.
knowledge_statements.title: Telescoping Successive-Correction Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraically exact conversion of a generic two-step correction recurrence into state-difference coordinates, without asserting a method-specific invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[X^{k+1}=A_1X^k-A_0X^{k-1}-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr)\] and define \(S^k=X^k-X^{k-1}\). Then the equivalent first-order system is \[S^{k+1}=(A_1-A_0-I)X^k+A_0S^k-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr),\qquad X^{k+1}=X^k+S^{k+1}.\] This coordinate change alone supplies no aggregate-stationarity invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-step correction becomes a first-order system in the current state and its successive difference; the current-state coefficient is A1 minus A0 minus the identity.
assumptions_latex: \(A_0\) and \(A_1\) are linear operators on the state space.
All displayed first-order-map values belong to the same vector space.

notation.meaning: linear operators in the two-step recurrence

review_flags: This is an algebraic equivalence only; exactness and convergence require method-specific initialization and stability conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact State-Difference Normal Form
Successive-Update Difference Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-step correction represented through differences of consecutive gradients and iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A successive-difference exact-correction scheme admits the two-step form \[X^{k+1}=A_1X^k-A_0X^{k-1}-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr),\] where \(A_0\) and \(A_1\) are network-local linear maps and \(G(X)\) stacks local first-order information. Equivalently, with \(S^k=X^k-X^{k-1}\), \[S^{k+1}=(A_1-A_0)X^k+A_0S^k-\alpha\bigl(G(X^k)-G(X^{k-1})\bigr).\] At a convergent trajectory the successive differences vanish, while summing the invariant induced by the initialization yields aggregate stationarity; this is the mechanism by which persistent local-gradient disagreement is canceled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differences of consecutive iterates and gradients preserve a correction invariant while canceling persistent disagreement at convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(A_0\) and \(A_1\) respect the communication graph.
The initialization supplies the aggregate-stationarity invariant required by the chosen method.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the representation algebraically covers canonical two-step exact-correction recurrences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the mechanism leaf, but the claimed equivalent recurrence is algebraically incorrect. From S^k=X^k-X^{k-1}, subtracting X^k from the two-step update yields the coefficient A_1-A_0-I on X^k, not A_1-A_0. The asserted initialization invariant and aggregate-stationarity consequence are also method-dependent and unspecified. A method-family source is needed to determine the intended corrected representation.

children.title: Exact-Correction Applicability
children.top_down_role: Network and objective regimes supporting exact first-order correction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-independent network requirement for global exact correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed-point argument based on (I-W)X=0, global consensus follows for every fixed point if and only if \ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}. If the nullspace is larger, the equation permits nonconsensual componentwise constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixing fixed-point space must equal global consensus; otherwise exact-correction equations certify only componentwise agreement.
assumptions_latex: The method uses (I-W)X=0 as its limiting consensus equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Identifiability Is Necessary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common Local Minimizers Are Not Required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-heterogeneity regime compatible with aggregate exact correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact first-order correction targets \sum_i\nabla f_i(x^\star)=0, not \nabla f_i(x^\star)=0 for every agent. For f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2 and f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x+1)^2, the local minimizer sets are disjoint, but their average has the unique minimizer x^\star=0, where the local gradients cancel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact correction can handle heterogeneous objectives even when no point minimizes every local objective.
assumptions_latex: The correction mechanism enforces aggregate-gradient cancellation.
The aggregate objective has the stated stationary point.
knowledge_statements.title: Common Local Minimizers Are Not Required

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Exact Stationary Fixed Point Without Aggregate Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-existence boundary independent of the chosen correction recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If

e0 for every x, no consensual state can satisfy both (I-W)X=0 and \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}
abla f(X)=0. Hence an algorithm whose fixed points obey these equations cannot converge to a finite exact stationary fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact correction cannot produce a finite exact solution when the aggregate objective has no stationary point.
assumptions_latex: \ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}.
Exact fixed points obey consensus and aggregate-gradient cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:\nabla F(x)=0\}=\varnothing\Rightarrow\text{no finite exact-correction fixed point exists}.
knowledge_statements.title: No Exact Stationary Fixed Point Without Aggregate Stationarity
Exact-Correction Applicability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient structural conditions for fixed-step exact correction on an undirected network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-step successive-difference exact correction is applicable when: the communication graph is fixed, connected, and undirected; a symmetric mixing matrix \(W\) satisfies \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\); every agent can evaluate its local gradient and retain one previous iterate and gradient; and the aggregate objective is convex with Lipschitz gradient. For linear convergence, additionally require strong convexity and choose the step size below the method-specific bound determined by objective and network conditioning. These conditions make the consensus constraint identifiable and the local two-step recurrence implementable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact correction applies when mixing identifies consensus, agents retain one-step memory, and objective regularity supports the required step-size bound.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^\top\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
Each agent can communicate with its neighbors and store one previous state and gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{consensus is identifiable and the successive-difference correction is locally implementable}.\]

children.title: Exact Diffusion Method
children.top_down_role: Diffusion-style exact correction and its stochastic variants.

children.title: Deterministic Exact Diffusion
children.top_down_role: Exact diffusion with deterministic local derivative information.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Exact Diffusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapt-correct-combine exact diffusion with deterministic local gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix and \(\bar A=(I+A)/2\). Each agent initializes \(x_i^0\), computes \(\psi_i^0=x_i^0-\alpha\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\), sets \(\phi_i^0=\psi_i^0\), and combines \(x_i^1=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\phi_j^0\). For \(k\ge1\), it performs \[\psi_i^k=x_i^k-\alpha\nabla f_i(x_i^k),\qquad \phi_i^k=\psi_i^k+x_i^k-\psi_i^{k-1},\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\phi_j^k.\] Stop when the consensus residual and successive-step norm satisfy prescribed tolerances; output the agents' final iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic exact diffusion applies a local gradient step, a one-step bias correction, and neighbor averaging at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^\top\), \(A\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and the induced graph is connected.
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable and its exact gradient is available.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the adapt-correct-combine recurrence is the canonical deterministic exact-diffusion form

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is correct for the deterministic exact-diffusion leaf, and the adapt-correct-combine form is recognizable. However, the initialization and index convention must be matched to a primary exact-diffusion source, and the orientation of the coefficients in the combine step must be consistent with that source's stochasticity convention. The missing source makes the precise algorithm unreliable.

children.title: Stochastic Exact Diffusion
children.top_down_role: Exact diffusion with sampled local information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Exact Diffusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact diffusion using conditionally unbiased sampled local gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the deterministic exact-diffusion initialization and mixing matrix, but at iteration \(k\) let agent \(i\) obtain \(g_i^k=g_i(x_i^k,\xi_i^k)\). It updates \[\psi_i^k=x_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k,\qquad \phi_i^k=\psi_i^k+x_i^k-\psi_i^{k-1},\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\sum_j\bar a_{ij}\phi_j^k.\] The oracle must satisfy \(\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|g_i^k-\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_i^2\). Stop at a prescribed iteration budget or residual tolerance and output the last iterate or a specified time average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic exact diffusion replaces each exact local gradient by an unbiased bounded-variance sample while retaining adapt-correct-combine updates.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[g_i^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\).
\(\mathbb E[\|g_i^k-\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_i^2<\infty\).
The mixing matrix satisfies the deterministic exact-diffusion connectivity conditions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unbiased bounded-variance substitution is the canonical stochastic specialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the stochastic exact-diffusion leaf, but the record inherits an unverified deterministic initialization and allows either a last iterate or time average without identifying the result for which each output is appropriate. Constant versus diminishing step sizes and the relevant stochastic exact-diffusion variant are also source-dependent. A specific source is required.

children.title: Exact-Diffusion Bias-Correction Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families explaining removal of steady-state network bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Diffusion Bias-Correction Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic convergence statement emphasizing removal of constant-step network bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, smooth, and strongly convex, and let the fixed undirected communication graph admit a symmetric doubly stochastic matrix \(A\) with \(\ker(I-A)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). For deterministic exact diffusion with a sufficiently small constant step size \(\alpha>0\), there exist \(C<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \[\|X^k-\mathbf1(x^\star)^\top\|^2\le C\rho^k,\] where \(x^\star\) is the unique minimizer of \(n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\). Hence the limiting consensus point is \(x^\star\), with no nonzero steady-state network bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With smooth strongly convex objectives and a small constant step, deterministic exact diffusion converges linearly to the exact consensual optimizer.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is smooth and strongly convex.
\(A=A^\top\), \(A\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), and \(\ker(I-A)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
\(\alpha>0\) satisfies the method-specific stability bound.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linear exact convergence is the canonical strongly-convex deterministic result

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is correct for this convergence leaf, but a linear-convergence theorem cannot be accepted from standard-field rationale alone. The exact admissible step-size and any additional eigenvalue, weighting, initialization, or objective assumptions must be taken from a method-specific theorem. No supporting source is supplied.

children.title: Primal-Dual Views of Exact Correction
children.top_down_role: Constraint-dual interpretations of exact decentralized methods.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disconnected Constraints Yield Only Componentwise Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity boundary for interpreting correction states as global-consensus multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \ker B\supsetneq\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}, then BX=0 permits distinct constants on different connected components. Moreover, G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 implies G\perp\ker B, imposing zero gradient sum on each component rather than only globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a connected consensus operator, primal-dual correction enforces componentwise consensus and stationarity rather than the intended global problem.
assumptions_latex: \ker B strictly contains the global-consensus subspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Constraints Yield Only Componentwise Correction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Correction Exists Exactly for Zero Aggregate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range characterization explaining how a multiplier balances heterogeneous local gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n} satisfy \ker B=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}. For G\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}, \exists Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}:G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 if and only if \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}G=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected consensus operator, a multiplier cancels heterogeneous local gradients exactly when they sum to zero.
assumptions_latex: \ker B=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}.

notation.meaning: stacked local gradients at a consensual state

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Correction Exists Exactly for Zero Aggregate Gradient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of correction states under redundant consensus constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Y satisfies G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0, then Y+H satisfies it for every H\in\ker(B^{\mathsf T}). Thus the correction state is unique only modulo \ker(B^{\mathsf T}) unless a gauge or full-row-rank constraint representation is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant consensus constraints make the correction state nonunique without altering primal stationarity.
assumptions_latex: A multiplier Y satisfying G+B^{\mathsf T}Y=0 exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Gauge Freedom
Primal-Dual Views of Exact Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-constrained optimization expressed through its primal-dual optimality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\) and choose a graph operator \(B\) satisfying \(BX=0\) exactly when all rows of \(X\) agree. The decentralized problem has the equivalent saddle representation \[\min_X\;F(X)\ \text{subject to}\ BX=0\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \min_X\max_Y\;F(X)+\langle Y,BX\rangle.\] For differentiable convex \(F\), a pair \((X^\star,Y^\star)\) is optimal precisely when \[\nabla F(X^\star)+B^\top Y^\star=0,\qquad BX^\star=0.\] Exact-correction recurrences can be viewed as primal-dual iterations for these equations, sometimes after eliminating the dual variable to obtain a two-step primal recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact decentralized correction enforces the KKT equations of a consensus-constrained problem, with the correction state acting as a dual variable.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex and differentiable.
\(\ker B\) is the consensus subspace and a saddle point exists.

children.title: Operator-Splitting Views of Exact Correction
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point and monotone-inclusion interpretations of exact methods.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Naive Forward Treatment of Skew Consensus Coupling Is Expansive
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting the consensus primal-dual inclusion as ordinary forward-backward splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal K be a nonzero bounded skew-adjoint linear operator. For every \gamma>0 and z, \|(I-\gamma\mathcal K)z\|^2=\|z\|^2+\gamma^2\|\mathcal Kz\|^2. Thus the forward map is expansive on every direction for which \mathcal Kz\ne0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero skew consensus coupling cannot be used naively as the forward component of ordinary forward-backward splitting.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal K^*=-\mathcal K and \mathcal K\ne0.
\gamma>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal Kz\ne0\Longrightarrow\|(I-\gamma\mathcal K)z\|>\|z\|;\text{ a separate splitting or preconditioner analysis is required}.
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Forward Treatment of Skew Consensus Coupling Is Expansive
Operator-Splitting Views of Exact Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone-inclusion representation of consensus optimality and exact correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper closed convex \(F\) and a consensus operator \(B\), define \(Z=(X,Y)\) and \[\mathcal A(Z)=\begin{pmatrix}\partial F(X)\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathcal K(Z)=\begin{pmatrix}B^\top Y\\-BX\end{pmatrix}.\] Then the consensus KKT system is the monotone inclusion \(0\in\mathcal A(Z)+\mathcal K(Z)\). Whenever a positive-definite preconditioner \(P\) makes the required resolvent computable, a preconditioned splitting has fixed-point form \[Z^{k+1}=J_{P^{-1}\mathcal A}\bigl(Z^k-P^{-1}\mathcal KZ^k\bigr).\] Eliminating or reparameterizing \(Y\) can produce the successive-difference primal recurrences used by exact decentralized corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus KKT conditions form a monotone inclusion; preconditioned splitting and dual elimination yield exact-correction fixed-point recurrences.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(B\) has the consensus subspace as its kernel.
\(P\) is positive definite and the displayed resolvent is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\in\mathcal A(Z)+\mathcal K(Z),\qquad Z=T(Z)\ \text{at every splitting fixed point}.\]

notation.meaning: subdifferential component of the KKT operator

children.title: Push-Sum Consensus
children.top_down_role: Ratio-based averaging under mass-preserving directed communication.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unnormalized Directed Mixing Is Generally Biased
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of ratio normalization on unbalanced directed graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be primitive and column-stochastic with \(A^k\to\pi\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\). Unless \(\pi=\mathbf1/n\), \(A^ks^0\to\pi\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0\), whose components are unequal for generic nonzero total mass. Division by \(A^kw^0\) cancels this Perron profile.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column-stochastic directed mixing alone approaches a nonuniform Perron profile; push-sum denominators remove that bias.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is primitive and column-stochastic.
Its normalized right Perron vector is nonuniform.

notation.meaning: normalized positive right Perron vector of A

knowledge_statements.title: Unnormalized Directed Mixing Is Generally Biased

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining algebraic invariants of push-sum normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s^{k+1}=As^k\) and \(w^{k+1}=Aw^k\) with column-stochastic \(A\), \[\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0,\qquad \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0.\] Replacing \((s^0,w^0)\) by \((cs^0,cw^0)\), \(c>0\), leaves every defined ratio \(s_i^k/w_i^k\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum conserves numerator and denominator mass separately, and common positive rescaling leaves all ratios unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is column-stochastic.
Ratios are evaluated only where denominators are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0\), \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^k=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0\), and the ratios are scale invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Mass Conservation and Scale Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication rounds implied by geometric ratio contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e_k\le C'\rho^k\), then \(e_k\le\varepsilon\) whenever \(k\ge\left\lceil\log(C'/\varepsilon)/(-\log\rho)\right\rceil\). With one directed exchange stage per iteration, this is also the communication-round bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric push-sum contraction gives logarithmic round complexity in inverse accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration has one directed communication stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Matrix Push-Sum Communication Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-time convergence consequence for fixed primitive column-stochastic push-sum dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be primitive and column-stochastic, \(A^k=\pi\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}+R_k\), and \(\|R_k\|\le C\rho^k\) with \(0<\rho<1\). For \(s^k=A^ks^0\), \(w^k=A^kw^0\), and \(w^0>0\), there are \(C'>0\) and \(k_0\) such that \(\max_i\|s_i^k/w_i^k-(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s^0)/(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0)\|\le C'\rho^k\) for \(k\ge k_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perron convergence yields geometric convergence of fixed-matrix push-sum ratios.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is primitive and column-stochastic.
The displayed Perron remainder bound holds.
review_flags: Constants depend on the Perron vector and denominator lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Fixed-Matrix Ratio Consensus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Hull Certificate for the Conserved-Mass Ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Snapshot ratio-spread certificate for scalar push-sum states with positive denominator masses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_i^k>0\), \(x_i^k=s_i^k/w_i^k\), and suppose numerator and denominator masses are conserved. Then \[\bar x=\frac{\sum_i s_i^k}{\sum_i w_i^k}=\frac{\sum_i w_i^k x_i^k}{\sum_i w_i^k}\in[\min_i x_i^k,\max_i x_i^k].\] Hence an exact global-extrema computation satisfying \(\max_i x_i^k-\min_i x_i^k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(|x_i^k-\bar x|\le\varepsilon\) for every node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conserved target is a positive weighted average of the current ratios, so an exact global ratio spread bounds every node's error.
assumptions_latex: The push-sum states are scalar.
\(w_i^k>0\) for every node.
Numerator and denominator masses are conserved.
The extrema refer to one common snapshot and are computed exactly.

notation.meaning: conserved numerator mass divided by conserved denominator mass

review_flags: For vector states, a coordinatewise or separately justified convex-hull diameter certificate is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Certificate for the Conserved-Mass Ratio
Push-Sum Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio consensus for a fixed primitive column-stochastic directed network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\ge0\) be a primitive column-stochastic matrix compatible with a strongly connected directed graph. Initialize arbitrary scalar or vector numerators \(s_i^0\) and weights \(w_i^0=1\). For \(k\ge0\), each node distributes its current mass according to its column of \(A\) and updates \[s^{k+1}=As^k,\qquad w^{k+1}=Aw^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=s_i^{k+1}/w_i^{k+1}.\] Since \(A^k\to\pi\mathbf1^\top\) for some \(\pi>0\), every denominator remains eventually positive and \[x_i^k\longrightarrow\frac{\mathbf1^\top s^0}{\mathbf1^\top w^0}=\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n s_j^0.\] Stop at a communication budget or ratio-disagreement tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum separately transports value and weight mass; their ratio removes directed-network imbalance and converges to the initial average.
assumptions_latex: \(A\ge0\), \(\mathbf1^\top A=\mathbf1^\top\), and \(A\) is primitive.
\(w^0=\mathbf1\).

notation.meaning: normalizing weight mass at node i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Perron convergence of a primitive column-stochastic matrix yields the stated ratio-consensus limit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind, primitive column-stochastic assumptions, ratio update, and average-consensus limit are mathematically coherent for fixed-matrix push-sum. However, no inspectable source is supplied, and standard-field rationale alone cannot certify this candidate-review record. Add a primary push-sum reference with a theorem or section locator.

children.title: Push-Sum Optimization Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed-objective weighting error caused by omitting ratio correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let directed mixing have nonuniform stationary influence weights \(\pi_i>0\). Without normalization or an equivalent correction, a directed descent method may target \(F_\pi(x)=\sum_i\pi_i f_i(x)\) rather than \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\). For \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12(x-a_i)^2\), the respective minimizers are \(\sum_i\pi_i a_i\) and \(n^{-1}\sum_i a_i\), which differ for suitable \(a_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without normalization, directed mixing can optimize a Perron-weighted objective instead of the intended uniform aggregate.
assumptions_latex: The directed influence vector \(\pi\) is nonuniform.
No normalization or stationary-distribution correction is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i\pi_i f_i(x)\ne\operatorname*{argmin}_x n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\) for some quadratic local objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Bias Without Push-Sum Normalization

assumptions_latex: Each local objective \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical subgradient-perturbed push-sum iteration on a directed network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), initialize \(z_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(w_i^0=1\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) evaluates \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\), where \(x_i^k=z_i^k/w_i^k\), and communicates weighted values along its outgoing arcs. It then updates
\[
z_i^{k+1}=\sum_j a_{ij}^k z_j^k-\alpha_k g_i^k,\qquad w_i^{k+1}=\sum_j a_{ij}^k w_j^k,
\]
and sets \(x_i^{k+1}=z_i^{k+1}/w_i^{k+1}\). Stop under a prescribed residual, iteration, or communication budget and return the normalized states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents mix numerator and weight variables with a column-stochastic directed operator, subtract local gradients, and divide by the propagated weights to remove mixing bias.
knowledge_statements.title: Push-Sum Optimization Methods

assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.

notation.meaning: local primal variable at agent i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-matrix push-pull gradient method with separate directed mixing operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a stepsize \(\alpha>0\), initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\). Stack the local variables as \(x^k\) and \(y^k\). The push-pull iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=Rx^k-\alpha y^k,\qquad y^{k+1}=Cy^k+\nabla f(x^{k+1})-\nabla f(x^k),
\]
where the gradient map is applied blockwise. The row-stochastic operator forms primal averages, while the column-stochastic operator preserves the sum of tracking variables. Stop under a prescribed consensus-stationarity tolerance or budget and return the agent states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents use a row-stochastic operator for primal mixing and a column-stochastic operator for gradient tracking, thereby accommodating directed communication without a common doubly stochastic matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Push-Pull Optimization Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and row-stochastic/column-stochastic division match the local topic, but the exact fixed-matrix recursion and its graph-compatibility requirements have no cited source. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Perturbations Generally Shift the Push-Sum Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction to the deferred claim that summability preserves the unperturbed average.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed primitive column-stochastic \(A\), let \(z^{k+1}=Az^k+e^k\), \(w^{k+1}=Aw^k\), \(w^0>0\), and \(\sum_k\|e^k\|<\infty\). Then the common ratio limit is \[\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z^0+\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}e^k}{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0}.\] It equals the unperturbed value only when the total injected mass is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable numerator disturbances preserve agreement under stable fixed mixing but generally shift the common value by their total injected mass.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is primitive and column-stochastic.
\(\sum_k\|e^k\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Perturbations Generally Shift the Push-Sum Limit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity obstruction to universal push-sum agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If after some finite time a directed graph sequence is reducible across a nontrivial ordered partition, compatible column-stochastic push-sum products cannot force every initialization to one common ratio. In particular, a fixed reducible mixing matrix cannot guarantee global ratio consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Push-sum cannot guarantee global agreement when directed information flow is permanently reducible.
assumptions_latex: Mixing matrices are graph-compatible and column-stochastic.
The graph sequence is eventually reducible across a nontrivial partition.
knowledge_statements.title: Lack of Recurrent Directed Reachability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unperturbed push-sum convergence under regular directed graph products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^k\) be column-stochastic matrices with positive diagonals, every positive entry at least \(\eta>0\), and graph unions over every \(B\) consecutive iterations strongly connected. For \(z^{k+1}=A^kz^k\), \(w^{k+1}=A^kw^k\), and \(w^0>0\), all denominators remain positive and there exist \(C<\infty\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \[\max_i\left\|\frac{z_i^k}{w_i^k}-\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z^0}{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}w^0}\right\|\le C\rho^k\|z^0\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform positivity, self-loops, and bounded-window strong connectivity keep push-sum normalization valid and yield geometric ratio consensus.
assumptions_latex: Each \(A^k\) is column-stochastic and graph-compatible.
Every positive entry is at least \(\eta>0\), including a positive diagonal entry.
Every union of \(B\) consecutive directed graphs is strongly connected.

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on positive mixing weights

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Time-Varying Push-Sum Convergence

assumptions_latex: Every positive entry of each \(A^k\) is at least \(\eta>0\), and each \(A^k\) has positive diagonal.
Each \(A^k\) is column-stochastic and respects the directed communication graph.
There exists \(B\geq1\) such that every union of \(B\) consecutive graphs is strongly connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Push-sum weights remain positive and normalized ratios asymptotically agree; summable perturbations do not change the consensus limit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard uniform joint-connectivity condition for time-varying directed push-sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^{k+1}=A^kz^k+e^k\), \(w^{k+1}=A^kw^k\), and \(x_i^k=z_i^k/w_i^k\), with \(w^0=\mathbf{1}\). The directed push-sum convergence condition requires column stochasticity, uniformly positive active weights, positive self-weights, and uniform strong connectivity over every \(B\)-step window. Under these conditions the weights satisfy \(w_i^k>0\), and for the unperturbed recursion \(e^k=0\), all ratios converge to \(\frac{1}{n}\sum_i z_i^0\). The same consensus conclusion holds for vanishing accumulated disturbances when \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e^k\rVert<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive column-stochastic weights, self-loops, and repeated strong connectivity keep normalization valid and force push-sum ratios to consensus, including under summable disturbances.
knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Graph Push-Sum Convergence Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) forms the consensus point \(v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k\), obtains \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(v_i^k)\), and computes
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k r_i}\!\left(v_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k\right),
\qquad
\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(u)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\{r(x)+\frac{\lVert x-u\rVert^2}{2\alpha}\right\}.
\]
Agents exchange the new iterates and repeat. Stop under a prescribed consensus-optimality residual or budget and return the local states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring iterates, takes a local gradient step, and applies its local proximal map to handle nonsmooth structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consensus Fixed-Point Boundary of Combine-Then-Proximal Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact obstruction to aggregate optimality for the accepted uncorrected constant-step recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(\alpha>0\) and row-stochastic \(W\), a consensual state \(x_i=x^*\) is a fixed point of the accepted update exactly when, for every agent,
\[
x^*=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r_i}(x^*-\alpha\nabla f_i(x^*))
\iff0\in\nabla f_i(x^*)+\partial r_i(x^*).
\]
Aggregate stationarity does not generally imply these agentwise conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consensual fixed point of plain constant-step proximal consensus must solve every local composite problem, which is stronger than solving their sum.
assumptions_latex: The accepted combine-then-proximal recursion uses fixed \(\alpha>0\).
\(W\) is row-stochastic.
Each \(r_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf1\otimes x^*\text{ is fixed}\iff0\in\nabla f_i(x^*)+\partial r_i(x^*)\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Fixed-Point Boundary of Combine-Then-Proximal Updates

\]
The proposal claims exact consensus convergence to a minimizer under doubly stochastic joint connectivity, bounded composite subgradients, attainment, and nonsummable square-summable stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed theorem claims exact convergence of the uncorrected diminishing-step proximal-consensus iteration.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex and differentiable, and each \(r_i\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable.
The aggregate objective attains a minimizer.

children.title: Proximal Gradient Tracking
children.top_down_role: Composite optimization combining proximal structure and gradient tracking.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tracker-Initialization Bias in Proximal Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent aggregate offset caused by incorrect tracker initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For doubly stochastic mixing and the gradient-difference tracker recursion, define
\[
\delta=\sum_i y_i^0-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^0).
\]
Then
\[
\sum_i y_i^k-\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)=\delta
\]
for every \(k\). At a consensual fixed point with tracker consensus, the proximal condition is therefore shifted to
\[
0\in\nabla F(x^*)+{\delta\over n}+\partial r(x^*),
\]
so true composite stationarity is not guaranteed unless \(\delta=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect tracker initialization creates a permanent aggregate offset and shifts the fixed-point stationarity condition.
assumptions_latex: The tracker update uses doubly stochastic mixing and gradient differences.
A consensual fixed point with tracker consensus exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta\ne0\Longrightarrow\text{the fixed-point condition is generally }0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\delta/n+\partial r(x^*).
knowledge_statements.title: Tracker-Initialization Bias in Proximal Gradient Tracking

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consensual Fixed Points Are Composite Stationary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness property of a correctly initialized common-regularizer proximal gradient-tracking recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\). Suppose the fixed mixing matrix \(W\) is doubly stochastic with \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), the tracker invariant \(\sum_i y_i=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\) holds, and the displayed proximal gradient-tracking recursion has a fixed point with \(x_i=x^*\) for every \(i\). The tracker fixed-point equation then makes all \(y_i\) equal to \(\nabla F(x^*)\), and
\[
x^*=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(x^*-\alpha y_i)
\iff0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\partial r(x^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any consensual fixed point of correctly initialized proximal gradient tracking is stationary for the aggregate smooth objective plus the common regularizer.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable and \(r\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(W\) is doubly stochastic and has only consensus fixed vectors.
The tracker-sum invariant and the fixed-point equations of the common-regularizer recursion hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i=x^*\ \forall i\text{ at a fixed point}\Longrightarrow0\in\nabla F(x^*)+\partial r(x^*).
knowledge_statements.title: Consensual Fixed Points Are Composite Stationary

assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable and each \(r_i\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable.
The matrix \(W\) is compatible with the network and preserves averages.
A common stepsize \(\alpha>0\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The variables \(y_i^k\) track the network-average smooth gradient while \(x_i^k\) undergo composite proximal updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the composite objective \(\frac1n\sum_i f_i(x)+r(x)\), initialize \(x_i^0\in\operatorname{dom}r\) and \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\). At iteration \(k\), compute
\[
v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha y_i^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha r}(v_i^k),
\]
followed by
\[
y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+\nabla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-\nabla f_i(x_i^k).
\]
Exchange \(x_i^{k+1}\) and \(y_i^{k+1}\), stop under a prescribed composite stationarity and consensus tolerance, and return the primal states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal primal step handles the common nonsmooth term, while a dynamic consensus recursion tracks the network-average gradient of the smooth terms.

children.title: Distributed Mirror Descent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connects local mirror-descent inequalities to aggregate suboptimality while exposing disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\), \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), and \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\). If every \(f_i\) is convex and \(G\)-Lipschitz on \(X\), then for every \(x\in X\),
\[
F(\bar x)-F(x)\le {1\over n}\sum_i\langle g_i,x_i-x\rangle+{G\over n}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate suboptimality is bounded by averaged local first-order terms plus a disagreement penalty.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex and \(G\)-Lipschitz on \(X\).
\(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), and \(x,x_i,\bar x\in X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local descent inequality once a network-generated mirror center is well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x\rangle+D_h(x,v_i^k)\},
\]
then every \(x\in X\) satisfies
\[
\alpha_k\langle g_i^k,x_i^{k+1}-x\rangle\le D_h(x,v_i^k)-D_h(x,x_i^{k+1})-D_h(x_i^{k+1},v_i^k).
\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact variational certificate for a local Bregman proximal solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\), then for every \(x\in X\),
\[
\alpha\bigl(\phi(x^+)-\phi(x)\bigr)\le D_h(x,v)-D_h(x,x^+)-D_h(x^+,v).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact Bregman proximal point satisfies the three-point inequality against every feasible comparator.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the Bregman proximal-map definition hold.
\(x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Three-Point Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman Proximal Map and Optimality Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Bregman proximal operation underlying distributed implementations; no network recursion is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha>0\), define
\[
P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\alpha\phi(x)+D_h(x,v)\},\qquad D_h(x,v)=h(x)-h(v)-\langle\nabla h(v),x-v\rangle.
\]
If the minimum is attained and the convex subdifferential sum rule applies, strong convexity of \(h\) makes the minimizer unique, and
\[
x^+=P_{\alpha\phi}^{h,X}(v)\iff0\in\alpha\partial\phi(x^+)+\nabla h(x^+)-\nabla h(v)+N_X(x^+).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman proximal point uniquely minimizes a convex function plus a Bregman distance and is characterized by a normal-cone inclusion.

\(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex.

children.title: Mirror-Geometry Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of geometry relative to feasible sets and objective structure.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and convex, and \(x^*\in\mathop{\arg\min}_{x\in X}f(x)\).
Every employed subgradient satisfies \(\lVert g\rVert_*\leq G\) with respect to the dual of the selected norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\).
The selected differentiable mirror map \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), and \(D_h(x^*,x^0)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within a candidate family of mirror geometries, the standard bound favors choices jointly controlling \(G^2D_h(x^*,x^0)/\mu\) while keeping mirror and proximal operations tractable.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a positive integer \(T\), constant stepsize \(\alpha>0\), and the standard weighted or averaged mirror-descent output, the optimization bound has the form
\[
\frac{D_h(x^*,x^0)}{\alpha T}+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2\mu}.
\]
Balancing these terms gives
\[
\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{2\mu D_h(x^*,x^0)}{G^2T}}.
\]
Thus a mirror geometry should be selected jointly with its norm to control the Bregman distance to an optimizer, the dual-norm scale of admissible subgradients, and the strong-convexity modulus. In a distributed implementation, mirror-coordinate aggregation and local mirror or proximal subproblems should also remain computationally tractable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the norm and mirror map together to reduce the product of squared dual-gradient scale and Bregman distance relative to strong convexity, while retaining tractable distributed updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Geometry Selection

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 Bregman methods p. 194

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rules out artificial improvement of the geometry-selection score by scalar rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\widetilde h=ch\) for \(c>0\), then \(D_{\widetilde h}=cD_h\) and \(\widetilde h\) is \(c\mu\)-strongly convex whenever \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. Hence
\[
{G^2D_{\widetilde h}(x^*,x^0)\over c\mu}={G^2D_h(x^*,x^0)\over\mu}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling changes Bregman distance and curvature equally, leaving the standard geometry score unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the selected norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Map Scaling Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical choices illustrating feasible-set, primal-norm, dual-norm, and Bregman-radius matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For Euclidean geometry, \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\) is one-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_2\) and \(D_h(x,y)=\tfrac12\|x-y\|_2^2\). On the simplex \(\Delta_d\), negative entropy \(h(x)=\sum_jx_j\log x_j\) is one-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_1\); for \(y\) with positive coordinates,
\[
D_h(x,y)=\sum_jx_j\log(x_j/y_j),
\]
and at \(u=\mathbf1/d\), \(\sup_{x\in\Delta_d}D_h(x,u)=\log d\). Entropic geometry therefore pairs a logarithmic simplex Bregman radius with the dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared Euclidean and negative-entropy geometries provide canonical norm-divergence pairings for Euclidean domains and probability simplices.
assumptions_latex: For entropy geometry, the second argument has strictly positive coordinates.
The convention \(0\log0=0\) is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Euclidean and Entropic Geometries

assumptions_latex: The entropy generator is \(h(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell\log x_\ell\) on the nonnegative orthant, with gradient defined on its positive interior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary points can make entropy mirror coordinates undefined, and primal averaging generally differs from averaging in mirror coordinates followed by the inverse mirror map.

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Bregman methods p. 194

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the entropy generator \(h(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell\log x_\ell\), the mirror coordinate satisfies \(\nabla h(x)=\mathbf{1}+\log x\) on the positive orthant and is not finite when a coordinate of \(x\) is zero. Consequently, an iterate or communicated center on the boundary makes a gradient-based mirror update undefined unless a suitable extension or limiting convention is specified. Moreover, because \(\nabla h\) is nonlinear, the primal average \(\sum_jw_{ij}x_j\) generally differs from the mirror-coordinate barycenter
\[
(\nabla h)^{-1}\!\left(\sum_jw_{ij}\nabla h(x_j)\right),
\]
whenever the inverse is defined. Thus replacing mirror-coordinate aggregation by ordinary primal consensus generally changes the intended Bregman geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy mirror coordinates are undefined at zero coordinates, and ordinary convex averaging generally differs from averaging in mirror coordinates and mapping back.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman-Geometry Boundaries

children.title: Distributed Successive Convex Approximation
children.top_down_role: Local-surrogate methods for nonconvex and composite network problems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity certificate using an exact aggregate-gradient correction, independent of its network implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi(x)=\sum_jf_j(x)+r(x)\) on \(X\), and define
\[
\widehat x_i(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\widetilde f_i(x;z)+\left\langle\sum_{j\ne i}\nabla f_j(z),x-z\right\rangle+r(x)\right\}.
\]
If the surrogate is differentiable, strongly convex, and first-order consistent, and the convex sum rule applies, then
\[
z=\widehat x_i(z)\iff0\in\sum_j\nabla f_j(z)+\partial r(z)+N_X(z).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact correction for the other agents' gradients, a surrogate best-response fixed point is exactly a composite stationary point.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_j\) is differentiable.
\(r\) is proper, closed, and convex; \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is differentiable, strongly convex, and first-order consistent.
A standard convex subdifferential sum qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Corrected-Surrogate Fixed-Point Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining local model used in distributed successive convex approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A surrogate \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is admissible when it is strongly convex on \(X\), its gradient is continuous in the relevant arguments, and
\[
\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(z;z)=\nabla f_i(z).
\]
Global majorization \(\widetilde f_i(x;z)\ge f_i(x)\) is an additional variant-specific condition and does not follow from first-order consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed SCA uses strongly convex local models matching the local gradient at the base point; majorization is optional and variant-specific.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex.
\(f_i\) is differentiable on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\text{ is strongly convex},\qquad\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(z;z)=\nabla f_i(z).

notation.meaning: agent i surrogate at base point z

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Descent Property of an Exact Corrected Surrogate Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local descent property of the SCA best-response direction, independent of its network implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_i(z)=\widehat x_i(z)-z\), where \(\widehat x_i(z)\) is the exact corrected surrogate best response. If \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) has \(\tau\)-strongly monotone gradient and is first-order consistent, then
\[
\left\langle\sum_j\nabla f_j(z),d_i(z)\right\rangle+r(\widehat x_i(z))-r(z)\le-\tau\|d_i(z)\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact gradient-corrected surrogate with strongly monotone model gradient produces a quantitatively descending displacement unless it is already at a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the accepted exact corrected-surrogate fixed-point certificate hold.
For fixed \(z\), \(\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(\cdot;z)\) is \(\tau\)-strongly monotone for \(\tau>0\).
\(\widehat x_i(z)\) is the exact surrogate minimizer.

The surrogate \(\widetilde f_i(\cdot;x_i^k)\) is strongly convex and first-order consistent at \(x_i^k\).
The regularizer \(r\) is proper, closed, convex, and proximable on the feasible set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration combines a uniquely solvable local convex model with network consensus and a relaxed primal update.

notation.meaning: gradient estimate for other agents' objectives

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic distributed SCA iteration with gradient tracking and convex local subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) constructs a strongly convex surrogate satisfying \(\nabla_x\widetilde f_i(x_i^k;x_i^k)=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\), maintains an estimate \(\pi_i^k\) of the other agents' aggregate gradient, and solves
\[
\widehat x_i^k=\mathop{\arg\min}_{x\in X}\left\{\widetilde f_i(x;x_i^k)+\langle\pi_i^k,x-x_i^k\rangle+r(x)\right\}.
\]
It forms \(z_i^k=x_i^k+\gamma_k(\widehat x_i^k-x_i^k)\), mixes \(z_i^k\) with neighboring values, and updates \(\pi_i^k\) through a gradient-tracking recursion. Stop at a prescribed consensus-stationarity residual or budget and return the local states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents minimize strongly convex local surrogates corrected by tracked global-gradient information, relax toward the minimizers, and mix the resulting states over the network.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Successive Convex Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for an estimated aggregate Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For derivative estimates \(\widehat H_i^k,\widehat g_i^k\), define \[\eta_i^k=\frac{\|\widehat H_i^kp_i^k+\widehat g_i^k\|}{\max\{1,\|\widehat g_i^k\|\}}.\] A small \(\eta_i^k\) certifies only the estimated linear solve; distributed optimality additionally requires small derivative-estimation error, primal disagreement, and aggregate-gradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Newton-equation residual verifies the local estimated solve but not consensus or global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The derivative estimates and direction are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Distributed Newton Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Averaging Local Newton Directions Is Generally Biased
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncommutativity boundary for naive distributed Newton averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In general, \[\frac1n\sum_iH_i^{-1}g_i\ne\left(\frac1n\sum_iH_i\right)^{-1}\left(\frac1n\sum_i g_i\right).\] For scalar data \((H_1,g_1)=(1,1)\) and \((H_2,g_2)=(3,1)\), the average local direction is \(-2/3\), whereas the aggregate Newton direction is \(-1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix inversion does not commute with averaging, so naive averaging of local Newton directions is not the aggregate Newton step.
assumptions_latex: Every local Hessian is nonsingular.
Agents compute \(p_i=-H_i^{-1}g_i\) independently.
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging Local Newton Directions Is Generally Biased

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Newton Equation in Consensus Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order equation that distributed Newton methods seek to reproduce.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), define \(\bar g(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i\nabla f_i(x)\) and \(\bar H(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i\nabla^2f_i(x)\). When \(\bar H(x)\) is nonsingular, the aggregate Newton direction satisfies \[\bar H(x)p_N(x)=-\bar g(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed Newton methods approximate the Newton equation formed from the aggregate gradient and average Hessian at a common point.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is twice differentiable at \(x\).
\(\bar H(x)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Newton Equation in Consensus Coordinates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perturbation Certificate for an Estimated Aggregate Newton Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates derivative-aggregation error from the estimated Newton-solve residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\succeq\mu I\), \(\mu>0\), \(p=-H^{-1}g\), \(\widehat H=H+E_H\), and \(\widehat g=g+e_g\). If \(\|E_H\|\le\varepsilon_H<\mu\), \(\|e_g\|\le\varepsilon_g\), and \(\|\widehat H\widehat p+\widehat g\|\le\rho\), then
\[
\|\widehat p-p\|\le\frac{\rho+\varepsilon_g+\varepsilon_H\|p\|}{\mu-\varepsilon_H}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed distributed direction is close to the aggregate Newton direction when derivative-estimation and linear-solve errors are small relative to aggregate curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(H\succeq\mu I\) for some \(\mu>0\).
\(\|\widehat H-H\|\le\varepsilon_H<\mu\).
\(\|\widehat g-g\|\le\varepsilon_g\).
\(\|\widehat H\widehat p+\widehat g\|\le\rho\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic consensus-based distributed Newton iteration for smooth unconstrained objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) uses communication and local derivatives to obtain \(g_i^k\) and \(H_i^k\) approximating \(\frac1n\sum_j\nabla f_j(x_i^k)\) and \(\frac1n\sum_j\nabla^2f_j(x_i^k)\). It solves
\[
H_i^kp_i^k=-g_i^k,
\]
forms \(z_i^k=x_i^k+\alpha_kp_i^k\), and applies the prescribed consensus or tracking update to the trial points. The stepsize or regularization is selected to maintain model stability. Stop under a consensus-Newton residual or budget and return the local states.

children.title: Distributed Hessian Tracking
children.top_down_role: Network mechanisms for estimating aggregate curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Hessian Samples Can Produce an Indefinite Local Tracker
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit boundary between the aggregate invariant and agentwise positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the scalar two-agent recursion with \(W=J\), initialize \(S^0=Q^0=(100,1)^\top\) and take \(Q^1=(1,100)^\top\). Then \(S_1^1=50.5+(1-100)=-48.5\), although every entry of \(Q^0\) and \(Q^1\) is positive. Thus dynamic Hessian tracking does not preserve agentwise positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing positive samples and adding their temporal differences can make a local Hessian tracker negative.
assumptions_latex: The scalar tracker uses \(S^{1}=JS^0+Q^1-Q^0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Hessian Samples Can Produce an Indefinite Local Tracker

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-average-consensus error dynamics for matrix-valued Hessian samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S^{k+1}=WS^k+Q^{k+1}-Q^k\), \(J=n^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), and consistently initialized aggregate components, the disagreement \(E^k=(I-J)S^k\) satisfies \[E^{k+1}=(W-J)E^k+(I-J)(Q^{k+1}-Q^k).\] If \(\|W-J\|=\sigma<1\), then \[\|E^k\|\le\sigma^k\|E^0\|+\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}\sigma^{k-1-t}\|(I-J)(Q^{t+1}-Q^t)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian-tracking disagreement is a stable consensus filter driven by changes in local Hessians.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(\|W-J\|=\sigma<1\) in a compatible norm.
Trackers and samples use a common vectorized or Frobenius-space representation.
The aggregate tracker component is initialized consistently.
knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Tracking Disagreement Recursion

assumptions_latex: Each local objective \(f_i\) is twice continuously differentiable.
The mixing matrix \(W\) preserves network averages.
Agents evaluate \(Q_i^k=\nabla^2f_i(x_i^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tracker sum equals the sum of current local Hessians, so consensus mixing can track their network average.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-average-consensus recursion for tracking network Hessian averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(S_i^0=Q_i^0=\nabla^2f_i(x_i^0)\). After producing \(x_i^{k+1}\), agent \(i\) evaluates \(Q_i^{k+1}=\nabla^2f_i(x_i^{k+1})\) and updates
\[
S_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}S_j^k+Q_i^{k+1}-Q_i^k.
\]
When \(W\) is average-preserving, summing over agents yields \(\sum_iS_i^{k+1}=\sum_iQ_i^{k+1}\). Thus \(S_i^k\) is a dynamic-consensus estimate of the aggregate Hessian. If a Newton solve requires invertibility, use a stated regularization such as \(H_i^k=S_i^k+\delta I\) with \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic consensus recursion mixes previous Hessian estimates and adds each agent's Hessian change, preserving the current aggregate curvature exactly in the network sum.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Hessian Tracking

However, no source confirms the matrix-valued tracking recursion, its stochasticity convention, or the conditions under which local trackers approximate the average stably.

children.title: Distributed Quasi-Newton Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition preserving a positive-definite local BFGS model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct BFGS update preserves positive definiteness when \(B_i^k\succ0\) and \((s_i^k)^\top y_i^k>0\). Because network and tracking errors can violate this inequality, a distributed implementation must damp, skip, or regularize pairs failing a declared bound such as \((s_i^k)^\top y_i^k\ge c\|s_i^k\|^2\), \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed BFGS needs an explicit curvature safeguard because observed secant curvature can become nonpositive.
assumptions_latex: A BFGS-type direct update is applied only to accepted pairs.
\(B_i^k\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Secant Curvature Safeguard

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local and tracked secant pairs used by decentralized curvature models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agent \(i\) forms \(s_i^k=x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k\) and \(y_i^k=q_i^{k+1}-q_i^k\), where \(q_i^k\) is either a local gradient or a tracked aggregate-gradient estimate. A direct model imposes \(B_i^{k+1}s_i^k=y_i^k\); an inverse model imposes \(H_i^{k+1}y_i^k=s_i^k\). Local and tracked choices generally approximate different curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed secant pairs may use local or tracked gradients, and the choice determines the curvature being approximated.
assumptions_latex: Successive displacements and the selected first-order estimates are available locally.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility boundary between curvature-matrix averaging and agent-specific secant data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each \(B_j\succ0\) satisfies \(B_js_j=y_j\) and \(\widetilde B_i=\sum_jw_{ij}B_j\) with convex weights, then \(\widetilde B_i\succ0\), but generally \(\widetilde B_is_i\ne y_i\) because neighboring matrices correspond to different secant pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging positive-definite quasi-Newton matrices preserves positivity but usually destroys each agent's current secant equation.

Every \(B_j\) is symmetric positive definite and satisfies its own secant equation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative consensus, gradient-tracking, and damped BFGS scheme on a fixed undirected network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each agent initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), \(y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0)\), and \(B_i^0\succ0\). Given a symmetric doubly stochastic mixing matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\), perform \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha_k(B_i^k)^{-1}y_i^k,\qquad y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k).\] Set \(s_i^k=x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k\), choose a damped gradient difference \(z_i^k\) satisfying \((s_i^k)^	op z_i^k>0\), and apply \[B_i^{k+1}=B_i^k- rac{B_i^ks_i^k(s_i^k)^	op B_i^k}{(s_i^k)^	op B_i^ks_i^k}+ rac{z_i^k(z_i^k)^	op}{(s_i^k)^	op z_i^k}.\] Stop when consensus and tracked-gradient residuals meet prescribed tolerances; output the network average.

children.title: Curvature-Heterogeneity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Variation of local curvature across network participants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Positive Curvature Does Not Imply Local Positive Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar cancellation example for heterogeneous Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar quadratic Hessians \(H_1=-1\) and \(H_2=3\), \(\bar H=1>0\), although \(H_1<0\). Thus aggregate strong convexity does not make every local Newton system positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly convex aggregate can contain a locally concave objective.
assumptions_latex: Two scalar quadratic local objectives are used.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Positive Curvature Does Not Imply Local Positive Curvature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise disagreement of local Hessians from aggregate curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_i(x)=\nabla^2f_i(x)\) and \(\bar H(x)=n^{-1}\sum_iH_i(x)\). Define \(\delta_H=\sup_{x\in\mathcal D}\max_i\|H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\|_2\). When \(\bar H(x)\succ0\), a relative regime satisfies \(\|H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\|_2\le\eta\lambda_{\min}(\bar H(x))\). If \(\eta<1\), then \((1-\eta)\bar H(x)\preceq H_i(x)\preceq(1+\eta)\bar H(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian heterogeneity measures local curvature deviation absolutely or relative to the aggregate strong-curvature scale.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is twice differentiable on \(\mathcal D\).
The relative regime assumes \(\bar H(x)\succ0\) throughout \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute and Relative Hessian Heterogeneity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian Heterogeneity Controls Local Newton-Direction Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation relation for local and aggregate Newton systems sharing a gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar H\bar p=-g\), \(H_ip_i=-g\), and both Hessians are positive definite, then \[p_i-\bar p=H_i^{-1}(\bar H-H_i)\bar p,\qquad \|p_i-\bar p\|\le\|H_i^{-1}\|\,\|H_i-\bar H\|\,\|\bar p\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Newton-direction error scales with Hessian heterogeneity and inverse local curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(H_i\) and \(\bar H\) are symmetric positive definite.
Both systems use the same gradient vector \(g\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Heterogeneity Controls Local Newton-Direction Error
Curvature-Heterogeneity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative regimes for disagreement among local Hessians relative to aggregate curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For twice differentiable local objectives \(f_i:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\), define \(H_i(x)=\nabla^2f_i(x)\) and \(\bar H(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nH_i(x)\). The curvature-heterogeneity level is \[\delta_H=\sup_{x\in\mathcal D}\max_i\lVert H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\rVert_2.\] The regime is homogeneous when \(\delta_H=0\), uniformly heterogeneous when \(0<\delta_H<\infty\), and relatively heterogeneous with parameter \(\eta\) when \[\lVert H_i(x)-\bar H(x)\rVert_2\leq\eta\,\lambda_{\min}(\bar H(x))\quad\text{for all }i,x.\] Relative heterogeneity with \(\eta<1\) implies uniformly comparable positive-definite local and aggregate curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature heterogeneity is measured by the worst local Hessian deviation from the network-average Hessian, either absolutely or relative to aggregate strong curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and every \(f_i\) is twice differentiable on \(\mathcal D\).
For the relative regime, \(\bar H(x)\succ0\) throughout \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\eta<1\), then \((1-\eta)\bar H(x)\preceq H_i(x)\preceq(1+\eta)\bar H(x)\) for every \(i\) and \(x\in\mathcal D\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute and relative heterogeneity definitions and the stated Loewner comparison are mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source is supplied for these exact named regimes or normalization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for convex distributed problems with consensus and affine coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(Bx=0\) and \(Ax=b\), define \[r_{\rm con}=Bx,\quad r_{\rm cpl}=Ax-b,\quad r_{\rm stat}=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\nabla f(x)+B^\top\lambda+A^\top\nu+N_X(x)\right).\] Under convexity and a constraint qualification, vanishing residuals certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus, coupling-feasibility, and stationarity residuals jointly certify a convex constrained distributed solution.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable.
\(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
A constraint qualification guarantees multiplier existence and KKT sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\rm con}=r_{\rm cpl}=r_{\rm stat}=0\Longrightarrow x\text{ is globally optimal}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Heterogeneous Local Feasibility Does Not Survive Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for reporting a network average as a feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(x_i\in X_i\) it does not follow that \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\in\bigcap_iX_i\). For \(X_1=\{0\}\), \(X_2=\{2\}\), \(x_1=0\), and \(x_2=2\), the average is \(1\), which belongs to neither local set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging points feasible for different local sets need not produce a feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Agents may have distinct feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneous Local Feasibility Does Not Survive Averaging

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local, Common, and Coupled Constraint Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical partition of constraint structures requiring different distributed handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Distributed constraints separate into local Cartesian constraints \(x_i\in X_i\), a common constraint \(x_i\in X\), and coupled constraints such as \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\). Projections onto \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\) separate agentwise, whereas projection onto a genuine coupling set is generally nonseparable and requires coordination, auxiliary variables, or multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agentwise projections handle Cartesian constraints, while genuine coupling constraints require coordinated or dualized handling.
assumptions_latex: Projection statements use nonempty closed convex sets and a separable positive-definite metric.

notation.meaning: agent-local block of a coupling operator

knowledge_statements.title: Local, Common, and Coupled Constraint Classes
Distributed Constraint-Handling Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected consensus-gradient method for a common closed convex constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given agents minimizing \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\) over a nonempty closed convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), initialize \(x_i^0\in X\). For a doubly stochastic network matrix \(W^k\), each agent computes \[v_i^k=\sum_jw_{ij}^kx_j^k,\qquad x_i^{k+1}=P_X\!\left(v_i^k-\alpha_k g_i^k\right),\quad g_i^k\in\partial f_i(v_i^k).\] Because projection is local, every iterate remains feasible. Stop when \(\max_{(i,j)}\lVert x_i^k-x_j^k\rVert\) and a projected subgradient residual are below prescribed tolerances; return any agent iterate or their average, which also belongs to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents average neighboring decisions, take local subgradient steps, and project onto the common convex constraint set, thereby preserving feasibility at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex on \(X\) and has bounded subgradients there.
The mixing sequence is doubly stochastic and uniformly connected.
The steps satisfy \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^k\in X\) for all \(i,k\), and the stated standard conditions support consensus toward a minimizer when one exists.

children.title: Distributed Nonconvex Network Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative stationarity certificate using an exact tracker-sum invariant and disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If every \(\nabla f_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz and \(\sum_i y_i=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\), then with \(\bar y=n^{-1}\sum_i y_i\) and \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\),
\[
\|\nabla F(\bar x)\|\le\|\bar y\|+{1\over n}\sum_iL_i\|x_i-\bar x\|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregate gradient is bounded by the average tracker plus a Lipschitz-weighted disagreement term.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) has an \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient.
\(\sum_i y_i=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Tracker–Consensus Stationarity Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation boundary for generic nonconvex network outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If every agent has \(f_i(x)=(x^2-1)^2\), then \(F(x)=(x^2-1)^2\). The consensual state \(x_i=0\) satisfies \(\nabla F(0)=0\), but
\[
F(0)=1>0=F(1)=F(-1),
\]
and \(0\) is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero aggregate gradient can identify a local maximum rather than a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: All agents use \(f_i(x)=(x^2-1)^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consensus First-Order Stationarity for Smooth Nonconvex Networks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic target of smooth unconstrained distributed nonconvex methods, independent of a particular recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), a product state is consensual first-order stationary when
\[
x_1=\cdots=x_n=x^*,\qquad\nabla F(x^*)=0.
\]
It is \((\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_s)\)-approximately stationary when
\[
{1\over n}\sum_i\|x_i-\bar x\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad\|\nabla F(\bar x)\|\le\varepsilon_s.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generic smooth nonconvex target is consensus plus a small aggregate gradient, not global optimality.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus First-Order Stationarity for Smooth Nonconvex Networks
Distributed Nonconvex Network Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient-tracking descent for smooth, possibly nonconvex finite-sum objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), possibly nonconvex. Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0)\). With a symmetric doubly stochastic matrix \(W\) and stepsize \(\alpha>0\), iterate \[x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}x_j^k-\alpha y_i^k,\qquad y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}y_j^k+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k).\] Stop when both \(\max_i\lVert x_i^k- ar x^kVert\) and \(\lVert n^{-1}\sum_i y_i^kVert\) are below chosen tolerances. Output \( ar x^k=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i^k\); the target certificate is first-order stationarity, not global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient tracking combines neighbor averaging with local nonconvex gradients; its natural output is a consensus point with a small global gradient, not a global optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) has an \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(F\) is bounded below.
The fixed communication graph is connected and \(W\) is symmetric and doubly stochastic.
The constant stepsize is chosen below the method's network- and smoothness-dependent stability threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping conditions certify approximate consensus and approximate first-order stationarity of \(F\) at the averaged iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Coordinated Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central multiplier update with parallel solutions of separable Lagrangian subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\). Initialize a master multiplier \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R^m\). At iteration \(k\), broadcast \(\lambda^k\); each agent returns \[x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda^k)^\top A_ix_i\bigr).\] The master forms \(r^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b\) and updates \[\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_kr^k),\] where \(\Lambda=\mathbb R^m\) for equality constraints. Stop when \(\lVert r^k\rVert\) and the dual improvement are below tolerances; output the multiplier and a primal recovery derived from the local solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master broadcasts prices, agents solve separable Lagrangian subproblems in parallel, and the master updates prices using the aggregate coupling residual.
assumptions_latex: Every local subproblem attains its minimum.
The coupling constraint is affine and separable by agent.
For convergence, strong duality holds and the projected dual-subgradient steps obey a valid diminishing-stepsize rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^k\) is a supergradient of the concave dual function at \(\lambda^k\), so the master update is projected dual ascent.
