children.title: Communication-Interval Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior across short, moderate, or extended intervals between aggregations.

assumptions_latex: Let \(K_r\in\mathbb N_{+}\) be the number of local updates between synchronization events \(r\) and \(r+1\).
Let \(T_R=\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}K_r\) denote the number of local updates completed through \(R\) communication intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Communication schedules are classified as unit, bounded, or growing according to the sequence \((K_r)\), with communication count determined by \(R(T)=\max\{R:T_R\le T\}\).

notation.meaning: Local-update length of communication interval r
Cumulative local updates after R intervals
Completed communication intervals by local-update budget T

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule classification only; no convergence rate is asserted.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Communication Aspects of Parallel and Distributed Systems p. 27
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A communication-interval schedule is a sequence \((K_r)_{r\ge0}\) of positive integers. It is unit-communication when \(K_r=1\) for all \(r\), bounded-period when
\[
1<\sup_rK_r<\infty,
\]
and growing-period when \(\sup_rK_r=
\infty\). Define
\[
T_R=
\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}K_r,
\qquad
R(T)=
\max\{R:T_R\le T\}.
\]
Then \(R(T)\) is the number of completed averaging events within \(T\) local updates, making the computation--communication tradeoff explicit without itself imposing convergence conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication regimes are determined by whether the number of local updates between averaging events is one, uniformly bounded, or unbounded over time.
knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Interval Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Communication Aspects of Parallel and Distributed Systems p. 27
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

children.title: Local-Update Drift Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where accumulated local movement undermines global progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Update Drift Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic within-round boundary under uniformly bounded local directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every client \(i\) and every \(k\in\{0,\ldots,K\}\), the within-round drift satisfies \[\lVert x_i^k-x\rVert\le \eta kG.\] In particular, \[\max_{0\le k\le K}\lVert x_i^k-x\rVert\le \eta KG.\] This dependence on \(\eta\), \(K\), and \(G\) is sharp under the bounded-direction assumption alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uniformly bounded local update directions, a client is at most eta times k times G from the synchronized model after k steps, and its maximum within-round drift is at most eta times K times G. This bound is sharp without further assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Each client objective \(F_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
During one round, client \(i\) starts from \(x\) and performs \(K\) updates \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k-\eta g_i^k\), with \(x_i^0=x\).
The local directions satisfy \(\lVert g_i^k\rVert\le G\) for \(0\le k<K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_i^k-x\rVert\le \eta kG\) for every \(0\le k\le K\); hence the worst-case within-round drift is at most \(\eta KG\).

notation.meaning: Client model after k local updates in the current round.
Local stepsize and number of local updates.
Uniform bound on local update directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SCAFFOLD-style cancellation at a synchronized model, with residual drift away from that model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i f_i\), where \(p_i>0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and fix a synchronization point \(x\). Suppose the client and server controls satisfy \(c_i-c=
abla f_i(x)-
abla F(x)\). The corrected client direction at a local point \(y\) is
\[d_i(y)=
abla f_i(y)-c_i+c=
abla F(x)+
abla f_i(y)-
abla f_i(x).\]
Consequently, \(d_i(x)=
abla F(x)\) for every client. If each \(f_i\) has an \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient, then
\[\lVert d_i(y)-
abla F(x)Vert\le L_i\lVert y-xVert,\]
so cancellation is exact at synchronization and degrades only with local displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper client and server controls remove inter-client gradient disagreement exactly at synchronization; during local motion, the remaining error is bounded by gradient smoothness times displacement.

\(c_i-c=\nabla f_i(x)-\nabla F(x)\).

children.title: Normalized Client Updates
children.top_down_role: Update scaling that compensates for unequal local magnitudes or work.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Client Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization converts variable-length local model displacements into average local directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(t\), client \(i\) initializes \(y_{i,0}=x_t\) and performs \(\tau_i\ge1\) steps
\[y_{i,k+1}=y_{i,k}-\eta_{i,k}g_{i,k},\qquad 0\le k<\tau_i.\]
Its displacement is \(\Delta_i=x_t-y_{i,\tau_i}=\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}\eta_{i,k}g_{i,k}\). Given a positive normalizer \(a_i=\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}\eta_{i,k}\), the normalized client update is
\[u_i=\frac{\Delta_i}{a_i}=\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}\frac{\eta_{i,k}}{a_i}g_{i,k}.\]
Thus \(u_i\) is a step-size-weighted average direction; for constant \(\eta_{i,k}=\eta_i\), it equals \(\tau_i^{-1}\sum_k g_{i,k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide each client displacement by its accumulated local step size. The result is an average direction whose scale does not grow mechanically with local step count.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_i\ge1\) and \(\eta_{i,k}>0\).
All local iterates and directions lie in the same Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_i=\Delta_i/a_i\) is a convex combination of the local directions \(g_{i,k}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalization follows directly from telescoping local descent steps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalization definition follows correctly from the local-step recursion and matches the leaf, but no inspectable source supports its placement as a federated update-calibration concept.

children.title: Local-Work Reweighting

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Work Reweighting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reweighting separates intended client importance from heterogeneous amounts of local work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let client \(i\) have target weight \(p_i\), local length \(\tau_i\), constant step size \(\eta_i>0\), and displacement \(\Delta_i=\eta_i\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}g_{i,k}\). The target-weighted average of client-average directions has the representation
\[\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\left(\frac1{\tau_i}\sum_{k=0}^{\tau_i-1}g_{i,k}\right)=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{p_i}{\eta_i\tau_i}\Delta_i.\]
Hence a server step \(x^+=x-\gamma\sum_i p_i\Delta_i/(\eta_i\tau_i)\) removes the purely multiplicative influence of unequal local step counts and step sizes while retaining the prescribed client weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weight each displacement inversely by its local steps and step size, then apply the intended client weight. This prevents extra local work from automatically increasing client influence.
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) uses a constant local step size \(\eta_i\) during the round.

notation.meaning: intended objective weight of client i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact algebraic reweighting of telescoped local updates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed representation is exact for constant client-specific step sizes, and representation is an acceptable role here. A source is required for the claimed federated local-work calibration interpretation.

children.title: Sampling-Probability Correction
children.top_down_role: Update weighting adjusted for unequal client selection probabilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Probability Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Horvitz–Thompson correction for randomly participating clients with known inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be a random participating set with inclusion probabilities \(q_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\). For fixed client vectors \(u_i\) and target weights \(p_i\), define
\[\widehat u=\sum_{i\in S}\frac{p_i}{q_i}u_i.\]
Then
\[\mathbb E[\widehat u]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i.\]
This identity requires only the marginal inclusion probabilities; independence of client selections is unnecessary. If some \(q_i=0\) while \(p_i u_i\ne0\), no estimator based solely on observed participating updates can recover that missing term without additional structural information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide each participating client’s target-weighted update by its inclusion probability. The aggregate is unbiased, provided every relevant client can be selected.

\(q_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\) whenever \(p_i u_i\ne0\).

children.title: Client-Weight Calibration
children.top_down_role: Alignment of aggregation influence with the intended federated objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Weight Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient coefficient calibration for an unbiased target-weighted client aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a random client set with \(q_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\), and let the server form \(\widehat u=\sum_{i\in S}a_i u_i\), where \(a_i\) is deterministic conditional on the sampling design. For arbitrary fixed vectors \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\), the calibration condition
\[\mathbb E[\widehat u]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i\]
holds if and only if
\[q_i a_i=p_i\qquad\text{for every }i.\]
Thus \(a_i=p_i/q_i\). Under full participation, \(q_i=1\), this reduces to the prescribed objective weights \(a_i=p_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate matches the intended client-weighted target for every possible update exactly when each server coefficient times its inclusion probability equals the target client weight.
assumptions_latex: \(q_i>0\) for every client with \(p_i\ne0\).
The coefficients \(a_i\) do not depend on the realized value of \(u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\sum_{i\in S}a_i u_i]=\sum_i p_i u_i\) for all \((u_i)\) if and only if \(a_i=p_i/q_i\).

notation.meaning: server coefficient applied when client i participates

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coefficient matching follows from linearity and arbitrary test vectors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For fixed coefficients and arbitrary client vectors, the stated coefficient-matching condition is correct and condition is the appropriate content kind. No source is supplied for this federated calibration characterization.

children.title: Federated Convergence under Client Heterogeneity
children.top_down_role: Convergence families separating sampling, drift, and objective mismatch.

knowledge_statements.title: Federated Convergence under Client Heterogeneity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonconvex smooth descent bound separating estimator bias, sampling variance, and local stochastic variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-smooth and bounded below by \(F_*\). Consider \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta g_t\), where \(0<\eta\le(4L)^{-1}\), \(\mathbb E[g_t\mid x_t]=\nabla F(x_t)+b_t\), and \(\mathbb E[\lVert g_t-\mathbb E[g_t\mid x_t]\rVert^2\mid x_t]\le V_t^{\mathrm{samp}}+V_t^{\mathrm{loc}}\). Then
\[\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\lVert\nabla F(x_t)\rVert^2\le\frac{4(F(x_0)-F_*)}{\eta T}+4\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\lVert b_t\rVert^2+2L\eta\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E\bigl[V_t^{\mathrm{samp}}+V_t^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr].\]
Here \(b_t\) can collect objective mismatch and uncorrected client drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average stationarity error is bounded by optimization progress, squared heterogeneity-induced bias, client-sampling variance, and local stochastic variance.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and bounded below by \(F_*\).
The displayed conditional mean and variance bounds hold for \(g_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed average-gradient bound separates persistent bias from sampling and local stochastic variance.

notation.meaning: conditional estimator bias from drift or objective mismatch

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic biased stochastic-gradient descent template specialized to federated error components
constants and hypotheses require source verification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A theorem fits this convergence container, but the exact constants and sufficient hypotheses in the biased stochastic-gradient bound require authoritative verification. The identification of the bias and variance terms with federated heterogeneity components is also unsourced.

children.title: Federated Client Selection

children.title: Uniform Client Sampling
children.top_down_role: Symmetric random client selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-size uniform sampling without replacement from a finite client population.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\) clients and an integer \(m\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), uniform client sampling without replacement draws a subset \(S\) uniformly from all \(m\)-element subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Thus
\[\mathbb P(S=A)=\binom{n}{m}^{-1}\quad\text{for every }A\text{ with }|A|=m,\qquad \mathbb P(i\in S)=\frac mn.\]
For fixed vectors \(u_i\), the sample mean \(\widehat u=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}u_i\) satisfies
\[\mathbb E[\widehat u]=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n u_i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose every fixed-size client subset with equal probability. Each client has inclusion probability m/n, and the sample mean estimates the population mean without bias.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le m\le n\).
The vectors \(u_i\) are fixed, or conditionally fixed, before sampling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(i\in S)=m/n\) and \(\mathbb E[m^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}u_i]=n^{-1}\sum_i u_i\).

children.title: Importance-Weighted Client Sampling
children.top_down_role: Client selection guided by optimization-relevant importance scores.

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Weighted Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-client importance sampling with unbiased weighting and second-moment-optimal probabilities, including the zero-update degenerate case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_i\ge0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\), and let \(u_i\in\mathbb R^d\) be fixed. Let \(q_i\ge0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=1\), with \(q_i>0\) whenever \(p_i\lVert u_i\rVert>0\). Draw \(I\) with probabilities \(q_i\) and define
\[G=\frac{p_I}{q_I}u_I.\]
Then
\[\mathbb E[G]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i,\qquad \mathbb E\lVert G\rVert^2=\sum_{i:q_i>0}\frac{p_i^2\lVert u_i\rVert^2}{q_i}.\]
Set \(Z=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\lVert u_j\rVert\). If \(Z>0\), the second moment is minimized by
\[q_i=\frac{p_i\lVert u_i\rVert}{Z}\]
for indices with \(p_i\lVert u_i\rVert>0\), with zero probability assigned to the remaining indices. If \(Z=0\), the target and second moment are zero, and every sampling distribution is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-probability weighting preserves the target mean. When at least one weighted update is nonzero, sampling in proportion to weighted update norms minimizes the second moment; when all weighted updates vanish, every sampling distribution is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i\in\mathbb R^d\), \(p_i\ge0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\).
\(q_i\ge0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=1\), and \(q_i>0\) whenever \(p_i\lVert u_i\rVert>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G]=\sum_i p_i u_i\); if \(Z>0\), the minimum second moment is attained by \(q_i\propto p_i\lVert u_i\rVert\), while if \(Z=0\), every sampling distribution is optimal.

children.title: Data-Aware Client Sampling
children.top_down_role: Client selection guided by dataset composition or statistical coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Aware Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Client sampling driven by positive data-derived scores, with inverse-probability aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given target weights \(p_i\), client vectors \(u_i\), and positive data scores \(s_i=s(D_i)>0\), set
\[q_i=\frac{s_i}{\sum_{j=1}^n s_j}.\]
Draw one client \(I\sim q\), obtain its update \(u_I\), and output \(G=(p_I/q_I)u_I\). For a minibatch of \(m\) independent draws, output the average of the \(m\) corrected vectors. Stop after the prescribed number of communication rounds and return the current server iterate. Conditional on the scores and client updates,
\[\mathbb E[G]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_i.\]
Thus data statistics alter sampling frequency without changing the target aggregate when correction is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert positive client-data scores into sampling probabilities, sample clients accordingly, and inverse-weight their updates so data-aware selection does not change the intended aggregate.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i=s(D_i)>0\) for every client with \(p_i u_i\ne0\).
Scores and updates are conditionally fixed when sampling occurs.

notation.meaning: client i's local dataset or data summary

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: score-proportional sampling combined with inverse-probability correction
specific federated data-aware sampling source required

children.title: Loss-Aware Client Sampling
children.top_down_role: Client selection guided by current loss or related progress signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss-Aware Client Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive sampling based on reported client losses, with explicit exploration and bias correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(t\), let \(\ell_{i,t}\ge0\) be a client loss estimate available before selection, choose \(\varepsilon>0\), and define
\[q_{i,t}=\frac{p_i(\ell_{i,t}+\varepsilon)}{\sum_{j=1}^n p_j(\ell_{j,t}+\varepsilon)}.\]
Draw \(I_t\sim q_t\), obtain update \(u_{I_t,t}\), and use \(G_t=(p_{I_t}/q_{I_t,t})u_{I_t,t}\) in the server update. Repeat until the round budget or stopping criterion is met. Conditional on the preselection history and fixed client updates,
\[\mathbb E[G_t]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_{i,t}.\]
The exploration constant ensures positive probability for every positively weighted client.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample high-loss clients more often while retaining exploration, then inverse-weight selected updates. Conditional unbiasedness is preserved when losses are fixed before selection.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\), \(\ell_{i,t}\ge0\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
The loss scores are measurable before round-\(t\) client selection.

notation.meaning: preselection loss score for client i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: adaptive score sampling with predictable probabilities and inverse weighting
specific loss-aware federated sampling source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact loss-based probability rule requires a source. Moreover, the conditional-unbiasedness conclusion requires the candidate updates to be measurable with respect to the preselection history, which is stated informally but omitted from the formal assumptions.

children.title: Sampling-Bias Correction
children.top_down_role: Control of objective distortion introduced by nonuniform selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Bias Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional-expectation certificate for adaptive client-selection bias correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_t\) contain all information available before round-\(t\) selection, and let \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P(I_t=i\mid\mathcal F_t)>0\). For target weights \(p_i\) and \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable candidate updates \(u_{i,t}\), define
\[G_t=\frac{p_{I_t}}{q_{I_t,t}}u_{I_t,t}.\]
The verifiable identities \(q_{i,t}>0\) and
\[\sum_{i=1}^n q_{i,t}\frac{p_i}{q_{i,t}}u_{i,t}=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i u_{i,t}\]
certify that \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=\sum_i p_i u_{i,t}\). The certificate fails if probabilities are computed after observing selection-dependent update information or if a required \(q_{i,t}\) is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logged preselection probabilities and inverse weights certify conditional unbiasedness. The certificate is invalid when relevant clients have zero probability or probabilities depend on post-selection information.
assumptions_latex: \(q_{i,t}\) and \(u_{i,t}\) are \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable.
\(q_{i,t}>0\) whenever \(p_i u_{i,t}\ne0\).

children.title: Resource-Aware Client Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection adapted to availability and systems resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Aware Client Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible client selection using availability, resource budgets, and optional inverse-probability correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(t\), client \(i\) reports an availability indicator \(a_{i,t}\in\{0,1\}\), resource cost \(c_{i,t}\ge0\), and utility score \(s_{i,t}\). Given budget \(B_t\), choose a distribution \(\pi_t\) supported on subsets
\[\mathcal C_t=\left\{S:S\subseteq\{i:a_{i,t}=1\},\ \sum_{i\in S}c_{i,t}\le B_t\right\}\]
that maximizes \(\mathbb E_{S\sim\pi_t}[\sum_{i\in S}s_{i,t}]\), possibly subject to inclusion floors. Draw \(S_t\sim\pi_t\), execute those clients, and aggregate using \(p_i/q_{i,t}\), where \(q_{i,t}=\mathbb P_{\pi_t}(i\in S_t)\), when an unbiased target aggregate is required. Return the server iterate after the stopping budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select only available clients whose total resource cost fits the round budget, optimize expected utility, and use inclusion-probability correction when preserving target weights is required.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{i,t}\), \(c_{i,t}\), and \(s_{i,t}\) are known before selection.
\(\mathcal C_t\ne\varnothing\).
For unbiased correction, \(q_{i,t}>0\) whenever \(p_i u_{i,t}\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\in\mathcal C_t\) almost surely, and inverse-inclusion weighting preserves \(\sum_i p_i u_{i,t}\) when all required probabilities are positive.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constrained subset selection combined with inclusion-probability correction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate content kind, but the proposed utility-maximizing selection model has no supporting resource-aware federated source. Optional inclusion floors and the corrected aggregation operation are also not specified fully enough to identify one exact algorithm.

children.title: Client-Selection Bias Correction
children.top_down_role: Correction families for nonuniform or availability-biased participation.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Selection Bias Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-probability correction for unequal client inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the target aggregate be \(g=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i g_i\), where \(p_i\ge 0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and \(g_i\in\mathbb R^d\). Let \(S\) be a random client subset with inclusion probabilities \(\pi_i=\Pr(i\in S)>0\). The Horvitz--Thompson aggregate is \[\widehat g=\sum_{i\in S}\frac{p_i}{\pi_i}g_i.\] Regardless of dependence among client-selection indicators, \(\mathbb E[\widehat g]=g\). Thus inverse-inclusion weighting removes first-order selection bias; its variance may nevertheless be large when some \(\pi_i\) are small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighting each selected client by the reciprocal of its inclusion probability yields an unbiased target aggregate, although rare clients can cause high variance.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\) is integrable for every client \(i\).
\(\pi_i>0\) whenever \(p_i>0\).

notation.meaning: marginal inclusion probability of client i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-inclusion weighting claim is mathematically correct and fits the correction topic, but no inspectable citation supports the estimator or variance warning.

children.title: Regularized Federated Personalization

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Federated Personalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically coupled client models with a learned global reference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For client losses \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), weights \(p_i\ge 0\) satisfying \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and \(\lambda>0\), regularized federated personalization solves \[\min_{w,\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_m\in\mathbb R^d}\ \sum_{i=1}^m p_i\left(f_i(\theta_i)+\frac{\lambda}{2}\lVert\theta_i-w\rVert_2^2\right).\] Here \(w\) is a shared reference and \(\theta_i\) is client \(i\)'s personalized model. The coupling penalizes deviation from \(w\) without requiring the client models to coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each client minimizes its own loss while a quadratic penalty keeps its personalized model near a jointly learned reference model.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\), \(p_i\ge0\), and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
Each \(f_i\) is proper and bounded below.
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed coupled objective defines the personalized client models and shared reference.

children.title: Multi-Task Federated Optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Task Federated Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint learning of related, nonidentical client tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=[w_1,\ldots,w_m]\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) collect client-specific task parameters. Multi-task federated optimization is the coupled problem \[\min_{W\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}}\ \sum_{i=1}^m p_i f_i(w_i)+\lambda R(W),\] where \(p_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(R\) encodes relatedness across client tasks, for example through graph, covariance, or low-rank structure. Unlike a single-global-model formulation, the decision variables \(w_i\) may differ; federation occurs through the nonseparable regularizer \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct client models are learned jointly, with a coupling regularizer encoding how the client tasks are related.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper.
\(R:\mathbb R^{d\times m}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is a specified coupling functional.
\(p_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A solution \(W^\star\) jointly determines related but potentially distinct client models \(w_i^\star\).

children.title: Clustered Federated Optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Clustered Federated Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Latent client partition with one optimized model per cluster.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(K\in\mathbb N\), client losses \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and weights \(p_i\ge0\), clustered federated optimization solves \[\min_{w_1,\ldots,w_K\in\mathbb R^d,\ z\in\{1,\ldots,K\}^m}\ \sum_{i=1}^m p_i f_i(w_{z_i}).\] The latent label \(z_i\) assigns client \(i\) to a cluster, and all clients assigned label \(k\) use cluster model \(w_k\). Optional balancing or separation constraints may restrict \(z\), but they are not part of the basic formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clients are assigned to latent groups, and one model per group is optimized against the losses of its assigned clients.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge1\) is fixed.
\(p_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
Each \(f_i\) is proper and bounded below.

children.title: Shared-Representation Personalization

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Representation Personalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common feature map with client-specific prediction heads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let client \(i\) have distribution \(P_i\) on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\). A shared-representation personalized model consists of a common map \(\phi:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z\) and client-specific heads \(h_i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal A\), chosen by \[\min_{\phi\in\Phi,\ h_i\in\mathcal H_i}\ \sum_{i=1}^m p_i\,\mathbb E_{(X,Y)\sim P_i}\!\left[\ell\bigl(h_i(\phi(X)),Y\bigr)\right].\] The representation parameters are federated across clients, while each head is optimized for its client's prediction task.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clients share a learned feature representation but retain separate prediction heads adapted to their own data distributions.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
The displayed losses are measurable and have finite expectations.
\(\Phi\) and \(\mathcal H_i\) are specified hypothesis classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The personalized predictor for client \(i\) is \(h_i^\star\circ\phi^\star\).

children.title: Secure Aggregation Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Secure Aggregation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate-only server interface for federated update computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a participating set \(S\), let client \(i\) submit \(u_i\in G\), where \((G,+)\) is an abelian group. A secure-aggregation-compatible optimization round requires the server's update to have the form \[w^{+}=\Psi\!\left(w,S,\sum_{i\in S}u_i,\xi\right),\] where \(\xi\) is public or server-side randomness. The secure aggregation interface reveals the sum and declared public metadata but no individual \(u_i\). Consequently, any server rule requiring inspection, ordering, clipping, or reweighting of individual plaintext updates must be performed before aggregation or replaced by an aggregate-computable rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible server update depends on client messages only through their secure sum and public metadata, never through individual plaintext updates.
assumptions_latex: Client messages lie in a common abelian group \(G\).
The secure protocol correctly returns \(\sum_{i\in S}u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization update is computable from aggregate-only visibility exactly when it admits the displayed interface.

notation.meaning: encoded update submitted by client i
server update rule using aggregate-visible inputs

children.title: Differential Privacy Interface for Federated Optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Differential Privacy Interface for Federated Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript privacy under record- or client-level adjacency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\sim D'\) denote either record-level adjacency or client-level adjacency, fixed before analysis. A randomized federated mechanism \(M\), whose output includes the observable training transcript and final model, is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differentially private if, for every adjacent \(D,D'\) and measurable event \(E\), \[\Pr(M(D)\in E)\le e^{\varepsilon}\Pr(M(D')\in E)+\delta.\] A federated optimizer interfaces with differential privacy by bounding each adjacent unit's contribution, randomizing the communicated or aggregated updates, and accounting for privacy across all rounds under the chosen adjacency relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complete observable training mechanism must satisfy differential privacy for a fixed record- or client-level adjacency relation across all communication rounds.
assumptions_latex: The adjacency relation \(\sim\) is specified as record-level or client-level.
\(M\) includes every data-dependent output visible to the adversary.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(0\le\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) satisfies the displayed \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-privacy inequality for all adjacent datasets and measurable events.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The differential-privacy definition correctly fixes one adjacency relation and covers the observable transcript, but no privacy source is cited.

children.title: Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Interface
children.top_down_role: Optimization compatibility with adversary-resistant aggregation.

knowledge_statements.title: Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic robust-aggregation contract under bounded honest dispersion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\) contain an unknown honest index set \(H\) with \(|H|\ge n-b\), and define \(\bar v_H=|H|^{-1}\sum_{i\in H}v_i\). An aggregation rule \(A:(\mathbb R^d)^n\to\mathbb R^d\) satisfies a \((b,c)\)-Byzantine-robust interface on radius \(\rho\) if \[\max_{i\in H}\lVert v_i-\bar v_H\rVert_2\le\rho\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\lVert A(v_1,\ldots,v_n)-\bar v_H\rVert_2\le c\rho\] for every choice of the remaining at most \(b\) vectors. An optimizer using \(A\) must establish honest-update dispersion compatible with this contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If honest updates concentrate around their mean, the aggregator must remain close to that mean despite any allowed Byzantine vectors.
assumptions_latex: Honest vectors satisfy the displayed radius bound.
Byzantine vectors are otherwise arbitrary.

children.title: Privacy–Utility–Robustness–Communication Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Joint performance frontiers induced by privacy, robustness, and communication mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Privacy–Utility–Robustness–Communication Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto representation of jointly attainable federated performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a data model, adversary model, privacy adjacency relation, and training horizon. For every admissible federated mechanism \(M\), let \(q(M)=(\varepsilon(M),\delta(M),\mathcal E(M),\beta(M),B(M))\), representing privacy loss, expected excess risk, tolerated Byzantine fraction, and communicated bits. The attainable region is \[\mathcal R=\{q(M):M\text{ is admissible}\}.\] With smaller \(\varepsilon,\delta,\mathcal E,B\) and larger \(\beta\) preferred, the joint tradeoff frontier is the set of nondominated points of \(\mathcal R\). Any claimed numerical frontier is meaningful only under the fixed models and resource conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint tradeoff is the Pareto frontier of achievable privacy, error, Byzantine tolerance, and communication cost under fixed models and conventions.
assumptions_latex: The data, adversary, privacy, and communication models are fixed.
All metrics are evaluated over the same training horizon.
The admissible mechanism class is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The privacy--utility--robustness--communication frontier equals the nondominated subset of \(\mathcal R\).

notation.meaning: expected excess risk of mechanism M

children.title: Quantization Methods
children.top_down_role: Reduced-precision encoding of states, gradients, or trackers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased scalar quantization between adjacent grid points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in[k\Delta,(k+1)\Delta]\), output \(k\Delta\) with probability \(((k+1)\Delta-x)/\Delta\) and \((k+1)\Delta\) otherwise. Then \(\mathbb E[Q_\Delta(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[(Q_\Delta(x)-x)^2\mid x]\le\Delta^2/4\). Coordinatewise application gives \(\mathbb E[\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x]\le d\Delta^2/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly selecting an adjacent grid point removes rounding bias while retaining bounded mean-square error.
assumptions_latex: Each coordinate lies between two finite adjacent grid points.

notation.meaning: index of the lower adjacent grid point

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise deterministic reduced-precision encoding on an unclipped grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For spacing \(\Delta>0\), define \(Q_\Delta(x)_j=\Delta\operatorname{round}(x_j/\Delta)\). If no coordinate is clipped, then \(|Q_\Delta(x)_j-x_j|\le\Delta/2\), and therefore \(\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2\le\Delta\sqrt d/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding coordinates to a uniform grid gives a deterministic absolute-error bound when no value is clipped.
assumptions_latex: Ties use a fixed rounding convention.
No coordinate is saturated or clipped.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Scalar Quantization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform absolute-error guarantees outside a finite reconstruction range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a scalar quantizer has reconstruction set \(\mathcal C\subset[-M,M]\), then for every \(|x|>M\), \(|Q(x)-x|\ge |x|-M\). Consequently, no such finite-range quantizer has a finite global input-independent absolute-error bound without a scaling or overflow mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite reconstruction range produces unbounded absolute error on unbounded inputs unless scaling or overflow handling is added.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\in\mathcal C\subset[-M,M]\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Range Saturation Boundary
Quantization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased finite-message compression of communicated vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), choose a randomized encoder-decoder quantizer \(Q\) whose possibly variable-length message has a finite encoding for each realization and whose decoded output satisfies \(\mathbb E[Q(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert Q(x)-x\rVert_2^2\mid x]\le\omega\lVert x\rVert_2^2\). A sending client samples and encodes \(Q(x)\), and the receiver decodes the resulting vector \(q\). In a first-order round with stepsize \(\eta_t>0\), the receiver may update \[w_{t+1}=w_t-\eta_t q_t.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is encoded by a randomized finite-message quantizer whose decoded value is unbiased and has controlled mean-square distortion.
assumptions_latex: The encoder and decoder share the quantization and coding scheme.
The quantizer satisfies the displayed conditional unbiasedness and distortion bounds.
The transmitted vector has finite second moment and \(\omega\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decoded message satisfies \(\mathbb E[Q(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert Q(x)-x\rVert_2^2\mid x]\le\omega\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).

notation.meaning: randomized quantization operator including encoding and decoding

children.title: Sparsification Methods
children.top_down_role: Coordinate selection and sparse update communication.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic retention of the largest-magnitude coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x\in\mathbb R^d and 1\le k\le d, let J_k(x) contain indices of k largest values of |x_j|, using a fixed tie rule, and define (T_k(x))_j=x_j\mathbf 1_{\{j\in J_k(x)\}}. Then \|x-T_k(x)\|_2=\min_{\|z\|_0\le k}\|x-z\|_2 and \|x-T_k(x)\|_2^2\le(1-k/d)\|x\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Top-k keeps the largest coordinates, is a best Euclidean k-sparse approximation, and satisfies the sharp uniform contraction bound.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^d.
1\le k\le d.
Ties are resolved by a fixed rule.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero coordinates of z

knowledge_statements.title: Top-k Sparsification
Sparsification Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random coordinate transmission with unbiased rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(1\le k\le d\), sample uniformly a subset \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) of size \(k\), and define \[Q_k(x)_j=\begin{cases}(d/k)x_j,&j\in J,\\0,&j\notin J.\end{cases}\] Transmit \(J\) and the selected values; the receiver reconstructs \(Q_k(x)\). Then \(\mathbb E[Q_k(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert Q_k(x)-x\rVert_2^2\mid x]=(d/k-1)\lVert x\rVert_2^2\). The reconstructed sparse vector replaces the dense message in the enclosing optimization update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly sample k coordinates, rescale them by d/k, and transmit their indices and values to obtain an unbiased sparse message.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(1\le k\le d\).
The subset \(J\) is sampled uniformly without replacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_k(x)\) is unbiased and has conditional mean-square error \((d/k-1)\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).

children.title: Low-Rank Sketch Compression Family
children.top_down_role: Structured low-dimensional representations of updates.

children.title: Low-Rank Update Compression
children.top_down_role: Compression through structured low-rank representations of distributed updates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Error and Exactness of Truncated-Rank Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-norm error and the lossless boundary for truncated-SVD update compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with ordered singular values and rank-\(r\) truncation \(X_r\), \(\|X-X_r\|_2=\sigma_{r+1}(X)\), where \(\sigma_{p+1}(X)=0\) and \(p=\min\{m,n\}\). Consequently, \(X_r=X\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral error is the first discarded singular value, and truncated-rank compression is lossless exactly when the update rank fits the budget.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le r\le p=\min\{m,n\}\).
Singular values are ordered nonincreasingly.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Error and Exactness of Truncated-Rank Compression
Low-Rank Update Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated-SVD encoding of matrix-shaped model updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a matrix update \(X\in\mathbb R^{a\times b}\) and rank budget \(1\le r\le\min\{a,b\}\), compute a singular value decomposition \(X=U\Sigma V^\top\). Retain the leading factors and form \[C_r(X)=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^\top.\] Transmit \(U_r,\Sigma_r,V_r\), or equivalent factored data, and let the receiver reconstruct \(C_r(X)\) for the optimization update. The reconstruction is a best rank-at-most-\(r\) approximation in Frobenius norm and satisfies \(\lVert X-C_r(X)\rVert_F^2=\sum_{j>r}\sigma_j(X)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a truncated SVD, transmit its leading factors, and reconstruct the best rank-r approximation to the matrix update.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb R^{a\times b}\).
\(1\le r\le\min\{a,b\}\).
Singular values are ordered nonincreasingly.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The truncated-SVD algorithm and approximation statement fit the exact low-rank update-compression leaf, but the Eckart–Young characterization and error identity lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Random Sketch Compression
children.top_down_role: Compression through randomized low-dimensional sketches.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided randomized range finding for a matrix-valued update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), draw \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times\ell}\), form \(Y=X\Omega\), and let \(Q\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\). Reconstruct \(\widehat X=QQ^\top X\), equivalently from transmitted factors \((Q,Q^\top X)\). For every realization, \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le\ell\) and \(X-\widehat X=(I-QQ^\top)X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random test matrix samples the update's range, and projection onto that range gives a rank-limited reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le\ell\le\min\{m,n\}\).
The factor-transmission convention is known to encoder and decoder.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis for the sampled range

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Range-Sketch Compression
Random Sketch Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-randomness linear sketching of a matrix-valued distributed update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an update matrix \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), a sketch size \(s<mn\), and a shared distribution over linear maps, sample \(S:\mathbb{R}^{mn}\to\mathbb{R}^{s}\). The sender transmits \(y=S\operatorname{vec}(X)\). The receiver, knowing \(S\), outputs \(\widehat X=D_S(y)\), where \(D_S:\mathbb{R}^{s}\to\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is a prescribed decoder, possibly constrained to return a matrix of rank at most \(r\). The compressed message is \((S,y)\) when randomness is not shared and only \(y\) when it is shared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random linear map reduces a matrix update to a short vector; a receiver using the same map reconstructs an optionally rank-limited approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(1\le s<mn\).
\(S\) is known to both encoder and decoder.

notation.meaning: decoder associated with the realized sketch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the Random Sketch Compression leaf and the encoder-decoder notation is coherent, but the record contains no citation. A specific source locator is required for this compression model, including the shared-randomness convention and optional rank-constrained decoding.

children.title: Rank-Budget Regimes
children.top_down_role: Communication and approximation behavior across rank constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum rank meeting a Frobenius reconstruction tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E_r^2=\sum_{j=r+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2\) and \(r_\varepsilon=\min\{r\in\{0,\ldots,p\}:E_r\le\varepsilon\}\). Then \(E_{r+1}\le E_r\), and \(r_\varepsilon\) is the smallest truncated-SVD rank meeting tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Under any message-cost function nondecreasing in \(r\), it has minimum cost among tolerance-feasible truncated-SVD ranks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarded singular-value energy decreases with rank, so the first rank meeting the tolerance is cheapest under any monotone rank-cost convention.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The declared message cost is nondecreasing in rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\varepsilon=\min\{r:E_r\le\varepsilon\}\) minimizes the declared monotone cost over tolerance-feasible ranks.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Rank–Accuracy Frontier
Rank-Budget Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank selection through approximation error and communication budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have singular values \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p\ge0\), where \(p=\min\{m,n\}\). For tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and scalar budget \(B\), rank \(r\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) is feasible when \(r(m+n+1)\le B\) and \(\sum_{j=r+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2\le\varepsilon^2\). Under factor transmission, these inequalities define the joint communication–accuracy regime; the truncated singular-value decomposition attains the stated Frobenius error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank is feasible when its factor representation fits the communication budget and the discarded singular-value energy meets the error tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
Rank-\(r\) transmission sends two factors and \(r\) singular values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|X-X_r\|_F^2=\sum_{j=r+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2\le\varepsilon^2\) and the representation uses at most \(B\) scalars.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the Rank-Budget Regimes leaf, and the truncated-SVD error formula is standard. However, no citation supports the particular factor-transmission cost r(m+n+1), whose validity depends on the chosen representation and counting convention.

children.title: Sketch Reconstruction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits arising from inadequate sketch dimension or unstable reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-recovery boundary for a structured matrix class under a fixed linear sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(\mathcal S(X)=S\operatorname{vec}(X)\). A decoder satisfying \(D(\mathcal S(X))=X\) for every \(X\in\mathcal X\) exists if and only if \(\ker S\cap\operatorname{vec}(\mathcal X-\mathcal X)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured class is exactly recoverable precisely when no nonzero difference of two admissible matrices lies in the sketch nullspace.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is linear.
The decoder may be defined arbitrarily outside \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Injectivity Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary conditioning for Lipschitz recovery on a structured class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}=\inf_{X\ne X',\,X,X'\in\mathcal X}\|S\operatorname{vec}(X-X')\|_2/\|X-X'\|_F\). If an \(L\)-Lipschitz decoder on \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\) exactly recovers every \(X\in\mathcal X\), then \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}\ge1/L\). Hence \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}=0\) precludes uniformly Lipschitz-stable exact recovery, even if the sketch is injective on \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Injectivity alone does not ensure stable reconstruction; admissible differences must have uniformly positive sketch gain.
assumptions_latex: \(D(S\operatorname{vec}(X))=X\) for every \(X\in\mathcal X\).
\(D\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Reconstruction Gain Boundary
Sketch Reconstruction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic obstruction to uniform exact recovery from undersized linear sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^{mn}\to\mathbb{R}^{s}\) be linear with \(s<mn\). Then \(\ker S\neq\{0\}\), so some nonzero \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) satisfies \(S\operatorname{vec}(H)=0\). Consequently, for every \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the distinct matrices \(X\) and \(X+H\) produce the same sketch. No decoder using only this sketch can recover every matrix exactly; exact recovery therefore requires additional structural restrictions or at least \(mn\) independent measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undersized linear sketch has a nontrivial nullspace, so unrestricted matrices cannot be reconstructed exactly without further structure.
assumptions_latex: \(S:\mathbb{R}^{mn}\to\mathbb{R}^{s}\) is linear.

notation.meaning: nonzero matrix in the sketch nullspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the nullspace obstruction is mathematically precise for unrestricted matrices and a fixed linear sketch with s<mn. The record nevertheless has no inspectable citation for the reconstruction boundary.

children.title: Reference-State Predictive Compression Family
children.top_down_role: Encoding innovations relative to stored or predicted states.

children.title: Difference Encoding
children.top_down_role: Encoding updates relative to a stored prior state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between consecutive-state variation and the encoded innovation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the shared reference is the preceding state, \(h_t=x_{t-1}\), then \(\Delta_t=x_t-x_{t-1}\). Hence \(\|\Delta_t\|=\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|\) and \(\sum_{t=1}^T\|\Delta_t\|=\sum_{t=1}^T\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|\). A bound on one-step state variation is therefore exactly a bound on the compressor input magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the previous state as reference, the encoded value is exactly the state increment, so its magnitude is governed by temporal variation.
assumptions_latex: Sender and receiver share the exact preceding state as reference.
knowledge_statements.title: Variation-Controlled Difference Magnitude
Difference Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding an update relative to a shared reference state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current state \(x_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and a reference \(h_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\) known to sender and receiver, define the innovation \(\Delta_t=x_t-h_t\). The sender transmits \(q_t=Q(\Delta_t)\), and the receiver reconstructs \(\widehat x_t=h_t+q_t\). Hence the reconstruction error is exactly \(\widehat x_t-x_t=Q(\Delta_t)-\Delta_t\); compression accuracy depends on the innovation rather than the magnitude of the full state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sender compresses the difference from a shared reference, and the receiver adds the decoded difference back to that reference.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,h_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
Sender and receiver use the same \(h_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits Difference Encoding, and the reconstruction-error identity is internally consistent. No cited source with a specific locator supports this reference-state encoding formulation.

children.title: Predictive State Compression
children.top_down_role: Encoding residual information relative to a predicted state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact distortion transfer when a state is compressed relative to its prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r_t=x_t-h_t, q_t=Q_t(r_t), and \widehat x_t=h_t+q_t. Then \widehat x_t-x_t=Q_t(r_t)-r_t. If \mathbb E[\|Q_t(r)-r\|_2^2\mid r]\le\omega_t\|r\|_2^2 for every r, then \mathbb E[\|\widehat x_t-x_t\|_2^2\mid x_t,h_t]\le\omega_t\|x_t-h_t\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction error is exactly compression error on the prediction residual, so a smaller residual proportionally reduces distortion under a relative-error compressor.
assumptions_latex: x_t,h_t\in\mathbb R^d.
Q_t satisfies the stated conditional relative mean-square error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Reconstruction Error Identity
Predictive State Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential compression using a synchronized state predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a common predictor \(h_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At round \(t\), the sender forms \(r_t=x_t-h_t\), transmits \(q_t=Q_t(r_t)\), and both parties reconstruct \(\widehat x_t=h_t+q_t\). They then apply the same deterministic prediction rule \(h_{t+1}=P_t(h_t,\widehat x_t)\). The procedure outputs \(\widehat x_t\) each round and may stop under any externally specified optimization stopping criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each round compresses prediction residuals, reconstructs the state, and updates an identical predictor at both endpoints.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,h_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
Both endpoints use identical maps \(Q_t\) and \(P_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Predictive State Compression, and the sequential encoder, decoder, and predictor updates are clearly specified. The record has no source for this particular synchronized predictive-compression procedure.

children.title: Reference-State Synchronization
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of compatible encoding references across communicating agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-State Synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant ensuring identical predictive references at sender and receiver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let sender and receiver references be \(h_t^{\mathrm{s}},h_t^{\mathrm{r}}\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Synchronization holds if \(h_0^{\mathrm{s}}=h_0^{\mathrm{r}}\), both endpoints receive the same message \(q_t\), and both update by one deterministic map \(U_t\): \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm{s}}=U_t(h_t^{\mathrm{s}},q_t)\) and \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm{r}}=U_t(h_t^{\mathrm{r}},q_t)\). These conditions preserve equality of the references at every round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal initialization, identical received messages, and identical deterministic updates keep sender and receiver references synchronized.
assumptions_latex: \(h_0^{\mathrm{s}}=h_0^{\mathrm{r}}\).
Both endpoints apply the same deterministic \(U_t\) to the same \(q_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Reference-State Synchronization, and the equality invariant follows from the stated common initialization, messages, and deterministic updates. No citation with a specific locator is supplied for this synchronization condition.

children.title: Prediction-Mismatch Failures
children.top_down_role: Compression degradation caused by inaccurate or inconsistent predictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar counterexample showing geometric amplification of unsynchronized predictor states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm s}=a h_t^{\mathrm s}\) and \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm r}=a h_t^{\mathrm r}\), with \(|a|>1\) and no resynchronization. If \(h_0^{\mathrm r}-h_0^{\mathrm s}=\delta\ne0\), then \(h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}=a^t\delta\). Thus an initial reference discrepancy grows geometrically even without additional quantization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstable predictor can geometrically amplify a small initial disagreement between encoder and decoder references.
assumptions_latex: No synchronization correction is applied.
knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Predictor Amplifies Reference Mismatch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step reference-desynchronization bound for a common predictor map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sender and receiver apply the same \(L\)-Lipschitz predictor \(P\), then \(\|P(h_t^{\mathrm r})-P(h_t^{\mathrm s})\|\le L\|h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}\|\). Therefore \(L\le1\) guarantees nonexpansion in the absence of other errors, whereas an assumption with \(L>1\) permits geometric amplification and supplies no nonexpansion guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexpansive predictor prevents one-step mismatch growth; an expansive Lipschitz bound permits geometric amplification unless synchronization corrects it.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
Sender and receiver apply the same predictor.
No synchronization correction or additional mismatch input is applied in this step.
review_flags: Corrected the builder's overly strong claim that nonexpansion is possible only when the declared Lipschitz constant is at most one.
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Mismatch Propagation
Prediction-Mismatch Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error caused by divergent encoder and decoder predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the sender encode \(q_t=Q(x_t-h_t^{\mathrm{s}})\) while the receiver reconstructs \(\widehat x_t=h_t^{\mathrm{r}}+q_t\). Then \(\widehat x_t-x_t=Q(r_t)-r_t+(h_t^{\mathrm{r}}-h_t^{\mathrm{s}})\), where \(r_t=x_t-h_t^{\mathrm{s}}\). Even with exact residual transmission \(Q(r)=r\), the reconstruction error equals the predictor mismatch. Thus an uncontrolled reference discrepancy cannot be removed by improving residual quantization alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mismatch between sender and receiver predictors appears directly in reconstruction error, even when the residual itself is transmitted exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,h_t^{\mathrm{s}},h_t^{\mathrm{r}}\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
The receiver adds the message to \(h_t^{\mathrm{r}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Prediction-Mismatch Failures, and the error decomposition is algebraically consistent. The record lacks an inspectable source supporting the predictive-compression failure interpretation.

children.title: Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Compressor classes supporting different stability and convergence mechanisms.

children.title: Unbiased Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Random compression preserving updates in expectation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent second-moment representation for an unbiased compressor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \mathbb E[Q(x)]=x, then \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2=\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2-\|x\|_2^2. Therefore \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2 is equivalent to \mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|_2^2. Either form implies Q(0)=0 almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unbiased compressor, a relative variance bound is equivalent to an output second-moment bound.
assumptions_latex: Q(x) has finite second moment for every x.
\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x for every x.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Output Second-Moment Form
Unbiased Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard second-moment class for unbiased randomized vector compressors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized map \(Q:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) is an unbiased compressor with variance parameter \(\omega\ge0\) if, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), its internal randomness satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[Q(x)]=x\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2]\le\omega\|x\|_2^2\). Expectations are conditional on the supplied input when that input is random.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The compressed vector equals its input in expectation, while its mean-square error is bounded proportionally to the input norm.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\) has a finite second moment for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, and the unbiasedness and relative second-moment bounds form a standard compressor class with explicit quantification. No authoritative definition or section locator is cited.

children.title: Contractive Biased Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Biased compression controlled through contraction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequences of mean-square compressor contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Q satisfies \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2 for 0<\delta\le1, then Q(0)=0 almost surely and \bigl(\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le\bigl(1+\sqrt{1-\delta}\bigr)\|x\|_2. For deterministic Q, both conclusions hold pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every contractive compressor fixes zero and has a uniformly controlled output second moment.
assumptions_latex: Q(x) has finite second moment for every x.
0<\delta\le1.
The mean-square contraction inequality holds for every input.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Preservation and Output-Moment Bound
Contractive Biased Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-square contraction class allowing biased randomized compressors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A possibly biased randomized map \(Q:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) is contractive with parameter \(\delta\in(0,1]\) if, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), \(\mathbb{E}[\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2]\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\). No equality such as \(\mathbb{E}[Q(x)]=x\) is required. For a deterministic compressor, the expectation is omitted and the inequality holds pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A biased compressor is controlled when its mean-square distortion contracts the squared input norm by a fixed positive factor.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\) has a finite second moment for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
\(0<\delta\le1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, and the mean-square contraction inequality correctly allows biased randomized compressors while identifying the deterministic specialization. No source with a specific locator is provided for this convention.

children.title: Absolute-Error Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Compression with magnitude-independent error control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute Error Does Not Imply Relative Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of magnitude-independent and relative compressor conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix b\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\} and define Q_b(x)=x+b. Then \|Q_b(x)-x\|_2^2=\|b\|_2^2 for every x, so Q_b has absolute-error parameter \sigma=\|b\|_2. No finite \omega satisfies \|Q_b(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2 for every x, because the right side vanishes at x=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed additive offset has uniformly bounded absolute error but cannot satisfy any global relative-error condition.
assumptions_latex: b\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_b\text{ satisfies a uniform absolute-error bound but no finite global relative-error bound.}
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Error Does Not Imply Relative Accuracy
Absolute-Error Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform magnitude-independent mean-square compression error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized map \(Q:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) has absolute-error parameter \(\sigma\ge0\) if, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), \(\mathbb{E}[\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2]\le\sigma^2\). The bound is independent of \(\|x\|_2\). For deterministic \(Q\), the expectation is removed and the same inequality must hold pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The compressor has uniformly bounded mean-square error, independent of the magnitude of the vector being compressed.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\) has a finite second moment for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
\(\sigma\ge0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Absolute-Error Compressor Conditions, and the uniform magnitude-independent mean-square bound is stated consistently. The record has no citation establishing this compressor class or its parameter convention.

children.title: Deterministic Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Fixed lossy encodings without randomization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between deterministic lossy compression and compressor-randomness unbiasedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d be deterministic. Expectation over the compressor's internal randomness gives \mathbb E[Q(x)]=Q(x). Hence \mathbb E[Q(x)]=x for every x if and only if Q(x)=x for every x. Thus a nonidentity deterministic lossy compressor cannot be unbiased in this sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without internal randomness, unbiasedness forces the compressor to be the identity.
assumptions_latex: Q has no internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Unbiasedness Is Trivial
Deterministic Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise distortion class for nonrandom lossy vector maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic compressor is a fixed map \(Q:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) with no internal randomness. Given \(\alpha\ge0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), it satisfies a mixed distortion condition if \(\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\alpha\|x\|_2^2+\beta^2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\). The cases \(\beta=0\) and \(\alpha=0\) respectively give relative and absolute pointwise error control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed compressor obeys a pointwise bound combining relative distortion and an absolute error floor, with no expectation involved.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) is fixed and nonrandom.
\(\alpha,\beta\ge0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Deterministic Compressor Conditions, and all variables and pointwise quantifiers are explicit. The mixed relative-plus-absolute distortion class is convention-dependent and is not supported by any cited source.

children.title: Compression Error Compensation
children.top_down_role: Memory and correction mechanisms controlling persistent compression error.

children.title: Error Feedback
children.top_down_role: Residual accumulation and reinjection across communication rounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual storage cannot compensate for a compressor that never transmits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q(v)=0 for every v, e_0=0, and g_t=g\ne0. Then q_t=0 and e_{t+1}=e_t+g=(t+1)g. If the optimizer moves only through q_t, its iterate remains fixed while the residual diverges linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero compressor stores every missing update but never releases it, so the method stagnates and its residual diverges.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\equiv0\).
The optimizer moves only through transmitted vectors.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncontractive Zero-Compressor Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary of the usual unweighted cumulative cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since q_t=g_t+e_t-e_{t+1}, arbitrary finite scalar stepsizes satisfy \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_tq_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_tg_t+\eta_0e_0+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}(\eta_t-\eta_{t-1})e_t-\eta_{T-1}e_T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With varying stepsizes, feedback cancellation includes stepsize-difference terms and is not only a terminal-residual identity.
assumptions_latex: The scalar stepsizes are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Stepsize Weighted Feedback Identity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Bound for a Contractive Compressor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of error-feedback memory under relative compression error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For p_t=g_t+e_t, q_t=Q(p_t), and e_{t+1}=p_t-q_t, suppose \|Q(v)-v\|\le\delta\|v\| for all v, with 0\le\delta<1. Then \[\|e_{t+1}\|\le\delta^{t+1}\|e_0\|+\delta\sum_{s=0}^t\delta^{t-s}\|g_s\|.\] If \|g_t\|\le G, then \[\sup_t\|e_t\|\le\|e_0\|+\frac{\delta G}{1-\delta}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive compressor bounds the feedback residual by a geometric convolution of past update magnitudes.
assumptions_latex: The standard error-feedback residual recursion is used.
\(\|Q(v)-v\|\le\delta\|v\|\) with \(\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Bound for a Contractive Compressor
Error Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual accumulation and reinjection for compressed distributed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(e_0=0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(t\), for an update \(g_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\), form \(p_t=g_t+e_t\), transmit \(q_t=Q(p_t)\), and set \(e_{t+1}=p_t-q_t\). Apply the communicated update through \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tq_t\), and stop according to the underlying optimization criterion. For every \(T\ge1\), the residual recursion gives \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}q_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}g_t+e_0-e_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compression error is stored, added to the next update, and therefore appears only as a terminal residual in cumulative communication.
assumptions_latex: \(g_t,e_t,x_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
The encoder and optimizer use the same transmitted vector \(q_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Error Feedback, and the residual recursion and telescoping cumulative identity are internally consistent. No source with a specific algorithm, section, theorem, or page locator is supplied for this error-feedback formulation.

children.title: Error-Compensated Consensus
children.top_down_role: Compression correction applied to network averaging states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sum-conservation condition for consensus corrections driven by reconstructed messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\gamma((W-I_n)\otimes I_d)h^{k+1}\) with \(\gamma\ne0\), the identity \((\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^{k+1}=(\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^k\) holds for every \(h^{k+1}\) if and only if \(\mathbf 1^\top W=\mathbf 1^\top\). Thus \(W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\) alone does not ensure preservation of the arithmetic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error compensation does not itself preserve the network average; the mixing matrix must preserve sums, and row stochasticity alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
\(\gamma\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Average-Preservation Boundary for Compensated Consensus
Error-Compensated Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual feedback corrects deterministic or randomized compression errors in synchronous consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each agent hold a state \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\), a communicated estimate \(h_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\), and a residual \(r_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\), with \(r_i^0=0\). At round \(k\), agent \(i\) forms \(u_i^k=x_i^k-h_i^k+r_i^k\), transmits \(q_i^k=Q(u_i^k)\), and updates \(r_i^{k+1}=u_i^k-q_i^k\) and \(h_i^{k+1}=h_i^k+q_i^k\). For a mixing matrix \(W=(w_{ij})\), perform \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k+\gamma\sum_j w_{ij}(h_j^{k+1}-h_i^{k+1})\). Stop under a prescribed consensus criterion and output the terminal states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents retain each compression discrepancy and add it to the next transmitted innovation, preventing discarded information from being permanently lost during consensus.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is compatible with the communication graph and satisfies \(W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\).
The compressor \(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is available at every agent.
The stepsize \(\gamma>0\) is prescribed.
review_flags: Exact literature source for this error-compensated consensus variant is absent from the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the precise residual/reconstruction recursion is a literature-specific error-feedback consensus variant. No citation supports this recursion or the mixing assumptions needed for its intended consensus behavior.

children.title: Compressed Gradient Tracking
children.top_down_role: Compression and correction of primal and tracking variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression of primal and tracker innovations with average-preserving corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let W be doubly stochastic. Agents maintain X^k,Y^k and sender-receiver-consistent reconstructions \widehat X^k,\widehat Y^k. They transmit \[Q_x(X^k-\widehat X^k),\qquad Q_y(Y^k-\widehat Y^k),\] add these messages to the corresponding reconstructions, and update \[X^{k+1}=X^k+(W-I)\widehat X^{k+1}-\alpha Y^k,\] \[Y^{k+1}=Y^k+(W-I)\widehat Y^{k+1}+
abla F(X^{k+1})-
abla F(X^k),\] with Y^0=
abla F(X^0).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents incrementally reconstruct compressed primal and tracker innovations and apply average-preserving corrections in both recursions.
assumptions_latex: W is doubly stochastic and graph compatible.
Local objectives are differentiable.
Sender and receivers initialize and update each reconstruction consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration compresses both primal and gradient-tracker communication while retaining uncompressed local states.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the preceding recursion, \mathbf1^	op(W-I)=0 gives \[\mathbf1^	op Y^{k+1}=\mathbf1^	op Y^k+\mathbf1^	op(

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average-preserving correction keeps the sum of trackers equal to the sum of current local gradients despite compressed tracker messages.
assumptions_latex: The preceding tracker recursion is used.
\(\mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top\).
The tracker is initialized with the correct aggregate gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Tracker-Sum Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori consistency and stationarity test for incrementally reconstructed compressed gradient tracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J=I_n-\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), let \(X,Y\) be the stacked primal and tracker states, and let \(\widehat X,\widehat Y\) be their communicated reconstructions. Define
\[r_{\rm cmp}^2=\|JX\|_F^2+\left\|\frac1n\mathbf1^\top\nabla F(X)\right\|_2^2+\|JY\|_F^2+\left\|\mathbf1^\top\bigl(Y-\nabla F(X)\bigr)\right\|_2^2+\|X-\widehat X\|_F^2+\|Y-\widehat Y\|_F^2.\]
Then \(r_{\rm cmp}=0\) exactly certifies primal consensus, zero aggregate gradient, tracker consensus, the tracker-sum identity, and exact primal and tracker reconstruction. For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\), primal consensus and the zero aggregate-gradient term certify stationarity of \(f\) at the common primal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero composite residual certifies primal consensus, aggregate stationarity, tracker consensus and mass consistency, and exact reconstruction of both communicated states.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
All stacked states and reconstructions are evaluated at the same logical iteration.
The aggregate objective is \(f=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\) for the stationarity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\rm cmp}=0\Longrightarrow X=\mathbf1x^\top,\quad \nabla f(x)=0,\quad JY=0,\quad \mathbf1^\top Y=\mathbf1^\top\nabla F(X),\quad X=\widehat X,\quad Y=\widehat Y.

notation.meaning: Communicated reconstructions of primal and tracker states.

review_flags: Revised from the builder proposal to include the tracker-sum defect; tracker consensus alone does not certify consistency with the aggregate gradient.
Zero residual certifies the displayed terminal conditions but does not establish that a recursion reaches them.
Evaluating this global residual may require a separate aggregation operation.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Compressed-Tracking Residual Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compressor-quality boundary for primal-and-tracker reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two scalar agents, let f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2, f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x+1)^2, X^0=(0,0)^{\mathsf T}, Y^0=(-1,1)^{\mathsf T}, and let Q_x=Q_y\equiv0 with zero reconstructions. In the accepted incrementally reconstructed recursion, for 0<\alpha<2, Y^{k+1}=(1-\alpha)Y^k and X^k=\bigl(1-(1-\alpha)^k\bigr)(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}. Hence Y^k\to0 while X^k\to(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressor transmitting no information can make the trackers vanish while agents converge to distinct local minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The accepted incrementally reconstructed recursion is used.
Q_x=Q_y\equiv0.
0<\alpha<2.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Information Compression Destroys Consensus
Compressed Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous gradient tracking with compressed, error-corrected primal and tracker innovations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Agent \(i\) initializes \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\), \(y_i^0=
abla f_i(x_i^0)\), reconstructions \(\hat x_i^0,\hat y_i^0\), and residuals \(r_{x,i}^0=r_{y,i}^0=0\). At round \(k\), it transmits \(q_{x,i}^k=Q_x(x_i^k-\hat x_i^k+r_{x,i}^k)\) and \(q_{y,i}^k=Q_y(y_i^k-\hat y_i^k+r_{y,i}^k)\), updates each reconstruction by adding its message, and sets each new residual equal to the corresponding compressor input minus message. With mixing matrix \(W\), update \(x_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}\hat x_j^{k+1}-\alpha y_i^k\) and \(y_i^{k+1}=\sum_jw_{ij}\hat y_j^{k+1}+
abla f_i(x_i^{k+1})-
abla f_i(x_i^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents compress innovations of both primal and gradient-tracking variables, retain both compression residuals, and mix reconstructed values before the next optimization step.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
\(W\) is a prescribed mixing matrix compatible with the network.
The stepsize \(\alpha>0\) and compressors \(Q_x,Q_y\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output after stopping is \((x_i^K)_{i=1}^n\), while \((y_i^K)_{i=1}^n\) supplies the terminal tracked-gradient states.
review_flags: The precise compressed gradient-tracking recursion requires a dedicated source not present in the supplied hints.
Convergence hypotheses and compressor class are intentionally not asserted.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but compressed gradient-tracking methods use materially different reconstruction, correction, and mixing recursions. A dedicated source is required to establish that this exact primal/tracker update is a valid named variant.
