children.title: Multi-Round Consensus
children.top_down_role: Multiple communication rounds allocated within each optimization epoch.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Round Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Each outer iteration applies several mixing rounds before the optimization update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a mixing matrix, let \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\), and let \(Z^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) stack the agents' vectors at outer iteration \(k\). Choose an integer \(s_k\geq1\), initialize \(Z^{k,0}=Z^k\), and compute \(Z^{k,\ell+1}=WZ^{k,\ell}\) for \(\ell=0,\ldots,s_k-1\). Supply \(\widetilde Z^k=Z^{k,s_k}=W^{s_k}Z^k\) to the prescribed outer optimization update. Stop when the outer method's criterion is met; the communication cost through iteration \(K\) is \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}s_k\) mixing rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer optimization step is preceded by a chosen number of repeated neighbor-averaging rounds, yielding the effective mixing operator W raised to that number.
assumptions_latex: \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\).
In the specified matrix norm, there is a \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \(\|(I-J)WZ\|\leq\rho\|(I-J)Z\|\) for every \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\).
Each integer \(s_k\geq1\) is selected before its inner loop.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Action of Multiple Consensus Rounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenmode representation for symmetric average-preserving mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) be doubly stochastic with eigenpairs \((\lambda_i,u_i)\), \(\lambda_1=1\), and \(u_1=\mathbf1/\sqrt n\). If \(Z=JZ+\sum_{i=2}^n u_i a_i^{\mathsf T}\), then \[W^sZ=JZ+\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^s u_i a_i^{\mathsf T},\qquad \|(I-J)W^s\|_2=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i|^s.\] Repetition converges to exact averaging exactly when \(\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i|<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated symmetric mixing preserves the average and raises each disagreement eigenvalue to the number of rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\) is doubly stochastic.
The consensus eigenvector is \(\mathbf1/\sqrt n\).

children.title: Inexact Consensus
children.top_down_role: Optimization performed with deliberately incomplete agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite inner communication is modeled by a bounded deviation from exact network averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stacked states \(Z^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\), define the exact averaging projector \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\). A consensus output \(\widetilde Z^k\) is \(\varepsilon_k\)-inexact, in a specified matrix norm, when \(J\widetilde Z^k=JZ^k\) and \(\|(I-J)\widetilde Z^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\). More generally, if the inner operation need not preserve the average, require \(\|\widetilde Z^k-JZ^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\). The nonnegative sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\) is part of the outer algorithm's accuracy specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact consensus returns states within a prescribed tolerance of exact averaging, optionally with exact preservation of the original network average.
assumptions_latex: All agent states have the same dimension \(d\).
A matrix norm and nonnegative tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inner consensus error at outer iteration \(k\) is bounded by \(\varepsilon_k\) under the selected formulation.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal decomposition distinguishing average drift from residual disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\), \[\widetilde Z-JZ=J(\widetilde Z-Z)+(I-J)\widetilde Z.\] Under the Frobenius norm these terms are orthogonal, so \[\|\widetilde Z-JZ\|_F^2=\|J(\widetilde Z-Z)\|_F^2+\|(I-J)\widetilde Z\|_F^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact-consensus error consists of average drift plus residual disagreement; disagreement alone is insufficient when the operation changes the average.
assumptions_latex: \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\).
The squared identity uses the Frobenius norm.

children.title: Inner-Consensus Budgeting
children.top_down_role: Allocation of communication effort to inner consensus work.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Consensus Budgeting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus rounds are selected to meet prescribed outer-iteration error tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one mixing round contracts disagreement by \(\rho\in(0,1)\): \(\|(I-J)WZ\|\leq\rho\|(I-J)Z\|\). If the pre-consensus disagreement at outer iteration \(k\) is bounded by \(D_k\), then any integer \(s_k\) satisfying \(\rho^{s_k}D_k\leq\varepsilon_k\) guarantees the requested consensus accuracy. For \(D_k>\varepsilon_k>0\), the smallest sufficient budget is \(s_k=\left\lceil\log(D_k/\varepsilon_k)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil\); take \(s_k=0\) when \(D_k\leq\varepsilon_k\). The cumulative communication budget through \(K\) outer iterations is \(S_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}s_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose enough inner mixing rounds that geometric disagreement contraction reaches the required tolerance; total communication is the sum of these round budgets.
assumptions_latex: \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\) and \(WJ=JW=J\).
A uniform contraction factor \(\rho\in(0,1)\) is known.
Bounds \(D_k\geq0\) and targets \(\varepsilon_k>0\) are available.

notation.meaning: bound on disagreement before inner consensus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cumulative Budgets for Standard Accuracy Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication cost induced by standard tolerance schedules under geometric mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(D_k\le D\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and choose the smallest \(s_k\ge0\) satisfying \(\rho^{s_k}D\le\varepsilon_k\). A fixed positive tolerance gives \(S_K=O(K)\). If \(\varepsilon_k=c(k+1)^{-p}\), with \(c,p>0\), then \(s_k=O(\log(k+1))\) and \(S_K=O(K\log K)\). If \(\varepsilon_k=cq^k\), with \(q\in(0,1)\), then \(s_k=O(k)\) and \(S_K=O(K^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric mixing costs linear cumulative rounds for fixed accuracy, order K log K for polynomial tightening, and order K squared for geometric tightening.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\le D<\infty\).
One-round disagreement contracts by \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
Budgets use the accepted seed's minimal geometric-contraction rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_K=O(K)\), \(O(K\log K)\), or \(O(K^2)\) for fixed, polynomial, or geometric tolerance schedules, respectively.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical schedules separating vanishing, summable, and nonsummable consensus-error regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c>0\), \(\varepsilon_k=c(k+1)^{-p}\) vanishes exactly when \(p>0\) and is summable exactly when \(p>1\). For \(q\in(0,1)\), \(\varepsilon_k=cq^k\) is summable and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k=c/(1-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial tolerances vanish for positive exponents but are summable only above exponent one; geometric tolerances are summable.
assumptions_latex: For the geometric schedule, \(q\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial and Geometric Accuracy Schedules
Consensus-Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance schedules distinguish exact, vanishing, summable, and fixed-error consensus regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_k=\widetilde Z^k-JZ^k\) be the consensus error entering outer iteration \(k\), with \(\|e_k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\). The schedule is exact when \(\varepsilon_k=0\), vanishing when \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), summable when \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), and uniformly inexact when \(\sup_k\varepsilon_k\leq\bar\varepsilon\) for some \(\bar\varepsilon>0\). Summability implies vanishing accuracy error, whereas a fixed positive bound alone does not. Consequently, convergence results requiring summable perturbations cannot generally be invoked from uniform boundedness alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus errors may be exact, vanishing, summable, or merely uniformly bounded; summability implies vanishing error, while a fixed positive tolerance does not.
assumptions_latex: The tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\).
The outer method receives additive consensus errors \(e_k\) bounded by \(\varepsilon_k\).

children.title: Event-Triggered Communication

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Triggered Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agents transmit only when a locally measurable innovation exceeds a scheduled threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agent \(i\) stores its last transmitted state \(\hat x_i^k\) and observes \(x_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\). Given thresholds \(\tau_i^k\geq0\), define \(a_i^k=1\) if \(\|x_i^k-\hat x_i^k\|>\tau_i^k\), and \(a_i^k=0\) otherwise. If \(a_i^k=1\), transmit \(x_i^k\) and set \(\hat x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\); otherwise transmit nothing and set \(\hat x_i^{k+1}=\hat x_i^k\). The prescribed distributed update uses neighbors' stored values \(\hat x_j^{k+1}\). Stop under the optimization criterion and output the terminal local states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent communicates only when its current state differs sufficiently from its last transmitted state; otherwise neighbors reuse the stored value.
assumptions_latex: Each agent can evaluate its local innovation norm.
Neighbors retain the most recently received state.
The threshold schedule \((\tau_i^k)\) is prescribed or locally computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When communication is suppressed, \(\|x_i^k-\hat x_i^k\|\leq\tau_i^k\), so the induced stale-state error is locally bounded.

notation.meaning: last transmitted state of agent i

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A worker reuses its last message while its current update remains sufficiently similar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Worker \(i\) computes a candidate message \(m_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) and retains its last transmitted message \(\hat m_i^{k-1}\). Given a nonnegative threshold \(\tau_i^k\), transmit and set \(\hat m_i^k=m_i^k\) when \(\|m_i^k-\hat m_i^{k-1}\|>\tau_i^k\); otherwise set \(\hat m_i^k=\hat m_i^{k-1}\) without communication. The coordinator or neighbors execute the prescribed optimization update using \(\hat m_i^k\) in place of \(m_i^k\). Terminate under the outer stopping rule and output the resulting iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker skips transmission when its new message is close to its cached message, and the algorithm reuses the cached value.
assumptions_latex: The message discrepancy is locally computable.
Recipients cache the last transmitted message.
Thresholds \(\tau_i^k\geq0\) are prescribed.

children.title: Skipped-Round Communication
children.top_down_role: Scheduled optimization rounds executed without message exchange.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when a scheduled communication process suppresses every round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two agents with scalar state \(z^k=(z_1^k,z_2^k)\), identity local computation, and communication indicator \(a_k\). If skipped rounds apply identity mixing, \(a_k=0\) for every \(k\), and \(z_1^0\neq z_2^0\), then \(z^{k+1}=z^k\) for every \(k\). Hence the initial disagreement persists and consensus is never attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every communication round is skipped and local computation does not couple agents, unequal initial states remain unequal forever.
assumptions_latex: Skipped rounds apply identity mixing.
\(a_k=0\) for every \(k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every block of B\ge1 consecutive iterations contains an active round, then C_K\ge\lfloor K/B\rfloor and \[\|JZ^K\|_F\le\rho^{\lfloor K/B\rfloor}\|JZ^0\|_F.\] For 0<\varepsilon<\|JZ^0\|_F, it suffices that \[K\ge B\left\lceil\frac{\log(\|JZ^0\|_F/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication-only disagreement dynamics with identity operators on skipped rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let J=I-\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top, let W be doubly stochastic with \|JW\|_2\le\rho<1, and set W_k=a_kW+(1-a_k)I for a_k\in\{0,1\}. For Z^{k+1}=W_kZ^k and C_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}a_k, \[Z^K=W^{C_K}Z^0,\qquad \|JZ^K\|_F\le\rho^{C_K}\|JZ^0\|_F.\]

Skipped-Round Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A prescribed activation schedule replaces selected communication rounds by identity mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k\in\{0,1\}\) specify whether communication occurs at iteration \(k\), and let \(W\) be the network mixing matrix. Define the effective operator \(W_k=a_kW+(1-a_k)I\). For stacked states \(Z^k\), compute \(\widetilde Z^k=W_kZ^k\), then apply the prescribed local optimization map to obtain \(Z^{k+1}\). Thus \(a_k=0\) causes no messages and preserves each local state before the optimization update, whereas \(a_k=1\) performs one mixing round. Stop under the outer criterion; the communication-round count through \(K\) is \(C_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}a_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary schedule selects which iterations perform network mixing; skipped rounds use identity mixing and incur no round of communication.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a message-substitution threshold into a per-event bound on the omitted update contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the recipient uses \(H_i^k\) satisfying \[\|H_i^k(u)-H_i^k(v)\|\le L_i^k\|u-v\|\] on the relevant region. If transmission is suppressed only when \(\|m_i^k-q_i^k\|\le\tau_i^k\), then \[\|H_i^k(m_i^k)-H_i^k(q_i^k)\|\le L_i^k\tau_i^k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid Lipschitz sensitivity bound converts the tested message-substitution error into a certified per-event downstream-impact bound.
assumptions_latex: The displayed Lipschitz inequality holds on the relevant message region.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Local Novelty Can Have Large Downstream Impact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calibration failure when message-space novelty is not matched to downstream sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar messages let \(H_c(m)=cm\). Given any novelty threshold \(\tau>0\) and desired impact \(M>0\), choose \(m-q=\tau/2\) and \(c>2M/\tau\). Then \[|m-q|\le\tau\quad\text{but}\quad|H_c(m)-H_c(q)|>M.\] Hence an unscaled message-difference score cannot uniformly control downstream error when sensitivity is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A message can appear locally redundant yet have arbitrarily large downstream effect when the recipient amplifies small differences.
assumptions_latex: No uniform upper bound on downstream sensitivity is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Small Local Novelty Can Have Large Downstream Impact

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic local definition tying a redundancy score to the exact substitute used when communication is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i^k\) be a candidate message and \(q_i^k\) the value that recipients can use without receiving it, such as a cached message or a jointly reconstructible prediction. Let \(R_i^k=R(m_i^k,q_i^k,\zeta_i^k)\ge0\) be a locally computable redundancy score. For \(\tau_i^k\ge0\), suppress transmission exactly when \(R_i^k\le\tau_i^k\); on suppression, recipients substitute \(q_i^k\) for \(m_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundancy rule suppresses a message when a local score is below threshold and uses the explicitly declared cached or predicted substitute.
assumptions_latex: The sender can compute the score from locally available information.
Recipients possess or can reconstruct the declared substitute \(q_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_i^k\le\tau_i^k\Longrightarrow m_i^k\text{ is not sent and recipients use }q_i^k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-novelty, prediction-error, and downstream-impact scores using the actual suppression substitute.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate message \(m_i^k\), cached value \(\widehat m_i\), receiver-reconstructible prediction \(\widetilde m_i^k\), and downstream contribution map \(H_i^k\), canonical choices are \[R_{\rm cache}=\|m_i^k-\widehat m_i\|,\qquad R_{\rm pred}=\|m_i^k-\widetilde m_i^k\|,\qquad R_{\rm imp}(q)=\|H_i^k(m_i^k)-H_i^k(q)\|.\] The first authorizes substitution by \(\widehat m_i\), the second by \(\widetilde m_i^k\), and the third directly scores the effect of its declared substitute \(q\). Their thresholds are not interchangeable without comparison bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundancy may be measured against a cached message, a shared prediction, or the induced downstream contribution, provided the tested value is the value actually substituted.
assumptions_latex: The prediction variant requires sender and receiver to reconstruct the same \(\widetilde m_i^k\).
The impact variant requires the relevant downstream map to be evaluable or soundly bounded.
Each score is paired with the substitute appearing in that score.

Redundancy-Based Suppression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transmission is suppressed when a locally testable message change is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) be agent \(i\)'s current message and \(\hat m_i^{k-1}\) its last transmitted message. For a nonnegative scale \(s_i^k\) and tolerance \(\eta_i^k\), declare the message redundant precisely when \(\|m_i^k-\hat m_i^{k-1}\|\leq\eta_i^k s_i^k\). A redundancy-suppression rule sends \(m_i^k\) only when this predicate fails and otherwise lets recipients reuse \(\hat m_i^{k-1}\). On every suppressed transmission, the substitution error equals \(m_i^k-\hat m_i^{k-1}\) and is bounded by the test threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A message is redundant when its change from the cached message falls below a scaled tolerance; suppression then creates a directly bounded substitution error.
assumptions_latex: Messages share a normed vector space.
The quantities \(s_i^k\geq0\) and \(\eta_i^k\geq0\) are locally available.
review_flags: The chosen norm-threshold formulation is standard but lacks a supplied redundancy-suppression source.

children.title: Suppression-Error Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Degradation caused by repeated omission of locally small communications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact accounting of staleness accumulated since the last transmitted message.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t(k)\le k\) be the last transmission time and \(\hat m^k=m^{t(k)}\). Then \[m^k-\hat m^k=\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}(m^j-m^{j-1}),\qquad \|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}\|m^j-m^{j-1}\|.\] If \(k-t(k)\le H\) and every one-step innovation is at most \(\delta\), then \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le H\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale-message error is the sum of innovations since the last transmission, so bounded refresh age or bounded skipped-interval variation controls accumulation.
assumptions_latex: \(m^k\) lies in a normed vector space.
\(\hat m^k=m^{t(k)}\), where \(t(k)\) is the last transmission time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}\|m^j-m^{j-1}\|\); bounded age and increments imply \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le H\delta\).

notation.meaning: last transmission time by iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Skipped-Innovation Accumulation Bound
Suppression-Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeatedly reusing stale messages can turn small per-round innovations into unbounded aggregate error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider one scalar message with \(m^k=k\delta\), where \(\delta>0\), and suppose no transmission occurs after \(\hat m^0=0\). Each one-step innovation is \(|m^k-m^{k-1}|=\delta\), so a rule testing only the latest increment against any threshold \(\tau\geq\delta\) suppresses every round. Nevertheless, the stale-message error is \(|m^k-\hat m^k|=k\delta\), which diverges. Thus bounding individual incremental changes does not bound accumulated suppression error unless the trigger compares against the last transmitted value, forces refreshes, or otherwise controls cumulative drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small per-round message changes can accumulate into unbounded staleness when suppression tests only consecutive increments and never forces a refresh.
assumptions_latex: The suppression test compares consecutive message increments only.
The cached message is not refreshed after iteration zero.
The threshold satisfies \(\tau\geq\delta>0\).

children.title: Adaptive Communication Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Communication effort adjusted as optimization progresses.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Communication Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication effort increases or decreases according to an outer-iteration accuracy target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), select a target communication error \(\varepsilon_k>0\) from locally or globally available progress information. Given a disagreement bound \(D_k\) and mixing contraction \(\rho\in(0,1)\), choose \(s_k=\max\{0,\lceil\log(D_k/\varepsilon_k)/\log(1/\rho)\rceil\}\), interpreting the logarithmic term as zero when \(D_k\leq\varepsilon_k\). Apply \(s_k\) consensus rounds, producing \(\widetilde Z^k=W^{s_k}Z^k\), and then execute the prescribed optimization update. Stop under the outer criterion and report both the terminal iterate and cumulative communication \(\sum_{t< K}s_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method converts a progress-dependent accuracy target into the minimum geometric-mixing budget needed at each optimization iteration.
assumptions_latex: One mixing round contracts disagreement by a known \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
A valid bound \(D_k\) on current disagreement is available.
The target sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\) is generated by a prescribed adaptation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected budget guarantees \(\|(I-J)\widetilde Z^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\) whenever \(\|(I-J)Z^k\|\leq D_k\).

children.title: Compressed Convex Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex convergence for synchronized workers averaging independently compressed subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf_i on a closed convex set C, let x^*\in\arg\min_C f, and choose g_{i,k}\in\partial f_i(x_k) with \|g_{i,k}\|\le G. Suppose q_{i,k}=Q_{i,k}(g_{i,k}) are conditionally independent across workers and satisfy \mathbb E_kq_{i,k}=g_{i,k} and \mathbb E_k\|q_{i,k}-g_{i,k}\|^2\le\omega\|g_{i,k}\|^2. For \[x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k\bar q_k),\quad \bar q_k=n^{-1}\sum_iq_{i,k},\quad \bar x_K=\frac{\sum_{k<K}\alpha_kx_k}{\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k},\] \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le\frac{\|x_0-x^*\|^2+G^2(1+\omega/n)\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k<K}\alpha_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronized distributed projected subgradient descent retains its convex ergodic bound, with independent unbiased compression adding averaged variance.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex with subgradients bounded by G on C.
Compressors are conditionally unbiased and conditionally independent across workers.
A minimizer exists and all workers use the common iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimized Convex Rate under Independent Unbiased Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon specialization of the synchronized unbiased-compressed subgradient theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound, suppose \(\|x_0-x^*\|\le D\) and choose \[\alpha_k=\frac{D}{G\sqrt{(1+\omega/n)K}},\qquad 0\le k<K.\] Then \(\bar x_K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x_k\) and \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f(x^*)]\le\frac{DG\sqrt{1+\omega/n}}{\sqrt K}.\] Consequently, expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\) is guaranteed when \[K\ge\frac{D^2G^2(1+\omega/n)}{\varepsilon^2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent unbiased compression preserves the inverse-square-root convex rate, inflating its constant by the square root of the averaged compressor-variance factor.
assumptions_latex: All assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Subgradient Bound hold.

Compressed Convex Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbed projected subgradient convergence under summable compression error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex with minimizer value \(f^*\). For \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), define \(Q_k(g_k)=g_k+e_k\) and \[x_{k+1}=P_C\!\left(x_k-\alpha_k Q_k(g_k)\right).\] If the subgradients are uniformly bounded, \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\), then \[\lim_{K\to\infty}\min_{0\le k\le K}f(x_k)=f^*.\] Thus summably weighted compressor error preserves convex objective convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected subgradient descent reaches the optimal value when steps diminish conventionally and the step-weighted compression error is summable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Horizon-dependent stepsize specialization of the synchronized unbiased-compression stationarity theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of Unbiased-Compressed Distributed Nonconvex Stationarity, write \(\Delta=f(x_0)-f_{\inf}\). If \(V>0\), choose \[\eta=\min\left\{\frac1L,\sqrt{\frac{2\Delta}{LVK}}\right\}.\] Whenever \(K\ge2\Delta L/V\), the second branch is active and \[\frac1K\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_k)\|^2\le2\sqrt{\frac{2\Delta LV}{K}}.\] Thus squared-gradient stationarity at most \(\varepsilon\) requires \(K=O(\Delta LV/\varepsilon^2)\) in the compression-variance-dominated regime. If \(V=0\), choosing \(\eta=1/L\) gives \(2L\Delta/K\).

For M_T such messages and h charged overhead bits per message, \[B_T=M_T\bigl(d\lceil\log_2N\rceil+h\bigr).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each of \(m\) workers transmits at most \(b\) bits per communication round and an error measure satisfies \(E_T\le CT^{-p}\) after \(T\ge1\) rounds, where \(C>0\) and \(p>0\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local biased compression need not preserve cancellation of heterogeneous gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_i(x)=\frac12\|x\|_2^2+c_i^\top x on \mathbb R^2, with c_1=(3,0.2), c_2=(-2,2), and c_3=(-1,-2.2). Since \sum_ic_i=0, the aggregate minimizer is x^*=0. children.title: Synchronous Execution

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based execution with a full coordination barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), synchronous execution consists of rounds \(k=0,1,\ldots\). At the start of round \(k\), every worker receives the same committed state \(x^k\), computes \(u_i^k\), and returns it before the next state is committed. The coordinator waits for every required worker and applies \[x^{k+1}=\Phi_k\!\left(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k\right).\] No worker begins computation for round \(k+1\) using an uncommitted state, and no update tagged with a different round enters this aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All required workers use the same round state, and the next state is committed only after the full barrier completes.
assumptions_latex: The required worker set \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is fixed for each round.
Each returned update carries its round index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle x^{k+1}=\Phi_k(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k)\) uses only updates computed from \(x^k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Semi-Synchronous Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cohort-based execution with bounded progress skew.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i(t)\in\mathbb{N}\) denote the number of updates completed by worker \(i\) by time \(t\). Execution is semi-synchronous with skew bound \(\Delta\in\mathbb{N}\) if workers may progress without a full barrier but the scheduler enforces \[\max_i s_i(t)-\min_i s_i(t)\le\Delta\quad\text{for every }t.\] Aggregations may use proper subsets of workers, but a worker whose progress would violate the bound is paused until lagging workers advance. The case \(\Delta=0\) reduces to lockstep progress; positive \(\Delta\) permits controlled overlap between computation rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers may advance in unequal cohorts, but the difference between the fastest and slowest progress counters remains uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many workers.
Each completed update increments exactly one progress counter.
\(\Delta\) is a fixed nonnegative integer.

knowledge_statements.title: Deadline-Based Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round aggregation using responses received before a fixed deadline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial state \(x^0\), deadline \(D>0\), and aggregation maps \(\Phi_k\), round \(k\) starts at time \(t_k\) by broadcasting \(x^k\). Define \[A_k=\{i:\text{worker }i\text{ returns }u_i^k\text{ by }t_k+D\}.\] At time \(t_k+D\), commit \[x^{k+1}=\Phi_k\!\left(x^k,\{u_i^k:i\in A_k\}\right).\] Responses tagged with round \(k\) that arrive later are discarded or retained only under an explicitly specified stale-update rule. Stop after a prescribed number of commits or when a stated termination test holds, and output the last committed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each round closes at a fixed time; only on-time responses enter its aggregation unless a stale-update rule is declared.
assumptions_latex: \(D>0\) is fixed or specified before each round.
Every response contains worker and round identifiers.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Barrier Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation triggered by a response quorum or deadline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a quorum \(q\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), an optional deadline \(D>0\), and initial state \(x^0\). In round \(k\), broadcast \(x^k\) at time \(t_k\) and let \(n_k(t)\) count distinct valid responses received by time \(t\). Close the barrier at \[\tau_k=\min\!\left\{\inf\{t\ge t_k:n_k(t)\ge q\},\ t_k+D\right\}.\] With \(A_k\) the responders available at \(\tau_k\), commit \(x^{k+1}=\Phi_k(x^k,\{u_i^k:i\in A_k\})\). Without a deadline, omit the second argument of the minimum. Output the last committed state at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A round commits after a response quorum arrives or a deadline expires, whichever occurs first.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le q\le m\).
Responses are deduplicated by worker and tagged by round.

knowledge_statements.title: Deadline-Induced Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Response-time dependence can bias the aggregated gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two equally weighted workers with deterministic local gradients \(g_1=1\) and \(g_2=-1\), so the full gradient is \((g_1+g_2)/2=0\). Suppose worker \(1\) always responds before a deadline and worker \(2\) never does. A deadline aggregator averaging available gradients therefore returns \[\widehat g=\frac{1}{|A|}\sum_{i\in A}g_i=g_1=1,\] not the full gradient. More generally, if response inclusion depends on worker identity, data, or gradient magnitude, then conditioning on timely response changes the sampling distribution and need not preserve unbiasedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If timely responses correlate with worker identity or data, averaging only on-time gradients can be biased even when the full gradient is zero.
assumptions_latex: Workers have equal objective weights.
Worker \(1\) is always included and worker \(2\) is always excluded by the deadline.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay reads that may combine components from different committed states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^0,x^1,\ldots denote committed shared states. A read used at update k may be represented by \widehat x_j^k=x_j^{\tau_j(k)}, where k-B\le\tau_j(k)\le k for every read component. The timestamps need not coincide, so \widehat x^k need not equal any single committed state x^s even though every component is at most B updates old.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded delay can constrain each component's age while allowing an inconsistent snapshot assembled from several recent versions.

Bounded-Delay Asynchrony
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous reads and activations with uniformly bounded age.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Index committed updates by \(k\in\mathbb{N}\). If worker \(i_k\) performs update \(k\), let \(\tau_{i_kj}(k)\le k\) be the version of component \(j\) that it reads. Execution has bounded-delay asynchrony with bound \(B\in\mathbb{N}\) when \[0\le k-\tau_{i_kj}(k)\le B\] for every component actually read, and every worker is activated at least once in each block of \(B+1\) consecutive committed updates. Computation and communication may otherwise overlap and arrive in arbitrary order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execution is asynchronous, but every read has bounded staleness and every worker is activated within a uniformly bounded update window.

children.title: Total Asynchrony

knowledge_statements.title: Total Asynchrony
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual activation and information refresh without uniform delay bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_1^i<k_2^i<\cdots\) be the committed updates performed by worker \(i\), and let \(\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)\le k_r^i\) denote the version of component \(j\) read at its \(r\)-th activation. Execution is totally asynchronous when every worker is activated infinitely often and \[\lim_{r\to\infty}\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)=\infty\quad\text{for every }i,j.\] Thus every worker eventually uses information newer than any fixed cutoff, although no finite constant need bound \(k_r^i-\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)\) or the gaps \(k_{r+1}^i-k_r^i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every worker and information stream progresses eventually, but neither staleness nor activation gaps need have a uniform finite bound.
assumptions_latex: Committed updates admit a global indexing.
Each worker-component read has an identifiable version index.
The worker set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle k_r^i\to\infty\quad\text{and}\quad\tau_{ij}(k_r^i)\to\infty\) for all \(i,j\), without uniform delay bounds.

notation.meaning: global index of worker i's r-th committed update
component-j version read at that activation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for the smooth unconstrained consensus model; it is not an asynchronous update rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be an incidence matrix of connected \(G\), \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), and \[r_{\rm con}(X)=\|(B^\top\otimes I_d)X\|,\qquad r_{\rm stat}(X)=\left\|\sum_i\omega_i\nabla f_i(x_i)\right\|.\] Then \(r_{\rm con}(X)=0\) is equivalent to consensus. At consensus, \(r_{\rm stat}(X)=0\) is equivalent to stationarity of \(F(x)=\sum_i\omega_i f_i(x)\), and certifies global optimality when every \(f_i\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero incidence disagreement certifies consensus; zero aggregate gradient at consensus certifies stationarity, and optimality in the convex case.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is connected.
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.
Convexity is required for the global-optimality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\rm con}(X)=r_{\rm stat}(X)=0\Longrightarrow X=\mathbf1\otimes x\text{ and }\nabla F(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus and First-Order Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective and agreement model independent of a particular asynchronous recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given local functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) and weights \(\omega_i>0\), solve \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_n}\sum_{i=1}^n\omega_i f_i(x_i)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_i=x_j\quad(\{i,j\}\in E),\] using computation and communication events that need not form global rounds. If \(G=(V,E)\) is connected, the constraints are equivalent to \(x_1=\cdots=x_n=x\), giving \(\min_x\sum_i\omega_i f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous consensus optimization solves a replicated-variable agreement problem without synchronized global rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(\omega_i>0\) for all \(i\).
\(G\) is connected for equivalence to one shared decision variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Consensus-Optimization Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for uncorrected consensus-gradient schemes using unbalanced mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be primitive and row-stochastic, with \(\pi^\top W=\pi^\top\), \(\pi_i>0\), and \(\pi^\top\mathbf1=1\). Mixing preserves the \(\pi\)-weighted aggregate, not generally the prescribed \(\omega\)-weighted aggregate. Thus an uncorrected method whose descent aggregate is induced solely by \(W\) need not optimize \(\sum_i\omega_i f_i\) unless \(\pi_i=\omega_i/\sum_j\omega_j\), or balancing, push-sum, eigenvector learning, or equivalent mass correction is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncorrected row-stochastic mixing generally follows stationary-distribution weights rather than the intended objective weights.
assumptions_latex: \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) is primitive.
No balancing or mass-correction mechanism is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi\not\propto\omega\Longrightarrow\text{consensus preservation alone does not ensure optimization of }\sum_i\omega_i f_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Objective-Bias Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asynchronous Coordinate Fixed-Point Realization of Consensus Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic event-driven realization when a consensus optimizer is represented by a block fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(T_1,\ldots,T_n):\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\) be a fixed-point map whose fixed points encode solutions of the stated consensus problem. At event \(k\), activate \(I_k\), read \(\widehat z^k=(z_1^{s_{k1}},\ldots,z_n^{s_{kn}})\), and set \[z_{I_k}^{k+1}=z_{I_k}^k+\lambda_k\bigl(T_{I_k}(\widehat z^k)-z_{I_k}^k\bigr),\qquad z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k\quad(i\ne I_k).\] Convergence additionally requires appropriate properties of \(T\), relaxation, activation, and delays.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asynchronous consensus optimizer can apply one block of a solution-encoding fixed-point map to delayed state information.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T\) encodes solutions of the consensus optimization problem.
Every read timestamp satisfies \(s_{kj}\le k\).
\(\lambda_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z^{k+1}\text{ differs from }z^k\text{ only in block }I_k.

notation.meaning: agent-i block of the solution-encoding fixed-point map

review_flags: This abstract realization does not validate the deferred uncorrected row-stochastic gradient recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Coordinate Fixed-Point Realization of Consensus Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite quadratic instance demonstrating the wrong-objective boundary for uncorrected unbalanced consensus optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let W=\begin{pmatrix}0.9&0.1\\0.2&0.8\end{pmatrix}, whose normalized stationary left vector is \pi=(2/3,1/3). Let f_1(x)=x^2/2 and f_2(x)=(x-3)^2/2, while the intended objective is F(x)=(f_1(x)+f_2(x))/2. Then \operatorname*{argmin}F=\{3/2\}, whereas \operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i\pi_i f_i(x)=\{1\}. Consequently, an uncorrected consensus-gradient realization whose limiting descent weights are induced by W can target x=1 rather than the intended equal-weight minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-agent row-stochastic network can target its stationary-weighted quadratic objective instead of the intended equal-weight sum.
assumptions_latex: W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1.
\pi^{\mathsf T}W=\pi^{\mathsf T}.
No balancing, push-sum, eigenvector learning, or equivalent objective-weight correction is used.
The realization's limiting descent weights are induced by \pi.

notation.meaning: stationary left probability vector of W

review_flags: The example establishes objective bias conditional on a realization inheriting the stationary weights; it is not a convergence theorem for every asynchronous implementation.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Agent Stationary-Weight Objective Bias
Asynchronous Consensus Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven consensus-gradient iteration using delayed neighbor states and no global rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) have \(n\) agents, local differentiable functions \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\), and row-stochastic weights \(W=(w_{ij})\) supported on \(E\). Initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At event \(k\), activate \(i_k\), choose read times \(s_{i_kj}(k)\le k\), and set
\[
x_{i_k}^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^n w_{i_kj}x_j^{s_{i_kj}(k)}-\alpha_k\nabla f_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^k),\qquad x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\quad(i\ne i_k).
\]
After \(K\) events, output the current agent states; terminate when a prescribed disagreement and stationarity test is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One activated agent mixes cached neighbor states and takes a local gradient step while all other agents remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(W\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\) and \(w_{ij}>0\) only for \(j=i\) or \((j,i)\in E\).
\(\alpha_k>0\), with delay and activation conditions imposed separately for convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed event rule defines a consensus-optimization iteration without synchronized communication rounds.

notation.meaning: timestamp of agent j's state read by agent i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic primal-dual correspondence for consensus optimization, not specifically an asynchronous method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=B^\top\otimes I_d\), \(F(X)=\sum_i\omega_i f_i(x_i)\), and consider \(\min_X F(X)\) subject to \(AX=0\). The Lagrangian is \(\mathcal L(X,\lambda)=F(X)+\langle\lambda,AX\rangle\), and the associated KKT equations are \(AX=0\) and \(\nabla F(X)+A^\top\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge multipliers produce the standard KKT representation of graph consensus, but this representation is not specific to asynchronous consensus optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is connected.
Each \(f_i\) is differentiable.

children.title: Asynchronous Gradient Tracking
children.top_down_role: Tracking with delayed and uneven agent activation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic condition preserving the aggregate-gradient identity across asynchronous events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G^k=\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\). If the augmented tracker state satisfies \[\mathcal M(Y^{k+1})=\mathcal M(Y^k)+G^{k+1}-G^k\] at every event and \(\mathcal M(Y^0)=G^0\), then \(\mathcal M(Y^k)=G^k\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative tracker transport plus injection of the aggregate gradient change preserves the tracker-mass invariant.
assumptions_latex: All held and in-transit tracker mass is included in \(Y^k\).
\(\mathcal M(Y^0)=G^0\).
Every event obeys the displayed balance equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Tracker-Mass Balance Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to applying one row of a synchronous balanced tracker recursion while retaining inactive trackers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar trackers \(y^k=(a,b)\), let only agent 1 apply the first row of \[W=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad y_1^{k+1}=\tfrac12(a+b),\quad y_2^{k+1}=b,\] with no gradient innovation. Then \[y_1^{k+1}+y_2^{k+1}=\tfrac12(a+3b)\ne a+b\] whenever \(a\ne b\), although \(W\) is doubly stochastic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Updating only one row of a doubly stochastic tracker mix generally changes total tracker mass.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one tracker is updated.
The inactive tracker is retained.
No buffer, push, or mass-correction state is used.
There is no gradient innovation at the event.
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Partial-Mixing Tracker Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-independent representation accounting for agent-held and in-transit tracker mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\). An asynchronous gradient-tracking realization uses an augmented state \(Y^k\) containing agent-held tracker variables and, where applicable, undelivered buffer or channel mass. A linear mass functional \(\mathcal M\) should satisfy exactly or asymptotically \[\mathcal M(Y^k)=\sum_{i=1}^n g_i^k\quad\text{or}\quad\left\|\mathcal M(Y^k)-\sum_i g_i^k\right\|\to0,\] while only the states involved in an activated computation or communication event change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid asynchronous tracking accounts for all held and in-transit tracker mass in an augmented event-driven state.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\) is defined.
The augmented state includes tracker mass that has left a sender but has not reached a receiver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M(Y^k)\text{ is the aggregate tracker quantity to be matched to }\sum_i\nabla f_i(x_i^k).

notation.meaning: total-mass functional on the augmented state

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Asynchronous Tracker State

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mass-preserving event primitive for asynchronous gradient tracking; primal descent and normalization remain separate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain held tracker masses \(y_i\), directed-channel buffers \(b_{ij}\), and gradients \(g_i=\nabla f_i(x_i)\). A send event at \(i\) chooses nonnegative fractions \(a_{ji}\) summing to one, replaces \(y_i\) by \(a_{ii}y_i^{\rm old}\), and adds \(a_{ji}y_i^{\rm old}\) to each outgoing buffer \(b_{ij}\). A receive event transfers one buffer to its receiver and zeros that buffer. When \(x_i\) changes, inject \(g_i^+-g_i^-\) into \(y_i\). Then \[\mathcal M=\sum_i y_i+\sum_{(i,j)}b_{ij}\] changes only by the injected gradient difference and equals \(\sum_i g_i\) at every event when initialized that way.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative splitting, buffering, delivery, and gradient-difference injection preserve total tracker mass despite delayed messages.
assumptions_latex: Every undelivered message is represented by a channel buffer.
Send fractions are nonnegative and sum to one, including retained mass.
Each delivered buffer is transferred exactly once.
Initially \(\mathcal M=\sum_i g_i\).

notation.meaning: undelivered tracker mass sent from i to j
fraction of sender i's old tracker mass assigned to recipient j

review_flags: This transport primitive is not by itself a complete convergent gradient-tracking optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Buffered Tracker Transport

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori test of the aggregate-gradient invariant in a buffered asynchronous tracker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For augmented tracker state \(Y^k\), mass functional \(\mathcal M\), and local gradients \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x_i^k)\), define \[r_{\rm tr}^k=\left\|\mathcal M(Y^k)-\sum_i g_i^k\right\|.\] Then \(r_{\rm tr}^k=0\) exactly certifies the aggregate tracker-mass identity. The test is sound only when all held and in-transit tracker mass is included in \(Y^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The defect between total augmented tracker mass and the current aggregate gradient exactly tests the tracking invariant when in-transit mass is included.
assumptions_latex: All agent-held and in-transit tracker mass is represented in \(Y^k\).
The aggregate of current local gradients is available when the certificate is evaluated.
review_flags: Zero mass defect does not certify consensus, descent, or optimality.
Computing the certificate may itself require aggregation of distributed state.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Tracker-Mass Defect Certificate
Asynchronous Gradient Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cached-neighbor gradient tracking with uneven single-agent activations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For differentiable \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(x_i^0\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(y_i^0=\nabla f_i(x_i^0)\). At event \(k\), agent \(i_k\) reads cached pairs \((x_j^{s_{i_kj}(k)},y_j^{s_{i_kj}(k)})\), forms
\[
\widehat x_{i_k}^{k}=\sum_j w_{i_kj}x_j^{s_{i_kj}(k)},\qquad
x_{i_k}^{k+1}=\widehat x_{i_k}^{k}-\alpha_k y_{i_k}^k,
\]
and updates
\[
y_{i_k}^{k+1}=\sum_j w_{i_kj}y_j^{s_{i_kj}(k)}+\nabla f_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^{k+1})-\nabla f_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^{k}).
\]
Inactive agents retain both variables. Output the current \(x_i\) values when the stopping test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activated agent mixes delayed primal and tracker states, then corrects its tracker by its own gradient change.
assumptions_latex: \(W=(w_{ij})\) is row-stochastic and graph-supported.
Every cached timestamp satisfies \(s_{ij}(k)\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion defines an asynchronous gradient-tracking scheme with delayed reads and uneven activation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied, and the displayed single-agent tracker update is not generically valid under merely row-stochastic mixing; asynchronous gradient tracking commonly requires additional mass correction, buffering, or augmented-state machinery.

children.title: Randomized Agent Activation
children.top_down_role: Distributed optimization driven by randomly selected participating agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Agent Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent categorical selection of one updating agent per event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given agents \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), a randomized single-agent activation process is a sequence \((I_k)_{k\ge0}\) taking values in \(V\). In the independent stationary model, there is a probability vector \(p\in(0,1]^n\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\) such that
\[
\mathbb{P}(I_k=i\mid I_0,\ldots,I_{k-1})=p_i
\]
for every \(k\) and \(i\). At event \(k\), only the state owned by agent \(I_k\) is eligible to change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each event independently selects exactly one agent, and every agent has a fixed positive selection probability.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\(p_i>0\) for every \(i\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every agent is selected infinitely often with probability \(1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp support boundary for independent stationary single-agent activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_i=0\), then agent \(i\) is never selected almost surely. Thus no algorithm whose only mechanism for changing agent \(i\)'s owned state is its activation can guarantee updating that state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent with zero selection probability is permanently starved.
assumptions_latex: Only activation of agent \(i\) can change its owned state.
The stationary activation distribution has \(p_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Probability Agent Starvation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-agent waiting-time law under independent stationary single-agent activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under independent activations with \(\mathbb P(I_k=i)=p_i>0\), the number \(T_i\) of events from one activation of agent \(i\) through its next activation satisfies \[\mathbb P(T_i=t)=(1-p_i)^{t-1}p_i,\qquad \mathbb E[T_i]=p_i^{-1},\qquad \mathbb P(T_i>m)=(1-p_i)^m.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent selected with probability p has geometric waiting times with mean 1/p.
assumptions_latex: Activations are independent across events.
\(p_i>0\) is stationary.

notation.meaning: events through the next activation of agent i

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Interactivation Times

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction for unequal selection probabilities in single-agent stochastic updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb P(I=i\mid\mathcal F)=p_i>0\), and let \(v_i\) be \(\mathcal F\)-measurable. Then \[\mathbb E\left[\frac{\omega_I}{p_I}v_I\,\middle|\,\mathcal F\right]=\sum_{i=1}^n\omega_iv_i.\] Without \(1/p_I\), the conditional mean is \(\sum_i p_i\omega_iv_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing a selected agent's contribution by its selection probability removes sampling bias for a prescribed aggregate.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\) whenever \(\omega_iv_i\) may be nonzero.
Each \(v_i\) is measurable before the activation draw.
review_flags: Importance weighting can increase variance when some selection probability is small.
knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Weighted Agent Contribution Is Unbiased

children.title: Randomized Block Activation
children.top_down_role: Distributed optimization driven by randomly selected variable or coordinate blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Block Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random selection of coordinate blocks eligible for an event update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\). A randomized block activation process is a sequence \((B_k)_{k\ge0}\) of random nonempty subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). At event \(k\), an update must satisfy
\[
x_b^{k+1}=x_b^k\quad\text{for every }b\notin B_k.
\]
In the independent full-coverage model, the sets \(B_k\) are independent and identically distributed, and each block has inclusion probability \(q_b=\mathbb{P}(b\in B_k)>0\). Singleton and minibatch sampling are both included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random nonempty set determines which coordinate blocks may change; in the independent full-coverage model, the sets are identically distributed and every block has positive inclusion probability.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\).
\(B_k\ne\varnothing\) almost surely.
The random sets \((B_k)_{k\ge0}\) are independent and identically distributed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under independent sampling with \(q_b>0\), every block is activated infinitely often almost surely.

notation.meaning: active block set at event k
marginal inclusion probability of block b

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of block coverage when one block is never activated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbb P(b\in B_k)=0\) for every \(k\), then the inactive-block rule gives \(x_b^k=x_b^0\) almost surely for all \(k\). Thus, for any update map satisfying \(T_b(x)=c_b\neq x_b^0\), the masked iteration cannot converge to a fixed point of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block that is never activated remains frozen and can prevent convergence even on a problem requiring only that block to change.
assumptions_latex: A block \(b\) has zero inclusion probability at every event.
Inactive blocks are retained exactly.
\(T_b(x)=c_b\neq x_b^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_b^k=x_b^0\ \text{for all }k\text{ almost surely, so convergence to a fixed point of }T\text{ is impossible}.

notation.meaning: required fixed-point value of the omitted block

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Inclusion Block Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent operator representation of simultaneous randomized block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(X_b\) be a vector space and let \(P_B\) retain precisely the blocks indexed by \(B\). Applying only the active blocks of \(T:X\to X\) is equivalent to \[x^{k+1}=x^k+P_{B_k}(T(x^k)-x^k).\] If \(B_k\) is independent of \(x^k\) and \(q_b=\mathbb P(b\in B_k)\), then \[\mathbb E[P_{B_k}\mid x^k]=\operatorname{diag}(q_1I_{X_1},\ldots,q_mI_{X_m}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized block update masks the residual of a full update map; the expected mask is diagonal with the marginal block-inclusion probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{b=1}^mX_b\), where every \(X_b\) is a vector space.
\(B_k\) is independent of the current iterate.
\(T:X\to X\) is block-valued.

notation.meaning: block mask retaining the coordinates indexed by B
full update map before activation masking

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Edge Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random communication-link selection for pairwise asynchronous updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite graph \(G=(V,E)\), a randomized edge activation process is a sequence \((E_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(E_k\in E\). In the independent stationary model, probabilities \(r_e>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{e\in E}r_e=1\) and
\[
\mathbb{P}(E_k=e\mid E_0,\ldots,E_{k-1})=r_e.
\]
At event \(k\), communication or pairwise state modification is restricted to the endpoints of \(E_k\); all other agent states remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each event independently selects one graph edge, permitting communication or updates only at that edge's endpoints.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and \(E\ne\varnothing\).
\(r_e>0\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every edge is activated infinitely often with probability \(1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global information propagation when sampled-edge support is disconnected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_+=(V,\{e:r_e>0\})\). If \(G_+\) is disconnected and communication is restricted to endpoints of sampled edges, no execution can transmit information between distinct components of \(G_+\). Therefore recurrence of every supported edge does not imply global network coverage or global consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite recurrence of every sampled edge cannot coordinate the whole network when the positive-probability edge support is disconnected.
assumptions_latex: Communication or state coupling occurs only across the sampled edge.
The positive-probability sampling-support graph is disconnected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global information propagation and global consensus cannot be guaranteed from supported-edge recurrence alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Sampling-Support Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic representation of independently sampled undirected edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orient each edge \(e\) arbitrarily and let \(b_e\) be its incidence vector. If edge \(e\) is sampled with probability \(r_e\), define \(L_{E_k}=b_{E_k}b_{E_k}^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[\bar L:=\mathbb E[L_{E_k}]=\sum_{e\in E}r_eb_eb_e^{\mathsf T},\qquad z^{\mathsf T}\bar Lz=\sum_{e=\{u,v\}\in E}r_e(z_u-z_v)^2.\] Its kernel consists of the vectors constant on each connected component of the positive-probability support graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected sampled-edge Laplacian is the weighted Laplacian of the sampling-support graph, whose nullspace identifies the components that activation can couple.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph.
\(r_e\geq0\) and \(\sum_{e\in E}r_e=1\).

notation.meaning: oriented incidence vector of edge e

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Activated-Edge Laplacian

children.title: Activation-Coverage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior under differing activation frequencies and coverage patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic and stochastic predicates ensuring recurrent activation of every component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite components \(\mathcal C\) and active sets \(A_k\subseteq\mathcal C\), common coverage regimes are: bounded coverage, when some \(B\ge1\) satisfies
\[
\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}A_t=\mathcal C\quad\text{for every }k;
\]
persistent conditional coverage, when constants \(B\ge1\) and \(\eta>0\) satisfy
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(c\in\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}A_t\mid\mathcal F_k\right)\ge\eta
\]
for every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and \(k\); and eventual coverage, when every \(c\) belongs to \(A_k\) for infinitely many \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage may require every component within each bounded window, positive conditional window probability, or merely infinitely many activations.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is finite.
\((\mathcal F_k)\) contains the activation history through event \(k-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded coverage implies eventual coverage; persistent conditional coverage implies eventual coverage almost surely under repeated conditional trials.

children.title: Bounded-Staleness Convergence
children.top_down_role: Guarantee families under uniformly controlled delays.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Staleness Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of asynchronous component updates for a contraction under bounded reads and bounded activation gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be complete under a block-maximum norm, and let \(F:X\to X\) satisfy \(\lVert F(x)-F(z)\rVert\le q\lVert x-z\rVert\) for some \(q\in[0,1)\). At event \(k\), selected components replace their values by the corresponding components of \(F\) evaluated at a mixed-time vector whose timestamps lie in \([k-\tau,k]\); unselected components are unchanged. If every component is selected at least once in every \(B\) consecutive events, then the asynchronous iterates converge to the unique fixed point \(x^*\) of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive fixed-point iteration converges despite asynchrony when delays and gaps between component updates are uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is complete and \(F\) is a contraction with modulus \(q<1\).
Every read is at most \(\tau<\infty\) events old.
Every component is updated within each window of \(B<\infty\) events.

children.title: Total-Asynchrony Convergence
children.top_down_role: Guarantees under eventual-update and fairness regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Total-Asynchrony Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contractive fixed-point convergence with unbounded delays satisfying only fairness and vanishing information age.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be complete under a block-maximum norm, and let \(F:X\to X\) be a contraction with modulus \(q<1\). At each event, any selected component \(i\) is replaced by \(F_i\) evaluated using timestamps \(s_{ij}(k)\le k\). Suppose every component is updated infinitely often and, along the update events of each component, \(s_{ij}(k)\to\infty\) for every required component \(j\). Then arbitrary finite but nonuniform update and communication delays are permitted, and the asynchronous iterates converge to the unique fixed point of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive asynchronous iteration converges with unbounded delays if every component updates forever and all information timestamps eventually advance.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a contraction on a complete block-maximum-norm product space.
Each component is updated infinitely often.
Every timestamp used along relevant updates tends to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}x^k=x^*\), where \(x^*\) is the unique solution of \(F(x^*)=x^*\).

notation.meaning: timestamp of component j used to update component i

children.title: Delay-Dependent Convergence Rates
children.top_down_role: Rate behavior parameterized by update delay or staleness.

knowledge_statements.title: Delay-Dependent Convergence Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case event complexity for delayed iteration of a contractive map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\to X\) be a contraction with modulus \(q\in(0,1)\) and fixed point \(x^*\). Consider
\[
x^{k+1}=F(x^{k-d_k}),\qquad 0\le d_k\le\min\{\tau,k\}.
\]
Then
\[
\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\le q^{\lceil k/(\tau+1)\rceil}\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert.
\]
Consequently, achieving \(\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\le\varepsilon\) is guaranteed after at most
\[
(\tau+1)\left\lceil\frac{\log(\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert/\varepsilon)}{-\log q}\right\rceil
\]
events, for \(0<\varepsilon<\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delay bound of τ slows the worst-case contraction exponent and event complexity by a factor of at most τ+1.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is complete and \(F\) is a \(q\)-contraction.
\(0\le d_k\le\min\{\tau,k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated error and event-complexity bounds hold for every admissible delay sequence.

children.title: Parallel Speedup Regimes
children.top_down_role: Concurrency ranges where additional workers improve optimization time.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Speedup Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-throughput criterion for near-linear asynchronous parallel speedup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K(\tau,\varepsilon)\) be the number of update events required for accuracy \(\varepsilon\) when staleness is bounded by \(\tau\). Suppose \(p\) workers process \(p\) events per unit time with negligible overhead and that the one-worker baseline has \(\tau(1)=0\). Define
\[
T_p(\varepsilon)=\frac{K(\tau(p),\varepsilon)}{p},\qquad T_1(\varepsilon)=K(0,\varepsilon),\qquad S_p(\varepsilon)=\frac{T_1(\varepsilon)}{T_p(\varepsilon)}.
\]
A worker range is a near-linear speedup regime with constant \(C\ge1\) when
\[
K(\tau(p),\varepsilon)\le C K(0,\varepsilon)
\]
throughout that range. Then \(S_p(\varepsilon)\ge p/C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel speedup is near-linear while delay increases the required update count by only a worker-independent constant factor relative to the zero-delay serial baseline.
assumptions_latex: Workers sustain aggregate throughput \(p\) updates per unit time.
Scheduling and communication overhead are excluded from \(T_p\).
The one-worker baseline satisfies \(\tau(1)=0\).

notation.meaning: updates required at delay bound τ and accuracy ε
speedup over the zero-delay one-worker baseline

children.title: Stale-Update Penalties
children.top_down_role: Optimization costs attributable to delayed information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Update Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz bound on gradient error caused by a delayed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and let an event use the stale gradient \(g^k=\nabla f(x^{k-d_k})\), where \(0\le d_k\le\tau\). Then
\[
\lVert g^k-\nabla f(x^k)\rVert
\le L\lVert x^{k-d_k}-x^k\rVert
\le L\sum_{t=k-d_k}^{k-1}\lVert x^{t+1}-x^t\rVert.
\]
Thus staleness contributes an error controlled by the cumulative motion during the omitted events; it vanishes whenever the sum of those intervening step lengths vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stale-gradient error is at most the smoothness constant times the accumulated iterate movement since the gradient was computed.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(z)\rVert\le L\lVert x-z\rVert\) for all \(x,z\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
\(0\le d_k\le\tau\).

notation.meaning: age of the gradient used at event k

children.title: Speedup Saturation Limits
children.top_down_role: Concurrency levels beyond which delay costs offset additional parallelism.

knowledge_statements.title: Speedup Saturation Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worker-independent speedup ceiling when delay-induced work grows linearly with concurrency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_0(\varepsilon)>0\) be the serial update count and suppose an asynchronous method with \(p\) workers requires
\[
K_p(\varepsilon)\ge c\bigl(1+\tau(p)\bigr)K_0(\varepsilon)
\]
for some \(c>0\). Under ideal throughput \(p\), its speedup is \(S_p=pK_0(\varepsilon)/K_p(\varepsilon)\). If the induced staleness satisfies \(\tau(p)\ge a(p-1)\) for some \(a>0\), then
\[
S_p\le\frac{p}{c(1+a(p-1))}\le\frac{1}{c\min\{1,a\}}.
\]
Hence increasing worker count cannot produce unbounded speedup in this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When staleness and delay-induced work both grow linearly with worker count, idealized parallel speedup remains uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(K_p(\varepsilon)\ge c(1+\tau(p))K_0(\varepsilon)\).
\(\tau(p)\ge a(p-1)\) with \(a,c>0\).
Aggregate processing capacity is at most \(p\) updates per unit time.

notation.meaning: parallel update count required for accuracy ε

children.title: Mixing-Weight Design

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Weight Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fastest-consensus weight design for a fixed undirected communication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a connected undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with \(|V|=n\), set \(J=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}/n\) and compute \[W^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{W}\ \lVert W-J\rVert_2\] subject to \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\), \(W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\), \(W_{ij}\geq0\), and \(W_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i\neq j\) and \(\{i,j\}\notin E\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), iterate \(x^{k+1}=W^\star x^k\), and stop when \(\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\). The design minimizes the worst contraction factor on \(\mathbf 1^\perp\) among feasible symmetric weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose graph-compatible symmetric stochastic weights minimizing disagreement contraction, then apply the resulting matrix until successive consensus iterates differ by at most the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, undirected, and connected.
Self-weights \(W_{ii}\) are permitted.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{W}\lVert W-J\rVert_2\) over the stated feasible set.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex epigraph formulation of symmetric mixing-weight design on a fixed topology.

Then \[\min_{W\in\mathcal W_G}\|W-J\|_2=\min_{W,t}\{t:-tI\preceq W-J\preceq tI,\ W\in\mathcal W_G\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fastest symmetric mixing-weight design is an SDP that bounds the disagreement operator between two semidefinite inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a fixed finite undirected graph.
Self-weights are permitted.

children.title: Communication-Topology Design
children.top_down_role: Selection or adaptation of the communication graph.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity-only specialization for static undirected topology design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((V,E_0)\) is an undirected candidate graph with nonnegative additive link costs and connectivity is the sole requirement, any minimum spanning tree is an optimal topology. A feasible connected topology exists exactly when \((V,E_0)\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With connectivity as the only requirement, a minimum spanning tree is an exact least-cost topology.
assumptions_latex: Candidate links are undirected.
Link costs are nonnegative and additive.
No degree, diameter, reliability, or spectral constraint is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cost Connected Topology

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between connectivity-only and constrained topology design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimum-cost undirected connectivity is polynomial-time solvable by a minimum spanning tree. Standard variants with additional degree, diameter, survivability, or spectral-performance requirements include NP-hard problems, so a complexity claim must name its constraint family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connectivity-only topology design is tractable, while common structural or performance-constrained variants can be NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: Inputs are finitely and rationally encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Connectivity-only design is in \(\mathbf P\); standard constrained topology-design families include NP-hard cases.
review_flags: The NP-hardness claim is existential across named constrained families, not universal for every additional constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Constraint Complexity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topology-only selection with fixed candidate links, costs, and graph-performance constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite nodes \(V\), candidate links \(E_0\), admissible family \(\mathcal G\subseteq2^{E_0}\), cost \(C(E)\), and topology performance measure \(\Phi(E)\), static topology design selects \[E^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{E\in\mathcal G}C(E)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\Phi(E)\le q.\] Mixing weights are not decision variables in this topology-only formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static topology design selects communication links under declared cost, feasibility, and graph-performance requirements.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(E_0\) are finite.
The admissible family and performance measure are explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Communication-Topology Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for connectivity-only undirected topology design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A spanning tree \(T\) is minimum-cost if and only if, for every \(e\in T\), edge \(e\) has minimum cost among candidate edges crossing the cut induced by deleting \(e\), with ties allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree is minimum-cost exactly when every tree edge is cheapest across its fundamental cut.
assumptions_latex: The finite candidate graph is connected and undirected.
Edge costs are additive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is an MST}\iff c_e=\min\{c_f:f\in\delta(S_e)\}\quad\forall e\in T.

notation.meaning: one component after deleting tree edge e

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Spanning-Tree Fundamental-Cut Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static redundancy-constrained undirected graph selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integer \(k\ge2\), solve \(\min_{E\subseteq E_0}\sum_{e\in E}c_e\) subject to \(|E\cap\delta(S)|\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(S\subset V\). These constraints are equivalent to connectivity after deletion of any \(k-1\) selected edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-edge-survivable topology places at least k selected links across every proper cut.
assumptions_latex: Candidate links are undirected.
Failures are arbitrary edge deletions.
Costs are additive.
knowledge_statements.title: Survivable Topology Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed rooted-reachability specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A minimum-cost spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r\) is the least-cost selected topology containing a directed path from \(r\) to every vertex. It exists exactly when every vertex is reachable from \(r\) and is computable by the Chu–Liu–Edmonds algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rooted directed reachability is optimized by a minimum-cost out-arborescence.
assumptions_latex: The candidate graph is finite and directed.
Arc costs are additive.
Only rooted outward reachability is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^\star\in\arg\min\left\{\sum_{a\in A}c_a:A\text{ is a spanning out-arborescence rooted at }r\right\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cost Rooted Directed Topology
Communication-Topology Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static topology selection under communication cost and consensus-rate requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate undirected links \(E_0\), link costs \(c_e\geq0\), and target contraction \(q\in[0,1)\), choose binary variables \(z_e\) and weights \(W\) by minimizing \(\sum_{e\in E_0}c_ez_e\) subject to \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(W\geq0\), \(W_{ij}=0\) when \(z_{\{i,j\}}=0\), and \(\lVert W-J\rVert_2\leq q\), where \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\). Output the active topology \(E(z)=\{e:z_e=1\}\) and its feasible mixing matrix; declare infeasibility if no pair satisfies the constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the least-cost set of links admitting symmetric stochastic weights whose disagreement contraction does not exceed a prescribed target.
assumptions_latex: \(E_0\) is a finite set of candidate undirected links.
Self-weights are allowed.
\(c_e\geq0\) and \(0\leq q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((z^\star,W^\star)\) minimizes \(\sum_{e\in E_0}c_ez_e\) subject to the stated mixing-rate constraints.

notation.meaning: indicator that candidate link e is activated
