children.title: Joint Weight–Topology Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Coupled adaptation of mixing weights and communication structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate procedure for a declared static joint objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a joint objective \(F(E,W)\), compute \[W^{r+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{W:(E^r,W)\text{ feasible}}F(E^r,W),\qquad E^{r+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{E:(E,W^{r+1})\text{ feasible}}F(E,W^{r+1}).\] Exact block minimization gives \(F(E^{r+1},W^{r+1})\le F(E^r,W^r)\), but does not by itself imply convergence to a global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating exact topology and weight updates decrease a common objective, without a generic global-optimality guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Both block subproblems attain minimizers.
Both steps use the same declared objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Topology–Weight Co-Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary preventing overstrong feasibility requirements for time-varying co-adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On three nodes, alternate \(E_{2r}=\{\{1,2\}\}\) and \(E_{2r+1}=\{\{2,3\}\}\), using positive self-weights and pairwise averaging on the active edge. Every instantaneous graph is disconnected, but every two-round union is connected and repeated products contract disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disconnected instantaneous graphs can still produce consensus through bounded-window joint connectivity.
assumptions_latex: Active-edge averaging uses positive self- and edge weights.
The two-edge pattern repeats.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_k\) disconnected for every \(k\) does not imply failure of consensus.
knowledge_statements.title: Per-Round Connectivity Is Not Necessary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled time-varying choice of active edges and compatible mixing weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A joint adaptation is a sequence \((E_k,W_k)\) with \(E_k\subseteq E_0\), where each \(W_k\) satisfies the declared stochasticity conditions and \((W_k)_{ij}=0\) for every off-diagonal pair \(\{i,j\}\notin E_k\). It is genuinely joint when topology choice depends on attainable weighted-mixing performance or weight choice depends on topology costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint adaptation changes links and graph-compatible weights together, with each decision influencing the other.
assumptions_latex: The node and candidate-link sets are fixed.
Every selected matrix is implementable on its selected graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Weight–Topology Adaptation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence interface for an adapted sequence of mixing operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\) and let every nonnegative \(W_k\) be doubly stochastic. For \(x^{k+1}=W_kx^k\), average consensus for every initial state is equivalent to \[\|(W_{k-1}-J)\cdots(W_0-J)\|_2\to0.\] If for some \(B\ge1\) and \(\rho<1\), every length-\(B\) block product has norm at most \(\rho\), then disagreement contracts geometrically by block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adapted graph-weight sequence reaches average consensus exactly when its matrix products contract disagreement; uniform block contraction gives a geometric bound.
assumptions_latex: Every \(W_k\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
All matrices act on the same finite node set.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Contraction Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observation-driven selection from a finite feasible family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) be a finite family of implementable graph-weight pairs and \(\ell_k(d)\in[0,1]\). Initialize \(q_1(d)=1\), sample \(d_k\) with probability \(q_k(d)/\sum_{d'}q_k(d')\), observe all losses, and set \(q_{k+1}(d)=q_k(d)e^{-\eta\ell_k(d)}\). Use the matrix in \(d_k\) for round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponential weighting adapts graph-weight choices to observed communication and mixing losses.
assumptions_latex: The feasible design family is finite and nonempty.
Every pair is graph-compatible and implementable.
Full-information losses lie in \([0,1]\).
review_flags: Bandit feedback requires a different estimator and bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Information Online Graph–Weight Adaptation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit implementation cost of exponential weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintaining explicit weights for \(M\) graph-weight pairs uses \(O(M)\) storage and \(O(M)\) arithmetic per full-information round, excluding loss evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naive online co-adaptation scales linearly with the number of feasible designs per round.
assumptions_latex: All design weights and updates are explicit.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Family Online Search Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regret and Consensus under Uniformly Contractive Online Choices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint guarantee for finite full-information adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=|\mathcal D|\), exponential weighting satisfies \(\mathbb E\sum_{k=1}^K\ell_k(d_k)-\min_d\sum_{k=1}^K\ell_k(d)\le\log(M)/\eta+\eta K/8\). With \(\eta=\sqrt{8\log(M)/K}\), regret is at most \(\sqrt{K\log(M)/2}\). If every selectable \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(\|W-J\|_2\le\rho<1\), then \(\|x^K-Jx^0\|_2\le\rho^K\|x^0-Jx^0\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-family adaptation has sublinear full-information regret, while uniform contraction guarantees geometric consensus.
assumptions_latex: Losses lie in \([0,1]\).
For consensus, every feasible matrix is doubly stochastic and uniformly contractive.
review_flags: Uniform per-round contraction is sufficient but stronger than bounded-window joint connectivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Regret and Consensus under Uniformly Contractive Online Choices

children.title: Topology-Feasibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Connectivity or implementability limits on adaptive communication structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp connectivity boundary for symmetric average-consensus mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and permit nonnegative self-weights. There exists a symmetric matrix \(W\) satisfying \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(W_{ij}=0\) for every absent off-diagonal edge, and \(\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1\), with \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/|V|\), if and only if \(G\) is connected. If \(G\) is disconnected, every compatible stochastic \(W\) has a nonconsensus vector \(v\perp\mathbf1\) with \(Wv=v\), so strict contraction of all disagreement vectors is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed undirected topology supports strict average-consensus contraction exactly when it is connected; disconnection leaves an invariant nonconsensus direction.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and undirected.
Mixing weights are symmetric and nonnegative.
Self-weights are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists W:\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1\) if and only if \(G\) is connected.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-flow obstruction for switching undirected topologies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a nonempty proper set \(S\subset V\) and \(k_0\) exist such that no \(G^k\), \(k\ge k_0\), contains an edge crossing \((S,V\setminus S)\). Every compatible mixing product after \(k_0\) is block diagonal across that cut, so initial states having different constants on the two sides cannot reach global consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If communication permanently stops across a cut, no compatible local averaging scheme can guarantee global consensus.
assumptions_latex: Mixing is graph-compatible.
A proper cut has no crossing edge after a finite time.

notation.meaning: one side of the persistent communication cut

Positive entries are uniformly bounded below and diagonals are positive.
Every bounded-window graph union is connected.

children.title: Communication Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Temporal allocation of links, nodes, and communication rounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two fairness levels for resources required to remain active over an infinite schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a schedule \((S_k)\) and required resource \(a\in\mathcal A\), persistent fairness requires \(\lvert\{k:a\in S_k\}\rvert=\infty\). Bounded-gap fairness requires some \(B_a<\infty\) such that \[a\in\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B_a-1}S_t\quad\text{for every }k\ge0.\] Bounded-gap fairness implies persistent fairness, but persistent fairness does not imply a uniform activation-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A required resource may merely recur infinitely often or, more strongly, recur in every window of a fixed length.
assumptions_latex: The schedule is infinite.
The condition is imposed only on resources declared required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{bounded-gap fairness}\Longrightarrow\text{persistent fairness}\), while the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent and Bounded-Gap Schedule Fairness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infinite Recurrence Does Not Imply Bounded-Window Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating eventual recurrence from uniform temporal connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On two nodes with sole edge \(e=\{1,2\}\), let \(E_k=\{e\}\) when \(k=2^r\) for some \(r\in\mathbb N\), and let \(E_k=\varnothing\) otherwise. The edge is activated infinitely often, but its activation gaps are unbounded. Consequently, no finite \(B\) makes every \(B\)-round union graph connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An edge can recur forever while increasingly long silent intervals prevent bounded-window connectivity.
assumptions_latex: Communication rounds are indexed by nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\text{ activated infinitely often}\not\Longrightarrow\exists B<\infty\text{ such that every }B\text{-round union is connected}.\)

notation.meaning: active edge set at round k

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Recurrence Does Not Imply Bounded-Window Connectivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified representation of link, node, and communication-resource scheduling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a finite set of schedulable communication resources and let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal F_k\subseteq2^{\mathcal A}\) be the family of simultaneously feasible activations at round \(k\). A communication schedule is a sequence \((S_k)_{k\ge0}\) satisfying \(S_k\in\mathcal F_k\). Link scheduling uses \(\mathcal A=E\), node scheduling uses \(\mathcal A=V\), and a silent round is represented by \(S_k=\varnothing\) when \(\varnothing\in\mathcal F_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, a communication schedule selects a feasible set of links, nodes, or other communication resources.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is finite.
\(\mathcal F_k\) is nonempty and specified for every round.

notation.meaning: feasible simultaneous activations at round k

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Activation-Schedule Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical open-loop policies over a declared feasible family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^{\mathcal A}\), a periodic policy selects \(S_0,\ldots,S_{P-1}\in\mathcal F\) and sets \(S_k=S_{k\bmod P}\). An i.i.d. randomized policy draws \(S_k\sim p\) on \(\mathcal F\). A resource appearing in a period has activation gap at most \(P\). Under the randomized policy, \(\Pr(a\in S_k)>0\) implies activation infinitely often almost surely, but generally gives no deterministic gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodic schedules provide deterministic recurrence bounds; positive-probability randomized schedules provide almost-sure recurrence without deterministic bounded gaps.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) and \(P\) are finite.
Randomized rounds are independent and identically distributed.
knowledge_statements.title: Periodic and Randomized Feasible Scheduling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interference-aware priority scheduling for one communication round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative priorities \(w_a^k\) and a finite nonempty feasible family \(\mathcal F_k\), select \[S_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{S\in\mathcal F_k}\sum_{a\in S}w_a^k.\] Under node-exclusive link interference, feasible sets are matchings; on a bipartite communication graph the subproblem is maximum-weight bipartite matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate a feasible set of communication resources having maximum total current priority.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_k\) is finite and nonempty.
Priorities are known before round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Weight Feasible Activation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for node-exclusive maximum-weight scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bipartite graph with edge weights \(w_{ij}\), a matching \(M\) is maximum weight if there are potentials \(u_i,v_j\ge0\) satisfying \(u_i+v_j\ge w_{ij}\) for every edge and \[\sum_i u_i+\sum_jv_j=\sum_{(i,j)\in M}w_{ij}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible matching and equal-valued feasible vertex potentials certify maximum-weight scheduling optimality.
assumptions_latex: The communication graph is bipartite.
At most one scheduled edge may meet each vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Bipartite Matching-Schedule Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tractable matching schedules versus general conflict-graph scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maximum-weight matching is polynomial-time solvable. If feasible simultaneous activations are the independent sets of an arbitrary conflict graph, maximum-weight scheduling is maximum-weight independent set and is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching-based scheduling is polynomially computable, whereas scheduling under an arbitrary conflict graph is NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: Weights are rationally encoded.
Complexity is measured in the explicit graph input size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{maximum-weight matching}\in\mathbf P\), whereas arbitrary conflict-graph maximum-weight scheduling is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling-Subproblem Complexity Boundary
Communication Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-varying scheduling with bounded-window connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication schedule on nodes \(V\) is a sequence \((G_k)_{k\geq0}\), where \(G_k=(V,E_k)\) contains exactly the links activated at round \(k\). It is \(B\)-connected if an integer \(B\geq1\) exists such that, for every \(k\geq0\), the union graph \((V,\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}E_t)\) is connected. A compatible scheduled mixing sequence \((W_k)\) satisfies \((W_k)_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i\neq j\) and \(\{i,j\}\notin E_k\). The schedule terminates at the first prescribed round or stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A schedule specifies active links each round; bounded-window connectivity requires every consecutive window of fixed length to contain a connected union graph.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a fixed finite node set.
Communication proceeds in indexed rounds.
\(B\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((G_k)_{k\geq0}\) is \(B\)-connected exactly when every \(B\)-round union graph is connected.

notation.meaning: active communication graph at round k

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i f_i(x)\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and a server counter \(k=0\). Whenever worker \(i_k\), sampled with probability \(q_{i_k}>0\), returns \(g_k=\nabla f_{i_k}(x^{k-\tau_k})\) with \(0\leq\tau_k\leq\tau_{\max}\), immediately set \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_k\frac{p_{i_k}}{q_{i_k}}g_k.\] Increment \(k\) without waiting for other workers. Stop after a prescribed number of accepted gradients or when a stated stationarity test is met, and output the latest iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update immediately when a worker responds, weighting its delayed gradient by the objective weight divided by its selection probability, without waiting at a global barrier.
knowledge_statements.title: Straggler-Aware Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12[(x-1)^2+(x+1)^2]\). If worker 2 never contributes, response-driven gradient descent may use only \(\nabla f_1(x)=x-1\) and converge to \(x=1\), whereas the minimizer of \(F\) is \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanently ignoring a worker can make an asynchronous method optimize the wrong objective.
assumptions_latex: Worker 1 continues to respond.
Worker 2 is permanently starved.

children.title: Load-Aware Optimization
children.top_down_role: Optimization methods adapted to unequal computational workloads.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initial assignment of indivisible tasks using predicted worker loads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For jobs with processing times \(p_j>0\) on \(m\) identical workers, list scheduling assigns each successive job to a currently least-loaded worker. Its makespan satisfies \[T_{\rm LS}\le\left(2-\frac1m\right)T^\star.\] The longest-processing-time-first variant orders jobs by nonincreasing \(p_j\) and, for \(m\ge2\), satisfies \[T_{\rm LPT}\le\left(\frac43-\frac1{3m}\right)T^\star.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-loaded assignment has a standard constant-factor guarantee, improved by assigning longer jobs first.
assumptions_latex: Jobs are independent and indivisible.
Workers are identical and processing times are known.
Migration and communication costs are excluded.

notation.meaning: predicted processing time of job j

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Load-Aware List Scheduling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial boundary absent from continuously divisible allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimizing \(\max_i\sum_{j\in A_i}p_j\) over partitions of indivisible jobs among at least two identical workers is NP-hard; for two workers its decision form contains PARTITION. Thus continuous equal-finish allocation does not extend exactly to indivisible jobs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal indivisible load balancing is NP-hard although continuously divisible constant-rate allocation has a closed form.
assumptions_latex: Job sizes are positive integers encoded in binary.
Every job is assigned wholly to one worker.
knowledge_statements.title: Indivisible Load Assignment Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustness limit of allocation based on predicted service rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(b_i=B\hat s_i/\sum_j\hat s_j\) is assigned using predicted rates but actual rates are \(s_i>0\), then \[T=\frac{B}{\sum_j\hat s_j}\max_i\frac{\hat s_i}{s_i},\qquad \frac{T}{T^\star}=\frac{\sum_i s_i}{\sum_j\hat s_j}\max_i\frac{\hat s_i}{s_i}.\] A sufficiently severe rate overestimate can therefore make the realized makespan arbitrarily worse than the actual-rate optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proportional allocation can perform arbitrarily badly when a worker's service rate is severely overestimated.
assumptions_latex: Work is divisible.
Predicted and actual rates are positive and constant during the batch.

notation.meaning: predicted service rate of worker i

knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Misestimation Makespan Boundary
Load-Aware Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divisible-work allocation using measured worker service rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a divisible batch of size \(B>0\) and measured worker rates \(s_i>0\), choose loads by solving \[\min_{b_i\geq0}\ \max_i\frac{b_i}{s_i}\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^n b_i=B.\] Dispatch load \(b_i^\star=B s_i/(\sum_j s_j)\) to worker \(i\), remeasure rates after completion, and repeat for the next batch. The optimal predicted makespan is \(B/(\sum_j s_j)\). Stop when all requested optimization work is processed and aggregate the workers' weighted contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate divisible work in proportion to measured service rates, which equalizes predicted completion times and minimizes the batch makespan.
assumptions_latex: The batch is continuously divisible.
Worker \(i\) processes at constant predicted rate \(s_i>0\) during the batch.
Communication overhead is excluded or already incorporated into \(s_i\).

notation.meaning: predicted service rate of worker i

review_flags: The supplied communication locator is too broad to support the proportional divisible-load theorem.
standard_field_rationale: equal-finish-time allocation is the standard continuous makespan solution for constant worker rates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proportional allocation and makespan value are correct under the stated continuously divisible, constant-rate model, and algorithm is an appropriate role for the leaf. No inspectable source is supplied for the allocation result, so the record cannot be accepted.

children.title: Workload Redistribution
children.top_down_role: Reallocation of computational responsibility across participants.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservation law distinguishing migration from dropping or replicating work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_j\ge0\) be work initially owned by participant \(j\), and let \(a_{ij}\ge0\) be the amount ultimately executed by \(i\) for \(j\). Redistribution is conservative when \[\sum_i a_{ij}=d_j\quad\text{for every }j,\] and is nontrivial when some \(a_{ij}>0\) with \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redistribution moves execution responsibility while conserving every original workload.
assumptions_latex: Work is divisible and exactly recombinable.

notation.meaning: work executed by i on behalf of original owner j

knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Workload Redistribution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of divisible linear redistribution models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each job must be transferred and executed as an indivisible unit, makespan-minimizing redistribution contains identical-machine scheduling as its zero-transfer-cost special case and is NP-hard. A divisible redistribution linear program therefore need not solve the indivisible problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal redistribution becomes NP-hard when jobs cannot be split, even with zero transfer costs.
assumptions_latex: Jobs have integer sizes and remain indivisible.
Transfer costs may be zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Indivisible Redistribution Is Combinatorial

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic conservative migration of unstarted work units.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an atomic owner for every unstarted unit and a deque at each worker. An idle worker atomically transfers a declared batch from a donor's unstarted tail. Completed or executing units are not stolen. Terminate only when all deques are empty, no unit is executing, and no transfer is in flight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Idle workers steal atomically owned unstarted work while preserving exactly-once execution.
assumptions_latex: Ownership transfer is atomic.
Only unstarted work is transferable.
Termination detection accounts for queued, executing, and in-flight work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every initial work unit is executed exactly once, and detected termination implies no work remains.}
knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Work-Stealing Redistribution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for the divisible-load linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal and dual feasible points certify optimality when \(T=\sum_j\lambda_jd_j-vH\). Equivalently, complementary slackness requires \(u_i(\sum_j a_{ij}/s_i-T)=0\), \(v(\sum_{i,j}h_{ij}a_{ij}-H)=0\), \(a_{ij}(u_i/s_i+vh_{ij}-\lambda_j)=0\), and \(T(1-\sum_i u_i)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching primal and dual objectives, equivalently full complementary slackness, certifies optimal redistribution.
assumptions_latex: The candidates are feasible for the displayed primal and dual.
review_flags: Corrected the builder certificate by adding complementary slackness for the nonnegative makespan variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Redistribution Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock condition for beneficial redistribution under a declared timing model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T_0\) is completion time without migration, \(T_1\) is post-redistribution execution makespan excluding migration, and \(C_{\rm mig}\) is critical-path migration time, redistribution helps exactly when \(C_{\rm mig}+T_1<T_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Migration is worthwhile exactly when saved execution time exceeds critical-path migration overhead.
assumptions_latex: All terms use one consistent nonoverlap timing model.
review_flags: Overlap or contention requires the corresponding critical-path replacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Migration Break-Even Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual pricing of load conservation, executor capacity, and transfer budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{a\ge0,T\ge0}T\) subject to \(\sum_i a_{ij}=d_j\), \(\sum_j a_{ij}/s_i\le T\), and \(\sum_{i,j}h_{ij}a_{ij}\le H\), the dual is \(\max_{\lambda,u,v}\sum_j\lambda_jd_j-vH\) subject to \(u_i,v\ge0\), \(\sum_i u_i\le1\), and \(\lambda_j\le u_i/s_i+vh_{ij}\) for all \(i,j\), with \(\lambda_j\) free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The redistribution dual prices original loads, executor time, and the transfer budget.
assumptions_latex: Loads are divisible.
The primal is feasible and finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of Divisible Makespan Redistribution
Workload Redistribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Makespan-minimizing redistribution of divisible work across heterogeneous workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let worker \(j\) initially own divisible load \(d_j\geq0\), and let \(a_{ij}\geq0\) denote the portion executed by worker \(i\). Given rates \(s_i>0\), transfer costs \(h_{ij}\geq0\), and budget \(H\), solve \[\min_{a,T}\ T\] subject to \(\sum_i a_{ij}=d_j\), \(\sum_j a_{ij}/s_i\leq T\) for every \(i\), and \(\sum_{i,j}h_{ij}a_{ij}\leq H\). Transfer and execute the resulting assignment, then stop after all assigned portions complete and combine their exact contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redistribute divisible work by minimizing the maximum worker processing time subject to conservation of every original load and a transfer-cost budget.
assumptions_latex: All loads are divisible and their contributions can be recombined exactly.
Rates satisfy \(s_i>0\).
Transfer costs are linear and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((a^\star,T^\star)\) minimizes predicted makespan subject to load conservation and transfer budget \(H\).

notation.meaning: load moved from owner j to executor i
initial load owned by worker j

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the redistribution linear program.
standard_field_rationale: divisible-load redistribution admits a linear makespan formulation under linear processing and transfer costs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linear makespan formulation is plausible for divisible loads, but no source supports this exact redistribution model. The transfer budget H should also be introduced with its domain and the algorithm should specify how infeasibility is handled.

children.title: Tail-Latency Mitigation
children.top_down_role: Policies limiting the influence of extreme completion times.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Waiting for the first q admissible responses rather than every assigned worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dispatch a common iterate to \(n\) workers and update after the first \(q\) admissible responses, \(1\le q\le n\), so round latency is \(T_{(q)}\). If the accepted subset \(S\) has known inclusion probabilities \(\pi_i>0\), then the Horvitz--Thompson aggregate \(\sum_{i\in S}(p_i/\pi_i)g_i\) is unbiased for \(\sum_i p_ig_i\), provided the inclusion model correctly accounts for response selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quorum limits waiting to the q-th response, while inclusion-probability correction can preserve the target aggregate.
assumptions_latex: Exactly the first \(q\) admissible responses are accepted.
The inclusion probabilities are positive and correctly specified.
review_flags: Correction is invalid if the stated inclusion model omits dependence between response times and returned values.
knowledge_statements.title: Quorum Response Mitigation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correlated Replicas Need Not Reduce Tail Latency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence boundary for speculative-execution benefits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If all replica completion times satisfy \(T_j=T\) almost surely, then \(\min_{j\le r}T_j=T\) for every \(r\). Perfect common-mode dependence therefore yields no latency reduction while potentially multiplying executed work by \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication cannot remove common-mode stalls.
assumptions_latex: Replica completion times are perfectly dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{(1)}=T\) almost surely for every replica count \(r\).
knowledge_statements.title: Correlated Replicas Need Not Reduce Tail Latency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Replica Completion as an Order Statistic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Latency law for speculative replication under an explicit stochastic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\) independent replica times with common distribution function \(F\), \[\Pr(\min_{j\le r}T_j>t)=(1-F(t))^r.\] If the times are exponential with rate \(\mu\), the minimum is exponential with rate \(r\mu\) and mean \(1/(r\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent replication replaces shard latency by a minimum order statistic.
assumptions_latex: Replica times are independent and identically distributed.
The mean specialization assumes exponential times of rate \(\mu\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\), let \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) have every \(m\)-row submatrix nonsingular, and let worker \(i\) return \(y_i=\sum_{s=1}^mC_{is}g_s\). From any responding set \(S\) of size \(m\), \(C_S\) is invertible, so all \(g_s\), and hence \(\sum_sg_s\), are recovered exactly. The recovery threshold is \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An MDS-coded linear response model recovers the exact aggregate from any m of n responses.
assumptions_latex: Shard contributions combine linearly.
Workers can form the coded responses exactly.
Every \(m\)-row submatrix of \(C\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |S|\ge m\Rightarrow\sum_{s=1}^mg_s\text{ is exactly recoverable from }\{y_i:i\in S\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For shards \(s=1,\ldots,m\), completion times \(T_{sj}\), and budget \(R\ge m\), choose \(r^\star\in\arg\min_{r_s\in\mathbb N,\,r_s\ge1,\,\sum_s r_s\le R}\mathbb E[\max_s\min_{1\le j\le r_s}T_{sj}]\). The finite feasible set can be enumerated to obtain a global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate a finite redundancy budget to minimize expected replicated makespan under the declared latency model.
assumptions_latex: The joint completion-time law is known or consistently estimated.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\) independent identically distributed nonnegative replica times with CDF \(F\), \(\mathbb E[T_{(1)}]=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^r\,dt\). Launching \(r\) copies uses at most \(r\) times the unreplicated work before cancellation.

Tail-Latency Mitigation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact speculative replication for reducing shard-completion tail latency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a deterministic gradient as \(g(x)=\sum_{s=1}^m g_s(x)\). At iteration \(k\), assign each shard \(s\) to \(r_s\geq1\) workers using the same iterate \(x^k\). Accept the first returned exact value of \(g_s(x^k)\), cancel its unfinished replicas, and update only after one value has arrived for every shard: \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_k\sum_{s=1}^m g_s(x^k)\). Stop at the prescribed iteration or optimization tolerance. The iteration latency equals the maximum, over shards, of each shard's first-replica completion time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replicate each gradient shard, accept its first exact response, cancel slower copies, and update after every shard has contributed once.
assumptions_latex: Replicas of a shard compute the same deterministic value.
Cancellation does not alter accepted results.
Each shard has at least one eventually completing replica.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_k\sum_{s=1}^m g_s(x^k)\) uses the exact unreplicated gradient while waiting only for first replica completions.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers speculative replication or order-statistic latency.
A coded-computation reference is required before candidate promotion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Sums Can Miss Discrete Pareto Co-Designs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of complete Pareto recovery by linear resource scalarization in a discrete joint design space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider three accuracy-feasible designs with two minimized resource costs \(r(d_1)=(0,2)\), \(r(d_2)=(1,1.1)\), and \(r(d_3)=(2,0)\). All three are Pareto efficient. For every \(\theta\in[0,1]\), however, the weighted cost \(\theta r_1+(1-\theta)r_2\) of \(d_2\) is strictly larger than that of \(d_1\) or \(d_3\). Thus no nonnegative weighted-sum scalarization selects \(d_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete compute–communication–precision design can be Pareto efficient yet unsupported by every linear resource weighting.

Only the three displayed accuracy-feasible designs are compared.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-independent joint comparison of computation, communication, precision, and elapsed-time resources at a common quality target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\in\mathcal D\) jointly specify local computation, communication frequency or volume, and message precision. Let \(Q(d)\) be a common quality measure and \(r(d)=(r_{\rm comp}(d),r_{\rm comm}(d),r_{\rm bits}(d),r_{\rm time}(d))\) be consistently accounted resource costs. For target \(\varepsilon\), a feasible design \(d^\star\) with \(Q(d^\star)\le\varepsilon\) is Pareto efficient if no feasible \(d\) satisfies \(r_j(d)\le r_j(d^\star)\) for every component with strict inequality in at least one component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint design is Pareto efficient when no equally accurate design uses no more of every declared resource and strictly less of at least one.
assumptions_latex: All compared designs use the same quality criterion and target \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Budgeted Scalarization of Joint Resource Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-independent scalarization of accuracy-feasible compute–communication–precision designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_\varepsilon=\{d\in\mathcal D:Q(d)\le\varepsilon\}\) and let \(r(d)\in\mathbb R_+^m\) contain consistently measured resource costs. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\), solve \(\min_{d\in\mathcal F_\varepsilon}\lambda^{\mathsf T}r(d)\). Every minimizer is weakly Pareto efficient; if \(\lambda_j>0\) for every \(j\), every minimizer is Pareto efficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted resource minimization yields weakly Pareto-efficient designs, and positive weights yield Pareto-efficient designs.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_\varepsilon\ne\varnothing\) and the minimum is attained.
All resource coordinates are minimized and consistently accounted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^\star\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal F_\varepsilon}\lambda^{\mathsf T}r(d)\Rightarrow d^\star\text{ is weakly Pareto efficient; if }\lambda>0\text{, it is Pareto efficient}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R\in\mathbb N\) local steps, communication interval \(H\in\mathbb N\), and precision \(b\in\mathbb N\), represent predicted runtime and error by \[T(R,H,b)=R t_{\mathrm c}+\left\lceil\frac{R}{H}\right\rceil t_{\mathrm m}(b),\qquad E(R,H,b)=\frac{A}{R}+BH^2+C2^{-2b}.\] Given tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the co-design is \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{R,H,b}T(R,H,b)\quad\text{subject to}\quad E(R,H,b)\leq\varepsilon.\] Here the three error terms model finite computation, local-drift accumulation, and quantization, respectively; only triples satisfying the model's domain constraints are admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose total local work, communication interval, and bit precision to minimize predicted runtime while a computation-drift-quantization error model meets the target tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Network Disconnection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-component quadratic instance showing failure of global information propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\) be even and partition the agents into two noncommunicating sets \(V_+\) and \(V_-\), each of size \(n/2\). Assign \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2\) on \(V_+\) and \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12(x+1)^2\) on \(V_-\). The global uniform objective has unique minimizer \(x^\star=0\). Any protocol whose messages and states remain confined to the two components cannot make observations in one component depend on data from the other; componentwise optimization instead yields \(1\) and \(-1\). Thus persistent disconnection prevents guaranteed recovery of the global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two permanently disconnected equal-size groups optimize quadratics centered at opposite points; each reaches its local center although the global minimizer is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(n\) is even.
No communication path ever joins \(V_+\) and \(V_-\).
Each agent accesses only local data and received messages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star=0\), but the disconnected component minimizers are \(x_+^\star=1\) and \(x_-^\star=-1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and doubly stochastic, let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/n\), and define \(\rho=\lVert W-J\rVert_2\in(0,1)\). For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and every integer \(k\geq0\), pure mixing satisfies \[\lVert W^k x-Jx\rVert_2\leq \rho^k\lVert x-Jx\rVert_2.\] Because a disagreement eigenvector attains the factor \(\rho\), the worst-case number of rounds required to reduce disagreement by a factor \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) is \[k_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil.\] Thus the worst-case mixing time diverges as \(\rho\uparrow1\), allowing network propagation to dominate optimization progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For symmetric doubly stochastic mixing, the worst disagreement mode contracts by the nonconsensus spectral factor. As that factor approaches one, the communication rounds needed for a fixed reduction diverge at inverse-spectral-gap scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Poor Network Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^{+}=Wx\), where \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/n\). Consensus states are preserved for every consensus input exactly when \(W\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\), and the arithmetic average is preserved for every input exactly when \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\). If either identity fails, an input exists for which the corresponding invariant is lost in one step. When both identities hold, asymptotic contraction of every disagreement requires \(\rho(W-J)<1\); if \(\rho(W-J)\geq1\), the powers of the disagreement operator do not converge to zero. Thus weights violating any of these requirements invalidate the corresponding standard consensus argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing weights must preserve consensus, preserve the intended arithmetic average, and asymptotically contract disagreement. Failure of any requirement destroys the corresponding invariant or convergence mechanism.

abla f_1(x_1),\ldots,

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Primal-Dual Network Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Modal instability of simultaneous primal-dual mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x^{k+1}=Wx^k-\alpha Ay^k\) and \(y^{k+1}=Wy^k+\beta A^{\mathsf T}x^k\), with \(\alpha,\beta>0\). On a common mode having mixing eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and coupling singular value \(\sigma>0\), the iteration matrix is \[M_{\lambda,\sigma}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&-\alpha\sigma\\ \beta\sigma&\lambda\end{pmatrix}.\] Its eigenvalues have modulus \(\sqrt{\lambda^2+\alpha\beta\sigma^2}\). Therefore this mode is unstable whenever \(\lambda^2+\alpha\beta\sigma^2>1\), demonstrating that individually plausible mixing and primal-dual gains can become unstable when coupled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual network mode diverges when the combined mixing and coupling gain places its eigenvalues outside the unit disk.
assumptions_latex: The mixing and coupling operators admit the stated common modal decomposition.
\(\alpha>0\), \(\beta>0\), and \(\sigma>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/n\), and define the disagreement \(d^k=(I-J)x^k\). Suppose a homogeneous network mode satisfies \(\lVert d^k\rVert_2=\rho^k\lVert d^0\rVert_2\) for every integer \(k\geq0\), where \(0<\rho<1\). For a threshold \(\delta\) satisfying \(0<\delta<\lVert d^0\rVert_2\), define \[N_\delta=\min\{k\in\mathbb{N}_0:\lVert d^k\rVert_2\leq\delta\}.\] Then \[N_\delta=\left\lceil\frac{\log(\lVert d^0\rVert_2/\delta)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil.\] Hence \(N_\delta\) grows on the order of \((1-\rho)^{-1}\log(\lVert d^0\rVert_2/\delta)\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\), producing a long pre-asymptotic phase above the prescribed network-error threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a disagreement mode contracting by a factor rho per iteration, the time to cross a fixed error threshold grows at inverse-spectral-gap scale as rho approaches one.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Acceleration Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Momentum amplification of a network disagreement mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the accelerated mixing recurrence \(d^{k+1}=(1+\beta)Wd^k-\beta Wd^{k-1}\), let \(v\) be a disagreement eigenvector with \(Wv=\lambda v\). Its scalar amplitude obeys \(a_{k+1}=(1+\beta)\lambda a_k-\beta\lambda a_{k-1}\), with characteristic polynomial \[p(r)=r^2-(1+\beta)\lambda r+\beta\lambda.\] The mode is stable only if both roots lie strictly inside the unit disk. If \(\max\{|r|:p(r)=0\}>1\), disagreement grows geometrically, so acceleration parameters acceptable for optimization dynamics may destabilize network dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Momentum is unstable whenever its characteristic roots for a disagreement eigenmode leave the unit disk, causing geometric amplification of disagreement.
assumptions_latex: \(Wv=\lambda v\) for a nonconsensus eigenvector \(v\).
The momentum parameter is \(\beta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{|r|:p(r)=0\}>1\) implies geometric divergence of the selected disagreement mode.

children.title: Execution-Fault Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by delay, congestion, dropout, or unreliable participants.

children.title: Uncontrolled Staleness
children.top_down_role: Information age outside the stability regime of a method.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Staleness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded-delay failure of delayed gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2/2\) and apply delayed gradient descent \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_{k-\tau_k})\) with \(\alpha>0\). Choose the admissible ages \(\tau_k=k\), so every update uses the initial point. Then \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha x_0,\qquad x_k=(1-k\alpha)x_0.\] For every \(x_0\neq0\), the iterates diverge in magnitude although \(f\) is smooth and strongly convex. Thus convergence guarantees requiring uniformly bounded delay or an age-dependent stepsize do not extend to uncontrolled staleness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on a scalar strongly convex quadratic, always reusing the initial gradient makes delayed gradient descent diverge linearly.
assumptions_latex: The delay sequence is \(\tau_k=k\).

notation.meaning: Age of the gradient used at iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is algebraically consistent and counterexample is the correct content kind, but no source is supplied. Because the record uses the example to delimit assumptions in delayed-gradient convergence theory, an inspectable delayed-optimization source must support the delay convention and the claimed failure boundary.

children.title: Straggler Tail-Latency Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Slow participants limiting synchronized progress.

children.title: Persistent Stragglers
children.top_down_role: Participants that repeatedly complete required work substantially later than peers.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Stragglers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated violation of a finite round-time threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_{i,k}\in[0,\infty]\) be participant \(i\)'s completion time in round \(k\). Participant \(i\) is a persistent straggler at threshold \(b<\infty\) when \[\limsup_{K\to\infty}\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbf{1}\{T_{i,k}>b\}>0.\] Thus excessive latency occurs with nonvanishing asymptotic frequency, rather than in finitely many exceptional rounds. In a barrier-synchronous method requiring every participant, each such occurrence makes the corresponding round exceed \(b\), preventing any uniform round-time bound below that threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent straggler exceeds a fixed latency threshold in a nonvanishing fraction of rounds, repeatedly delaying any all-participant barrier.
assumptions_latex: Completion times \(T_{i,k}\) are defined for every participant and round.
The protocol waits for every participant at each barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistence implies a nonvanishing frequency of synchronous rounds whose duration exceeds \(b\).

notation.meaning: Completion time of participant i in round k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a terminal notion of persistent straggling, but the proposed definition is unsourced. In addition, a positive limsup gives positive upper asymptotic frequency along a subsequence of horizons; it does not by itself establish a positive limiting frequency or positive lower frequency. A source is needed to choose and state the intended persistence notion.

children.title: Tail-Latency Regimes
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes dominated by extreme completion-time observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Latency Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularly varying model for severe completion-time tails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonnegative completion time \(T\) is in a regularly varying tail-latency regime with index \(a>0\) when \[\mathbb{P}(T>t)=t^{-a}L(t)\] for all sufficiently large \(t\), where \(L(ct)/L(t)\to1\) for every \(c>0\). The regime has no finite first moment when \(a\leq1\). For \(n\) independent workers with this latency law, the synchronous round time \(M_n=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}T_i\) satisfies \(\mathbb{P}(M_n\leq t)=(1-\mathbb{P}(T>t))^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heavy tail with regular-variation index at most one has infinite mean, while synchronous rounds inherit the maximum of all worker latencies.
assumptions_latex: \(T\geq0\) and its survival function is regularly varying.
Worker latencies are independent and identically distributed for the maximum formula.

notation.meaning: Barrier completion time for n workers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is suitable for the tail-regime leaf, but the first-moment claim is false at tail index one without an additional condition on the slowly varying factor. For example, an index-one survival tail with a sufficiently decaying slowly varying factor can be integrable. An authoritative regular-variation source is required before correcting the exact boundary statement.

children.title: Barrier Amplification
children.top_down_role: Magnification of participant delays by synchronization barriers.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-statistic amplification at a synchronous barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_1,\ldots,T_n\) be independent nonnegative worker completion times with common distribution function \(F\), and let the barrier time be \(M_n=\max_iT_i\). Then \[\mathbb{P}(M_n\leq t)=F(t)^n,\qquad \mathbb{E}[M_n]=\int_0^\infty\bigl(1-F(t)^n\bigr)\,dt.\] Consequently, the \(q\)-quantile of the barrier time is \(F^{-1}(q^{1/n})\). Increasing the number of required workers pushes the barrier toward progressively higher latency quantiles, amplifying even infrequent tail delays.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An all-worker barrier takes the maximum latency, so adding workers moves round completion toward increasingly extreme latency quantiles.
assumptions_latex: Worker completion times are independent and identically distributed.
The displayed expectation is interpreted in \([0,\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barrier distribution is \(F^n\), and its \(q\)-quantile equals \(F^{-1}(q^{1/n})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits and the maximum-distribution and tail-integral formulas are standard under the stated independence assumptions. However, no source is supplied, and the quantile identity requires an explicit generalized-inverse convention when F has atoms or flat portions. A specific order-statistics or distributed-systems locator is required.

children.title: Slow-Participant Dominance
children.top_down_role: Regimes where overall progress is governed by the slowest participants.

knowledge_statements.title: Slow-Participant Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round time controlled by the slowest required participant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a synchronous method requiring every participant, let \(T_{i,k}\geq0\) be participant \(i\)'s time in round \(k\), and let \(R_k=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}T_{i,k}\). Then \(R_k\geq T_{j,k}\) for every participant \(j\), and therefore \(\mathbb{E}[R_k]\geq\max_j\mathbb{E}[T_{j,k}]\) whenever the expectations exist. If one participant's mean latency tends to infinity along a system family, the expected synchronous round time also tends to infinity, regardless of improvements to the other participants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because synchronous round time is a maximum, one increasingly slow required participant can dominate total throughput despite all other improvements.
assumptions_latex: Every round waits for all \(n\) participants.
The relevant completion-time expectations exist, possibly as extended values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[R_k]\geq\max_j\mathbb{E}[T_{j,k}]\); divergence of one required participant's mean forces divergence of the round mean.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind matches the leaf and the maximum-based inequality is mathematically standard, including with extended expectations. Nevertheless, the record has no inspectable source for either the synchronous execution model or its straggler interpretation, so it remains source-dependent candidate material.

children.title: Communication Congestion-Contention Boundary
children.top_down_role: Bandwidth sharing and hotspots distorting algorithmic cost.

children.title: Network Congestion
children.top_down_role: Performance degradation caused by excessive traffic relative to network capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Congestion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue-instability boundary on an overloaded communication link.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a communication link \(e\), let cumulative arrivals and service satisfy \(A_e(t)/t\to\lambda_e\) and \(S_e(t)/t\to\mu_e\), and let backlog obey \(Q_e(t)\geq Q_e(0)+A_e(t)-S_e(t)\). If \(\lambda_e>\mu_e\), then \[\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{Q_e(t)}{t}\geq\lambda_e-\mu_e>0.\] Hence backlog and communication delay cannot remain bounded. Any distributed optimization method whose required messages traverse this persistently overloaded link lacks a finite steady communication-time guarantee unless traffic is reduced, rerouted, or service capacity is increased.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If required message traffic exceeds a link's service capacity, its queue grows at least linearly and bounded communication delay is impossible.
assumptions_latex: Long-run arrival and service rates exist.
The link backlog satisfies cumulative flow conservation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_e>\mu_e\) implies asymptotically linear backlog growth and excludes bounded steady delay.

notation.meaning: Cumulative traffic arriving at link e.
Cumulative service available at link e.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overload calculation supports linear backlog growth and failure_boundary is the correct kind. The further conclusion about communication delay requires a specified queueing discipline and a relation between backlog and message delay; it does not follow from the displayed cumulative inequality alone. A queueing or network-calculus source with an exact locator is required.

children.title: Communication Contention
children.top_down_role: Competition among simultaneous exchanges for shared communication resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Contention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-resource contention in one iteration of a distributed optimization algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be the set of shared communication resources. During iteration \(k\), let \(d_{ir}^k\ge 0\) be worker \(i\)'s service demand on resource \(r\), and let \(c_r^k>0\) be its available service capacity. The iteration crosses the communication-contention boundary when
\[\exists r\in R:\quad \sum_{i=1}^n d_{ir}^k>c_r^k.\]
Requests must then queue, serialize, or be dropped; hence the communication completion time exceeds the no-contention time even when every physical link remains operational.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contention occurs when simultaneous worker demand exceeds a shared communication resource's capacity, forcing queuing, serialization, or dropped requests.
assumptions_latex: \(n<\infty\) and \(R\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r\in R:\sum_i d_{ir}^k>c_r^k\) is the contention boundary.

notation.meaning: Service demand of worker i on resource r during iteration k.
Available capacity of resource r during iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The locator is specific, but a general communication-aspects section does not establish this bespoke capacity predicate. Exceeded demand does not necessarily imply that requests are dropped, nor that completion time increases when excess work is dropped. The demand and capacity measurement interval also requires definition.

children.title: Communication Hotspots
children.top_down_role: Localized traffic concentration at particular links, agents, or servers.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Hotspots
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Load-concentration condition for distributed communication resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iteration \(k\), let \(L_r^k=\sum_{i=1}^n d_{ir}^k\) be the load assigned to communication resource \(r\in R\), and let \(C^k=\sum_{r\in R}c_r^k\). For a prescribed factor \(\gamma>1\), resource \(r\) is a communication hotspot when
\[\frac{L_r^k}{c_r^k}\ge \gamma\frac{\sum_{s\in R}L_s^k}{C^k}.\]
Thus its capacity-normalized load is at least \(\gamma\) times the system-wide normalized load; overload is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hotspot is a resource whose capacity-normalized communication load substantially exceeds the system-wide normalized load.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite and nonempty.
\(c_r^k>0\) for every \(r\in R\).

notation.meaning: Communication load assigned to resource r at iteration k.
Capacity of resource r at iteration k.

children.title: Communication-Cost Distortion
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between idealized communication costs and congested execution costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Cost Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch between modeled and realized communication cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat C_k>0\) be the communication cost predicted for iteration \(k\) by an algorithmic cost model, and let \(C_k\ge0\) be the realized cost measured in the same units. For tolerance \(\varepsilon_C\ge0\), communication-cost distortion occurs when
\[|C_k-\widehat C_k|>\varepsilon_C\widehat C_k.\]
For cumulative evaluation through iteration \(K\), replace the two costs by \(\sum_{k=0}^{K}C_k\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^{K}\widehat C_k\). The predicate is meaningful only when modeled and realized costs use identical accounting boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-cost distortion occurs when measured cost differs from modeled cost by more than a specified relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat C_k>0\) and \(C_k\ge0\).
\(C_k\) and \(\widehat C_k\) use the same cost units and accounting boundary.
\(\varepsilon_C\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Realized communication cost at iteration k.
Modeled communication cost at iteration k.

children.title: Distributed Fault Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Missing updates caused by node or communication failure.

children.title: Node Crash Faults
children.top_down_role: Loss of participant availability caused by node termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Crash Faults
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crash-stop faults in an iterative distributed optimization execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be the worker set and let \(a_i^k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether worker \(i\) executes and communicates at iteration \(k\). Worker \(i\) has a crash-stop fault at time \(\tau_i\) when
\[a_i^k=1\quad(k<\tau_i),\qquad a_i^k=0\quad(k\ge\tau_i).\]
After \(\tau_i\), the worker produces no updates or messages unless an external recovery mechanism creates a new active process. This definition excludes transient omissions followed by spontaneous resumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node crash-stop fault permanently removes a previously active worker from computation and communication from some iteration onward.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite worker set.

notation.meaning: Activity indicator for worker i at iteration k.

children.title: Update Omission Faults
children.top_down_role: Missing transmitted or applied updates despite continuing execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Update Omission Faults
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transient loss of an otherwise defined worker update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose worker \(i\) computes a prescribed candidate update \(u_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) at iteration \(k\). Let \(m_i^k\in\{0,1\}\) be its delivery-and-application indicator. An update omission fault occurs when \(u_i^k\) is defined but \(m_i^k=0\), so the server or neighboring workers apply
\[\widetilde u_i^k=m_i^k u_i^k=0\]
in place of that update. Unlike a crash-stop fault, omission at iteration \(k\) imposes no restriction on \(m_i^\ell\) for \(\ell>k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An update omission occurs when a computed worker update is not delivered or applied, without requiring permanent worker failure.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) is defined.

notation.meaning: Candidate update computed by worker i.

children.title: Link Failure Faults
children.top_down_role: Message loss or isolation caused by communication-link failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Link Failure Faults
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-varying loss of a communication edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the nominal communication graph and let \(b_{ij}^k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether the directed link \((i,j)\in E\) successfully transmits during iteration \(k\). A link failure fault on \((i,j)\) occurs when \(b_{ij}^k=0\); the effective graph is
\[G_k=(V,E_k),\qquad E_k=\{(i,j)\in E:b_{ij}^k=1\}.\]
The fault disconnects the entire execution at iteration \(k\) precisely when the connectivity property required by the algorithm fails for \(G_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A link failure removes a nominal communication edge from the effective graph; it is execution-critical when required connectivity is lost.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the nominal graph.

notation.meaning: Effective communication graph at iteration k.
